data.title: Heavy chatbot usage is correlated with loneliness and reduced socialization
data.author: suvan
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了人工智能聊天机器人（如ChatGPT）对用户心理健康和社交互动的潜在影响。文章提到了两项新研究，由MIT媒体实验室和OpenAI的研究人员发布。这些研究发现，大多数用户将ChatGPT视为一种中立的软件工具，但有一部分重度用户表现出更高的孤独感、情感依赖和社交减少。研究强调，虽然聊天机器人可以提供情感支持，但过度使用可能加剧孤独感，尤其是那些寻求情感连接的用户。文章还指出，虽然这些发现需要更多研究来验证，但开发者应注意减轻潜在风险。同时，一些公司正积极吸引寻求情感关系的用户，提供更具沉浸式的体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：ChatGPT及聊天机器人对心理健康的影响

不同观点：
• 支持正面影响：
   - [drooby] 认为ChatGPT作为一种情感支持工具，能够帮助他处理情感和思想，减轻压力。
   - [labrador] 分享了使用ChatGPT了解自己过度沉思的问题，并从中得到了有益的建议，有助于心理健康。
   - [rqtwteye] 提到如果患有痴呆症的家庭成员能与聊天机器人对话，可以减轻家属的负担。

• 质疑与中立观点：
   - [brookst] 表示聊天机器人的影响不确定，可能对某些人有益，对其他人则未必，且难以与其他变量区分。
   - [gandalfgeek] 用讽刺的方式指出相关性不代表因果关系，暗示文章可能存在逻辑问题。

• 负面影响与伦理担忧：
   - [kmnc] 担心聊天机器人的新颖性效应会很快消失，并且这些机器人通过游戏化设计利用用户的孤独感，可能变得具有成瘾性。
   - [mmsc] 担心对于精神障碍患者，聊天机器人可能会强化他们的错误认知，如被监听的感觉。
   - [m3kw9] 认为依赖聊天机器人可能会影响人与人之间的互动，因为机器人总能说出更合适的话。

补充讨论：
• 因果关系的争议：
   - [kianN], [superb-owl], [ameixaseca], [blahburn], [aussieguy1234] 均提到文章在相关性和因果关系上存在问题，指出孤独的人可能更倾向于使用聊天机器人，而不是使用聊天机器人导致了孤独。

• 政策与控制的讨论：
   - [keepamovin] 以讽刺的方式提到对聊天机器人的监管问题，认为政府害怕个人通过技术获得更多权力和控制。

整体来看，评论中的争议主要集中在聊天机器人对心理健康的影响是正面还是负面，特别是其成瘾性和对精神障碍患者的潜在影响，以及因果关系的辨析。

43467681.article_content:
This is a column about AI. My boyfriend works at Anthropic, and I also co-host a podcast at the New York Times, which is suing OpenAI and Microsoft over allegations of copyright infringement. See
my full ethics disclosure here
.
I.
Few questions have generated as much discussion, and as few generally accepted conclusions, as how social networks like Instagram and TikTok affect our collective well-being. In 2023, the US Surgeon General
issued an advisory which found that social networks can negatively affect the mental health of young people
. Other studies have found that the introduction of social networks
does not have any measurable effect on the population’s well-being
.
As that debate continues,
lawmakers in dozens of states have passed laws
that seek to restrict social media usage in the belief that it does pose serious risks. But the implementation of those laws has largely been stopped by the courts, which have
blocked them
on First Amendment grounds.
While we await some sort of resolution, the next frontier of this debate is coming rapidly into view. Last year, the mother of a 14-year-old Florida boy
sued chatbot maker Character.ai
alleging that it was to blame for his suicide. (We spoke with her on this episode of
Hard Fork
.) And millions of Americans — both young people and adults — are
entering into emotional and sexual relationships with chatbots
.
Over time, we should expect chatbots to become even more engaging than today’s social media feeds. They are personalized to their users; they have realistic human voices; and they are programmed to affirm and support their users in almost every case.
So how will extended use of these bots affect their human users? And what should platforms do to mitigate the risks?
II.
These questions are at the center of two new studies
published on Friday by researchers from the MIT Media Lab and OpenAI
. And while further research is needed to support their conclusions, their findings are both consistent with earlier research about social media and a warning to platforms that are building chatbots optimized for engagement.
In the first study, researchers collected and analyzed more than 4 million ChatGPT conversations from 4,076 people who had agreed to participate. They then surveyed participants about how those interactions had made them feel.
In the second study, researchers recruited 981 people to participate in a four-week trial. Each person was asked to use ChatGPT for at least five minutes a day. At the end of the trial, participants filled out a survey about how they perceived ChatGPT, whether they felt lonely, whether they were socializing with people in the real world, and whether they perceived their use of the chatbot as problematic.
The studies found that most users have a neutral relationship with ChatGPT, using it as a software tool like any other. But both studies also found a group of power users — those in the top 10 percent of time spent with ChatGPT — whose usage suggested more reason for concern.
Heavy use of ChatGPT was correlated with increased loneliness, emotional dependence, and reduced social interaction, the studies found.
“Generally, users who engage in personal conversations with chatbots tend to experience higher loneliness,” the researchers wrote. “Those who spend more time with chatbots tend to be even lonelier.”
(Quick editorial aside: OpenAI deserves real credit for investing in this research and publishing it openly. This kind of self-skeptical investigation is exactly the sort of thing I have long advocated for companies like Meta to do more of; instead,
in the wake of the Frances Haugen revelations
, it has done far less of it.)
Jason Phang, a researcher at OpenAI who worked on the studies, warned me that the findings would need to be replicated by other studies before they could be considered definitive. “These are correlations from a preliminary study, so we don't want to draw too strong conclusions here,” he said in an interview.
Still, there is plenty in here that is worth discussing.
Note that these studies aren’t suggesting that heavy ChatGPT usage directly
causes
loneliness. Rather, it suggests that lonely people are more likely to seek emotional bonds with bots — just as an earlier generation of research suggested that lonelier people spend more time on social media.
That matters less for OpenAI, which has designed ChatGPT to present itself as more of a productivity tool than a boon companion. (Though that hasn’t stopped some people from
falling in love with it
, too.) But other developers — Character.ai, Replika, Nomi — are all intentionally courting users that seek more emotional connections. “Develop a passionate relationship,” read
the copy on Nomi’s website
. “Join the millions who already have met their AI soulmates,” touts Replika.
Each of these apps offers paid monthly subscriptions; among the benefits offered are longer “memories” for chatbots to enable more realistic roleplay.

and
Replika
sell additiona

data.title: Fuckarounditis (2011)
data.author: fzliu
data.article_summary: "Fuckarounditis"是作者Martin Berkhan提出的概念，指一种行为障碍，表现为尽管在健身房花费大量时间，但体型平庸且毫无进展。其特征包括过度关注卷腹、弯举、平衡板等无效训练，害怕深蹲和硬拉，以及体能消耗不当。该问题源于误导信息和不良训练建议，尤其是在健身杂志和网络上。环境和社交网络是主要传播途径，90-100%的商业健身房顾客受影响。预防措施包括识别症状、避免复杂化的信息迷宫，以及专注于有效的强度训练。作者强调，信息的过载和复杂性错觉是问题的核心，需谨慎选择信息来源以做出明智决策。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：健身方法和理念的差异

不同观点：
• [justonceokay] 认为健身的效果应该以具体的重量指标（如卧推190磅）来衡量，任何低于这个标准的都是浪费时间。他认为姿势练习和物理治疗是弱者的选择，并强调健身应该以肌肉增长和力量提升为核心，而不是为了感觉良好或社交。

• [fxtentacle] 支持一种“原始”或“古健身”的理念，认为健身应该避免无效的、杂乱的锻炼方式（fuckarounditis），并暗示一些人不正确的锻炼方式让他们变得虚弱。他批评了某位私人教练对客户的描述方式。

• [florbnit] 反对那种只重视肌肉体积的观念，指出很多人去健身房并不是为了追求这种“进步”，他们可能更关注功能性运动如攀岩或超马跑步。他批评那些称这些运动员为“弱者”的健美人士，认为他们缺乏对其他运动形式的理解。

• [twalla] 强调健身成功的关键在于长期的一致性，而不是短期的强度。他认为每次锻炼70%的努力但保持100%的时间出勤率，比短期内投入110%然后受伤或倦怠要好。

• [richard___] 反驳那些认为深蹲和硬拉能塑造好身材的观点，坚持认为卧推是唯一能提供良好上身美学的复合动作。

• [F0UKYOU-HN] 将这种健身的误解归因于互联网上的错误信息和误导性建议，并将其与其它社会误解（如反疫苗、选举舞弊等）相提并论。他认为这是教育体系失败的结果。

• [krn1p4n1c] 指出很多健美驱动的信息与实际运动员的体能训练（S&C）相悖，暗示健美式的训练方法并不适合所有类型的运动员。

• [joemazerino] 回顾了Leangains在2010年代推广间歇性断食的历史，认为虽然现在看来有些过时，但在当时是独一无二的。

• [davidee] 以简短幽默的方式指出某人只是“举重”。

• [immibis] 认为这种关于健美的讨论也适用于软件开发，尤其是网页开发，强调太多时间浪费在框架上，而没有实际编写HTML代码。

• [lolc] 批评文章作者没有明确表达去健身房的目的，认为文章内容冗长且态度令人疲惫，因此没有读完。

• [sfn42] 支持[twalla]的观点，并以个人经验证明这种简单高效的锻炼方法（如5个基本动作，定期记录进展）可以带来显著效果。他强调这种方法的低时间投入和高收益，但也指出每个人健身的目标不同，去健身房社交或放松也是完全可以接受的。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于健身的目标和方法，一些人强调力量和肌肉体积，另一些人则重视功能性运动和长期一致性。
• 对互联网信息的可靠性和误导性也有讨论，将健身误解与社会上的其它误解相提并论。
• 不同人对健身的态度和期望不同，有些人追求具体的身体成果，有些人则更重视社交和心理效益。

43466252.article_content:
Fuckarounditis
September 27, 2011
— Posted in
Training
Goal Setting
Reverse Pyramid Training
Weight Training
Dear readers, it is with troublesome news I break my three months of silence.
The statistics all point towards the same conclusion: we have a global outbreak of fuckarounditis.
Fuckarounditis is a behavioral disorder characterized by a mediocre physique and complete lack of progress, despite significant amounts of time spent in the gym.
Fuckarounditis most commonly manifests itself as an intense preoccupation with crunches, curls, cable movements, belts, gloves, balance boards, Swiss Balls and Tyler Durden. Fear of squats and deadlifts is another distinguishing trait. Physical exertion is either completely lacking or misapplied (towards questionable or unproductive training practices).
Despite an alarming increase of fuckarounditis in recent years, prevalance may vary greatly depending on location. However, in most commercial gyms, it has been estimated that 90-100% of individuals are afflicted to varying degrees.
Environment and social networks are crucial factors for triggering the disease. It has been proposed that the roots of the disease stems from misinformation and counterproductive training advice found in popular media (“fitness magazines”) and information hubs on the Internet.
Human nature and the so-called “laziness”, “magic bullet” and “complacency” genes plays a permissive role for allowing the disease to take hold.
The disease spreads rapidly, as carriers of the disease communicate with other individuals in locker rooms, Internet discussion forums and other arenas of interaction and information exchange in real life or otherwise.
The onset of symptoms typically occurs in young adulthood and may go undiagnosed for a lifetime. Diagnosis is set by a professional and based on observed behaviors and physique progress.
Symptoms, preventative measures and intervention strategies are reviewed and discussed.
Berkhan, M. (2011)
“Targeting The Fuckarounditis Epidemic: Preventative Measures and Intervention Strategies.”
Fuckarounditis: A Serious Threat
I have been trying to cure people of fuckarounditis since the late 90’s, starting from the day I was first cleansed from it myself. Ever since I recognized the disease, I have acknowledged it as a serious threat to physique development and mental well-being. It is therefore with shock and horror I have watched an increasing number of people fall victim to the disease and the dubious training practices it inspires.
In educating myself of good strength training practices, I was very lucky. Yes, I wasted some time with the usual bench’n’curl/bodybuilding magazine-inspired crapola all my friends were doing, spending my time in the gym joking around more than doing any actual training. I was 16 or so when I first set my foot at the gym. (See
“My Transformation”
for pictures from this time period.)
However, I did not spend more than a few months fooling around with my friends. I found that I enjoyed strength training, so I started to take an increasing interest in the topic. I started to explore and I eventually came across an excellent resource that set the tone for my entire approach and attitude. The resource was the book
Beyond Brawn
by Stuart McRobert, and it taught me the value of working hard at the right things.
However, I may have never been lucky enough to find this tome of wisdom if I had first lost myself in the malicious maze that resides behind…
the illusion of complexity.
The Illusion of Complexity
The Internet provides a rich soil for fuckarounditis to grow and take hold of the unsuspecting observer. Too much information, shit, clutter, woo-woo, noise, bullshit, loony toon theories, too many quacks, morons and people with good intentions giving you bad advice and uninformed answers. Ah yes, the information age.
Some of it is bullshit wrapped up in a fancy paper with scientific terms, elaborate detail, promising cutting edge strategies based on the latest research. This makes it easier to swallow for intellectuals and those seeking a quick fix; two different groups, both equally susceptible to bullshittery and easy prey for scam artists.
Yes, if anything has surprised me so far in my work, it’s the complete disassociation between IQ and “exercise intelligence” (essentially common sense and knowledge in regards to training fundamentals). I have many clients from academic circles, many clients that are very successful financially and in their each respective field, but some were complete idiots with regards to their training before they came to me.
The problem at the core of the fuckarounditis epidemic is the overabundance of information we have available to us. If there are so many theories, articles and opinions on a topic, we perceive it as something complex, something hard to understand. An illusion of complexity is created.

data.title: Status as a Service (2019)
data.author: simonebrunozzi
data.article_summary: 这篇文章是作者长时间未更新博客后的长篇汇总，包含多个编辑注释。作者解释因长时间未更新，本文汇集了多篇短文，并建议读者根据兴趣选择阅读。作者还提到因健康问题和设备限制导致写作中断，并为长时间停更致歉。文章核心内容探讨社交网络与ICO的相似性，提出“追求地位的猴子”这一概念，认为人们在社交网络上寻求最大化社会资本的效率路径。尽管缺乏精确测量社会资本的方法，但社交网络生成的大量社会资本常常预示着未来的经济收益。作者将社交网络视为“地位即服务”（StaaS）的业务，深入分析其运作模式和动态，并指出这种分析有助于解释许多在线行为。文章最后表示，由于缺乏某些数据，观点尚不 definitive，期待读者反馈。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对一篇长文章的评论，涉及社交状态、社交媒体的效用和状态追求等主题。

不同观点：
• [lordfrito] 期望文章介绍一种通过付费服务提升社交地位的方式，类似于购买社交象征（如Sneeches中的星星），绕过实际努力。
• [sujumayas] 提到Google Reader的例子，认为它是一个高度依赖实际努力的服务，但最终被关闭，表达了对此的遗憾。
• [DrNosferatu] 对“社交状态作为服务”的概念表示疑惑或质疑。
• [nathan_compton] 分享个人经历，表示婚后因为忙碌，追求社交地位的行为基本消失。
• [vivzkestrel] 关心如何便捷地找到网站上所有博客文章的列表，而不是通过大量滚动。
• [trash_cat] 对文章进行总结，认为文章从效用和社交资本来解释社交媒体，并提出个人见解，认为不应将自己的快乐与别人的评分体系挂钩。
• [grvdrm] 高度评价文章，认为文章提出的“网络扩展需要一定的基础工作”的观点重新定义了他对网络扩展的理解。
• [thomasfl] 认为社交网络与加密货币有很多共同点，尤其是早期采用者在两者中都能获得优势。
• [jiri] 认为文章长但精彩，引用“猴子即使离开追求地位的游戏，但追求地位的本能不会消失”的观点。
• [yuzhun] 表示文章非常有趣，阅读它是一种享受。
• [damnitbuilds] 表示不喜欢阅读大量关于社交想法的文章，尤其是那些基于个人轶事和现实联系不紧密的内容，更喜欢技术性强的文章。

补充讨论：
• 文章的长度和深度引发了两种不同的反应：一些人认为文章精彩且有深度（如[EA0707], [grvdrm], [jiri], [yuzhun]），而另一些人则认为文章过长且内容空泛（如[damnitbuilds]）。
• 对“社交状态作为服务”的概念存在不同理解和争议，部分人表示疑惑（如[DrNosferatu]），而[trash_cat]则尝试解释并提出个人见解。

争议焦点：
• 对“社交状态作为服务”概念的理解和实际应用存在争议。

43468666.article_content:
Editor's Note 1
: I have no editor.
Editor’s Note 2
: I would like to assure new subscribers to this blog that most my posts are not as long as this one. Or as long as
my previous one
. My long break from posting here means that this piece is a collection of what would’ve normally been a series of shorter posts. I put section titles below, so skip any that don’t interest you. My short takes are on
Twitter
. All that said, I apologize for nothing.
Editor's Note 3
: I lied, I apologize for one thing, and that is my long writing hiatus. Without a work computer, I had to resort to using my 7 year old 13" Macbook Pro as my main computer, and sometime last year my carpal tunnel syndrome returned with a vengeance and left my wrists debilitated with pain. I believe all of you who say your main computer is a laptop or, shudder, an iPad, but goodness gracious I cannot type on a compact keyboard for long periods of time without having my hands turn into useless stumps. It was only the return to typing almost exclusively on my old friend the
Kinesis Advantage 2 ergo keyboard
that put me back in the game.
Editor’s Note 4
:
I was recently on Patrick O'Shaughnessy's podcast Invest Like the Best
, and near the end of that discussion, I mentioned a new essay I'd been working on about the similarities between social networks and ICO's. This is that piece.
Status-Seeking Monkeys
"It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a person in possession of little fortune, must be in want of more social capital."
So wrote Jane Austen, or she would have, I think, if she were chronicling our current age (instead we have
Taylor Lorenz
, and thank goodness for that).
Let's begin with two principles:
People are status-seeking monkeys*
People seek out the most efficient path to maximizing social capital
* Status-Seeking Monkeys will also be the name of my indie band, if I ever learn to play the guitar and start a band
I begin with these two observations of human nature because few would dispute them, yet I seldom see social networks, some of the largest and fastest-growing companies in the history of the world, analyzed on the dimension of status or social capital.
It’s in part a measurement issue. Numbers lend an air of legitimacy and credibility. We have longstanding ways to denominate and measure financial capital and its flows. Entire websites, sections of newspapers, and a ton of institutions report with precision on the prices and movements of money.
We have no such methods for measuring the values and movement of social capital, at least not with anywhere near the accuracy or precision. The body of research feels both broad and yet meager. If we had better measures besides user counts, this piece and many others would be full of charts and graphs that added a sense of intellectual heft to the analysis. There would be some annual presentation called the State of Social akin to Meeker's Internet Trends Report, or perhaps it would be a fifty page sub-section of her annual report.
Despite this, most of the social media networks we study generate much more social capital than actual financial capital, especially in their early stages; almost all such companies have internalized one of the popular truisms of Silicon Valley, that in the early days, companies should postpone revenue generation in favor of rapid network scaling. Social capital has much to say about why social networks lose heat, stall out, and sometimes disappear altogether. And, while we may not be able to quantify social capital, as highly attuned social creatures, we can feel it.
Social capital is, in many ways, a leading indicator of financial capital, and so its nature bears greater scrutiny. Not only is it good investment or business practice, but analyzing social capital dynamics can help to explain all sorts of online behavior that would otherwise seem irrational.
In the past few years, much progress has been made analyzing Software as a Service (SaaS) businesses. Not as much has been made on social networks. Analysis of social networks still strikes me as being like
economic growth theory
long before
Paul Romer's paper on endogenous technological change
. However, we can start to demystify social networks if we also think of them as SaaS businesses, but instead of software, they provide status. This post is a deep dive into what I refer to as
Status as a Service (StaaS)
businesses.
Think of this essay as a series of strongly held hypotheses; without access to the types of data which i’m not even sure exists, it’s difficult to be definitive. As ever, my wise readers will add or push back as they always do.
Traditional Network Effects Model of Social Networks
One of the fundamental lessons of successful social networks is that they must first appeal to people when they have few users. Typically this is done through some form of single-user utility.
This is the classic cold start problem of social.  The answer to the traditional chicken-and-egg question is actually ans

data.title: Writing your own C++ standard library from scratch
data.author: JNRowe
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了C++标准库（STL）的优缺点，特别是编译时间长和因严格向后兼容导致的代码可读性和性能问题。作者认为许多对C++的批评实际上源于STL，并提出可以自行构建标准库（命名为pystd），借鉴Python标准库的设计。作者展示了如何从零开始实现一个简单版本的标准库，并通过一个文本处理应用演示其功能。与STL版本相比，pystd的编译时间更短，可执行文件更小，运行速度相近。作者还提出了通过每年更新命名空间来实现ABI稳定性及其灵活性的设计思路。所有代码在Github上开源，并提供了禁用STL和实现基础功能的详细步骤。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：重写C++标准库或类似功能库的合理性和可行性

不同观点：
• bregma：认为重写一个类似于C++标准库的库并不特殊，尤其是在不满足所有标准库需求和实际应用场景的情况下。他还指出，ABI稳定性的声明在现实世界中是不切实际的，因为一个小错误可能会导致严重的法律问题。
• leni536：质疑所谓的“完美的ABI稳定性”，指出如果一个第三方库暴露了使用特定版本的pystd类的头文件，那么该库就与该版本绑定，不能安全地与其他版本链接。
• fefe23：强调作者并不是在重写STL，而是在实现一些功能类似于STL的C++类。
• BonusPlay：提到在编写自定义stdlib时遇到的问题，例如某些语言特性期望stdlib的存在，这使得没有stdlib的情况下这些特性不可用。
• grandempire：主张通过研究像STL设计这样的学术工作来设计可重用的容器和算法，而不是随意拼凑开源项目。

补充讨论：
• unwind：对帖子的语气和内容表示赞赏，但对编译时间差异表示困惑。
• dvh：质疑C++标准库为何没有字符串修剪功能，指出很多人都在自行实现。
• quibono：询问有哪些好的开源库可以阅读以学习干净和现代的C++。
• cozzyd：对“py prefix”的命名表示不解，并提到与不同版本的pystd兼容性的问题。
• germandiago：对C++模块支持表示关注，并认为这是一个好的实验。
• daemin：好奇如果STL只针对单一C++标准编写，代码量和编译速度会如何变化。
• larusso：关心自定义库如何在未来与新编译器兼容。
• usrnm：回顾过去每个C++项目都有自己的基础实现，希望这种现象已经过去。
• SleepyMyroslav：对代码改进效果表示不满，指出多处可优化的地方，并认为命名和命名空间并不能显著改变代码质量。
• atombender：澄清C++标准库和STL的区别，强调C++标准库包含STL但远不止这些。

争议焦点：
• 重写类似标准库的功能是否实际和有用。
• ABI稳定性的现实可行性。
• 自定义库与标准库在实际应用中的兼容性和可维护性。

43468976.article_content:
The C++ standard library (also know as the STL) is, without a doubt, an astounding piece of work. Its scope, performance and incredible backwards compatibility have taken decades of work by many of the world's best programmers. My hat's off to all those people who have contributed to it.
All of that is not to say that it is not without its problems. The biggest one being the absolutely abysmal compile times but unreadability, and certain unoptimalities caused by strict backwards compatibility are also at the top of the list. In fact, it could be argued that most of the things people really dislike about C++ are features of the STL rather than the language itself. Fortunately, using the STL is not mandatory. If you are crazy enough, you can disable it completely and build your own standard library in the best Bender style.
One of the main advantages of being an unemployed-by-choice open source developer is that you can do all of that if you wish. There are no incompetent middle damagers hovering over your shoulder to ensure you are "producing immediate customer value" rather than "wasting time on useless polishing that does not produce immediate customer value".
It's
my
time, and I'll waste it if I want to!
What's in it?
The biggest design questions of a standard library are scope and the "feel" of the API. Rather than spending time on design, we steal it. Thus, when in doubt, read the Python stdlib documentation and replicate it. Thus the name of the library is
pystd
.
The test app
To keep the scope meaningful, we start by writing only enough of stdlib to build an app that reads a text file, validates it as UTF-8, splits the contents into words, counts how many time each word appears in the file and prints all words and how many times it appears sorted by decreasing count.
This requires, at least:
File handling
Strings
UTF8 validation
A hash map
A vector
Sorting
The training wheels come off
The code is available in
this Github repo
for those who want to follow along at home.
Disabling the STL is fairly easy (with Linux+GCC at least) and requires only these two Meson statements:
add_global_arguments('-nostdinc++', language: 'cpp')
add_global_link_arguments('-nostdlib++', '-lsupc++', language: 'cpp')
The
supc++
library is (according to stackoverflow) a support library GCC needs to implement core language features. Now the stdlib is off and it is time to implement everything with sticks, stones and duct tape.
The outcome
Once you have implemented everything discussed above and auxiliary stuff like a hashing framework the main application looks like this.
The end result is both Valgrind and Asan clean. There is one chunk of unreleased memory, but that comes from
supc++
. There is probably UB in the implementation. But it should be the good kind of UB that, if it would actually not work, would break the entire Linux userspace because
everything
depends on it working "as expected".
All of this took fewer than 1000 lines of code in the library itself (including a regex implementation that is not actually used). For comparison merely including
vector
from the STL brings in 27 thousand lines of code.
Comparison to an STL version
Converting this code to use the STL is fairly simple and only requires changing some types and fine tuning the API.  The main difference is that the STL version does not validate that the input is UTF-8 as there is no builtin function for that. Now we can compare the two.
Runtime for both is 0.001 to 0.002 seconds on the small test file I used. Pystd is not noticeably slower than the STL version, which is enough for our purposes. It almost certainly scales worse because there has been zero performance work on it.
Compiling the pystd version with
-O2
takes 0.3 seconds whereas the STL version takes 1.2 seconds. The measurements were done on a Ryzen 7 3700X processor.
The executable's unstripped size is 349k for STL and 309k for pystd. The stripped sizes are 23k and 135k. Approximately 100 k of the pystd executable comes from
supc++
. In the STL version that probably comes dynamically from
libstdc++
(which, on this machine, takes 2.5 MB).
Perfect ABI stability
Designing a standard library is exceedingly difficult because you can't ever really change it. Someone, somewhere, is depending on every misfeature in it so they can never be changed.
Pystd has been designed to both support perfect ABI stability
and
make it possible to change it in arbitrary ways in the future. If you start from scratch this turned out to be fairly simple.
The sample code above used the
pystd
namespace. It does not actually exist. Instead it is defined like this in the cpp file:
#include <pystd2025.hpp>
namespace pystd = pystd2025;
In pystd all code is in a namespace with a year and is stored in a header file with the same year. The idea is, then, that every year you create a new release. This involves copying all stdlib header files to a file with the new year and regexping the namespace declarations to match. The old co

data.title: The Lost Towers of the Guelph-Ghibelline Wars
data.author: wallflower
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了中世纪意大利城市如博洛尼亚和佛罗伦萨曾拥有密集的高塔建筑，这些塔楼由富裕家族建造，作为防御和炫耀财富的象征。由于塔楼引发了火灾和城市安全问题，佛罗伦萨最终立法限制私人建筑高度，迫使许多塔楼被削顶，留下我们现在看到的石质残余。这种现象反映了中世纪意大利城市内部家族间的激烈争斗，特别是圭尔夫和吉伯林战争期间。文章还提到博洛尼亚曾有“百塔之城”之称，而佛罗伦萨尽管塔楼数量较少，也曾拥有数十座。如今，这些塔楼遗迹成为了中世纪家族争斗的历史见证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于意大利博洛尼亚中世纪塔楼的讨论，涉及塔楼的数量、用途、建筑形式以及历史背景。

不同观点：
• toyg指出博洛尼亚不仅有两座著名的塔楼，实际上还有22座塔楼部分保存下来，其中7座保持了原来的高度，并提供了相关博客链接以支持其观点。
• DeathArrow对塔楼的高度和用途提出疑问，认为虽然这些塔楼可能是为了防御而建，但选择高塔形式可能与炫耀财富和地位有关，类似于现代的摩天大楼。

补充讨论：
• libraryofbabel提到博客的作者是历史学家Ada Palmer，并指出她同时也是一位成功的科幻作家，对其在繁忙的教学工作之余还能撰写博客表示惊讶。
• internet_points对博客内容表示兴趣，并指出中世纪社会能够为了共同利益采取协调行动，例如消除某些竞争性建筑。
• YeGoblynQueenne用一种比喻的方式描述视觉效果，提到当眼睛像苍蝇一样嗡嗡作响时，是一种摩尔纹现象，但与主要讨论点关系不大。
• DrSiemer质疑第一张图片中塔楼高度的历史准确性，认为可能包含艺术夸张。
• intrasight表示对博洛尼亚塔楼历史的兴趣，并补充了卢卡的中世纪塔楼也可以攀爬。
• ErigmolCt提到了解到许多意大利街区中的粗糙石块实际上是中世纪塔楼的残余部分。
• trhway将博洛尼亚的塔楼与也门的塔楼房屋和格鲁吉亚的Svan塔楼进行了比较，提供了跨文化的建筑对比。
• lucidguppy思考是否存在类似于博洛尼亚塔楼设定的《龙与地下城》游戏背景。
• gostsamo赞赏图片的alt文本描述得当，注重了无障碍访问的细节。

争议焦点：
• 塔楼的高度和建筑形式是否主要出于防御目的，还是为了炫耀财富和地位。DeathArrow认为塔楼的高度可能与炫耀有关，而toyg则提供了历史数据支持塔楼数量和高度的真实性。

43452588.article_content:
Looks fake, doesn’t it?  This implausible Medieval forest of towers, as dense as Manhattan skyscrapers, is our best reconstruction of the town of Bologna at its height, toward the end of the Medieval Guelph-Ghibelline wars. We don’t see many such towers today… or think we don’t, but actually their remnants are all over Italy.
Often when in Florence one sees buildings like this, where one section is rough stone standing out amid stucco neighbors.
These are actually the bottom nubs of Medieval stone towers. The town of San Gimigniano (below) is famous for having several still intact. Wealthy families built these as mini-fortresses within the city, where they could defend against riots, enemy families (think Montagues and Capulets) and invasion:
Signs of wealth and prestige, these all-stone buildings were also fireproof, leading to a terrible but effective tactic: take your family, treasures & goods up into your tower then set fire to enemies’ homes and let the city burn around you while you sit safe above. This was VERY BAD for cities.
street corner in San Gimigniano
After many disasters, Florence’s solution was to BAN private buildings over a certain height, forcing everyone who had a tower to knock the top off down to regulation height, leaving these recognizable stone nubs all around the city. This round one below is the oldest (now a restaurant).
My favorite tower stub is this one, in Via dei Cerchi. I lived on the top floor for a year as a grad student, up 111 steps! I had calves of steel by spring, but the views from the top looked like someone had put a poster of Florence on the wall except it was a window!
Only city buildings were allowed to exceed the mandated height, which is why Florence’s skyline is now all special buildings: monastery bell towers, the cathedral & baptistery, Orsanmichele the city’s granary (tall to keep grain away from water & mice), the seat of government, and one special guy…
The tower on the right here is part of Bargello, the prison & police fortress, but it didn’t start that way. It was built by a private family, who sold it to the city when the law banning towers was passed, and the city incorporated it into their prison fort.
The city jail had to be a fortress in case someone from a powerful family was arrested and the family sent goons to break them out (those guys who bite their thumbs in the opening scene of Romeo & Juliet would *totally* have stormed the jail to bust Romeo out!).
In this photo you can see how the brick battlements are a later addition, added to the tower as part of its transformation from private fortress to public.
What did Florence look like back when it had all its towers? Its long-time ally across the mountains Bologna is famous for still having two intact towers, but in the Middle Ages Bologna was known as the City of 100 Towers because so many families built them. The reconstructions look absolutely incredible. Florence didn’t have so many but did have dozens, so the richest part of the city center would have looked much like this.  Much to the despair of the city fire brigade!
So, whether in a film or on the street, if you ever see a historic Italian city and walk along a block where for some reason one chunk of wall is stone and all the others smooth, you’re probably looking at a relic of the faction feuds that Guido Ruggiero aptly calls “The Italian 300 Years’ War.”
I talk about this long war in
“Inventing the Renaissance,”
one of many points of continuity which show how the supposed difference between a bad “Dark Ages” and Renaissance “golden age” is 100% propaganda, but fascinating propaganda with a deep history.
And I’ll share more tidbits like over the coming days as we countdown to the book’s release!

data.title: A study reveals that deciduous trees' roots remain active in winter
data.author: bryanrasmussen
data.article_summary: 一项新研究发现，落叶树种如山毛榉和桦树的根系在冬季仍持续生长，挑战了此前根系在冬季休眠的认知。该研究发表于《Nature Ecology & Evolution》期刊，由安特卫普大学牵头，涉及多个温带森林和330株树苗。研究显示，即使在土壤温度低于3°C时，粗根仍在生长，这表明森林土壤的碳汇能力比之前认为的更强，因为树木全年都在固定碳。根系的持续生长为春季树木迅速恢复叶片生长和光合作用提供了储备，有助于树木应对气候变化。该研究强调了地上与地下部分生长周期的差异，根系在冬季生长，而地上部分在春季活跃。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：树木在冬季的根系生长及其生态影响

不同观点：
• volleygman180：对使用草甘膦控制入侵植物（如金银花）的常见做法提出质疑。尽管在树叶掉落的秋季使用草甘膦被认为是最佳实践，但新的研究表明树木在冬季仍可能通过根系吸收物质，暗示草甘膦对生态系统的潜在影响可能被低估。

• hoeoek：作为森林研究者，认为新研究提供了有趣的视角，尤其是在季节性生长模型中。传统模型通常忽略了冬季根系生长的细节，而这可能对树木生长动态有重要影响。

• y-c-o-m-b：认为根系在冬季继续生长应是常识，并以个人观察为例（如红枫在冬季破坏人行道）。

• mapt：部分同意研究结果，特别是关于根系在冬季储存养分的观点。但质疑冬季森林土壤积累碳的能力，因为没有光合作用，树木主要依赖储存的碳进行细胞分裂和维持根系生长。

• londons_explore：认为逻辑上地下部分在温度不极端的情况下继续生长是合理的。

• taeric：提出落叶可能是树木的一种生存策略，以减少冬季的风阻和生物竞争，并希望看到更多关于树木生长的研究。

• jnellis：通过实际经验（冬季树根堵塞下水道）支持冬季根系生长的观点。

• damnitbuilds：认为这种发现应在几百年前就被揭示，暗示其显而易见。

• mvdtnz：认为这是常识，研究是浪费时间和精力。

• naikrovek：自称早就知道冬季根系生长的事实，并通过童年实验（观察染色水在根中的移动）支持这一观点。

补充讨论：
• 研究的新颖性和实用性受到不同程度的认可和质疑。
• 个人经验和观察在讨论中扮演重要角色，提供了实际例子支持不同观点。
• 争议的焦点在于冬季树木根系生长的发现是否为新知识，以及草甘膦对生态系统的影响是否被低估。

43448035.article_content:
09/01/2025
News
A study reveals that deciduous trees’ roots remain active in winter
Media Relations Manager
Ángela Justamante
Biologist and scientific communicator, currently she is the press officer at CREAF. She also has experience in European projects and scientific outreach.
Deciduous trees — such as beeches and birches — change colour from season to season. Between autumn and winter, they lose their leaves and go into a state of dormancy, halting their above-ground growth to save energy for the coming spring, when they will sprout new leaves. Until now, their roots were also thought to become dormant, ‘hibernating’ along with the rest of the tree. However, a study published today in the journal
Nature Ecology & Evolution
shows that the roots of deciduous trees actually grow without pause all year round.
The study was led by University of Antwerp researcher Lorène J. Marchand and involved CREAF and the Spanish National Research Council (CSIC)
. Its findings suggest that forest soils have a greater carbon sink capacity than was previously believed, as they accumulate carbon all year long rather than only when trees are more active and their leaves are photosynthesizing. This discovery alters our ideas about how deciduous trees might adapt to climate change in the future.
Our results demonstrate that the above-ground and below-ground parts of a tree follow separate calendars, allowing for underground growth to be prioritized in winter and aerial growth at the beginning of spring.
Paolo Zuccarini
“Our results demonstrate that
the above-ground and below-ground parts of a tree follow separate calendars
, allowing for underground growth to be prioritized in winter and aerial growth at the beginning of spring,” says CREAF researcher Paolo Zuccarini, a co-author of the study. This divergence could offer a
strategic advantage
: in winter, while the rest of the tree is dormant, its roots store reserves of carbohydrates and nitrogen-rich substances, such as proteins and amino acids. Thus, when the tree ‘reawakens’, it will have enough nourishment for leaves to bud and photosynthesis to resume, which is essential for trunk and branch growth. “It’s kind of like having building blocks ready to use in the spring, when the priority is to produce leaves so that photosynthesis can start again,” explains Zuccarini.
This surprising research was conducted with four tree species — European beech (
Fagus sylvatica
), silver birch (
Betula pendula
), pedunculate oak (
Quercus robur
) and common aspen (
Populus tremula
) — in various temperate forests in
Spain, Belgium and Norway
. In total, the
researchers studied 330 specimens
, comprising both mature trees and three-year-old saplings. They collected a
thousand samples of coarse roots, i.e. roots with a diameter of over 2 mm
, which are woody organs and therefore undergo wood formation (referred to as xylogenesis). “Our data show that coarse roots remain active even at soil temperatures of under 3°C, refuting the theory that cold brings growth below ground to a halt,” remarks Marchand, the study’s lead author.
Some of the roots analysed. Author: Lorène J. Marchand, researcher at the University of Antwerp and lead author of the study.
Some of the roots analysed. Author: Lorène J. Marchand, researcher at the University of Antwerp and lead author of the study.
More carbon below ground
Another noteworthy finding is that forest soils may be a greater carbon reservoir than was previously thought, given that the study establishes that
deciduous trees fix carbon throughout the year
. The researchers explain that trees store carbon in their structure and use it for wood growth in their roots and trunks. This stored carbon is highly stable, as it is incorporated into plant tissues in the form of lignified biomass, composed of cellulose, hemicellulose and lignin. “Coarse roots actually contribute significantly to trees acting as carbon reservoirs, as they account for up to
20 to 30% of a tree’s total biomass
due to their high density,” points out Zuccarini. The carbon cycle in trees has traditionally been considered to be closely linked to the aerial growth cycle; that would entail carbon dioxide fixing peaking in spring, when trees have leaves, carry out photosynthesis, and capture carbon to use it for trunk and root growth. However, the new data from the study show that trees use carbon all year round.
Roots that help trees cope with climate change
As the study’s results indicate that root growth does not stop in winter, the authors suggest that
the biological clock of roots may be not so much influenced by external signals (e.g. temperature and light)
as controlled by internal signals (e.g. the tree’s carbon reserves). “This is in contrast to the above-ground part of the tree, which is more affected by the external climate,” comments CREAF-based CSIC researcher Josep Peñuelas, another of the study’s co-authors. Preparing their roots in winter for use in spring could help trees adapt

data.title: My Favorite C++ Pattern: X Macros (2023)
data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了C++中一种称为“X宏”的模式，该模式主要用于代码生成，特别适合处理大量重复代码的情况，如声明多个变量或类、执行相似操作等。作者以Chapel编译器中的字符串驻留（String Interning）为例，展示了如何使用X宏来简化和自动化代码编写。通过在一个头文件中定义宏列表，开发者可以在多个地方“迭代”该列表以生成所需的代码，从而减少手动编写和维护重复代码的工作量。文章还提到该模式在抽象语法树（AST）类层次结构中的应用，展示了其广泛的实用性。使用X宏不仅提高了代码的可维护性，还减少了添加新代码时的出错风险。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：X宏的使用及其在C和C++中的实现与争议

不同观点：
• senozhatsky认为X宏的实现类似于Linux内核中的trace-events，通过宏定义实现结构化的跟踪和日志记录，并提供具体实现例子。
• kragen指出X宏更多是一种C语言模式，并分享了自己使用X宏和X-macros来处理VNC协议消息的序列化和反序列化的经验，认为这种方法比传统的C预处理器方法更干净。
• jchw认为X宏是C++中的一种经典模式，尽管它主要因为C++宏不够强大而有用，并提到了一种通过生成字节数组文本的方式来进行bin2c转换的技巧。
• loeg表示虽然不喜欢X宏，但承认其在某些情况下非常有用，例如用于生成枚举和字符串表。
• Blackthorn对X宏的使用持怀疑态度，倾向于使用外部代码生成脚本而不是依赖预处理器宏。
• wat10000建议对宏进行更具描述性的命名，并提出了一些改进宏使用的方法。
• kevin_thibedeau指出X宏在需要同时在同一翻译单元中使用多个宏时的问题，建议通过传递列表宏来避免使用#undef。
• malkia通过在LuaJIT源码中学习到X宏的使用，并应用在C API的封装中。
• gibibit认为X宏在C中非常有用，但需要避免过度使用，并将其与Rust的声明宏进行比较。
• PaulHoule分享了X宏在IBM 360汇编语言和CICS应用中的历史使用情况。
• randomNumber7对需要使用这些“ hack”方法解决问题感到怀疑，认为可能有更简单的语言可以更容易地实现相同功能。
• sfpotter认为使用D语言可以完全避免这些问题。
• KerrAvon强烈反对X宏，认为这种预处理器与代码混合的方式难以调试和维护，是一种反模式，建议在C++中尽量避免使用。

补充讨论：
• X宏在C和C++中的使用历史和实际应用案例。
• 对X宏的不同改进建议，包括更具描述性的命名和避免使用#undef的方法。
• 对X宏的争议，主要集中在代码的可维护性和调试难度上，部分开发者认为这是一种反模式。
• 其他语言（如D语言）在处理类似问题上的优势。

争议的焦点：
• X宏是否是一种良好的编程实践，尤其是在C++中，其可维护性和调试难度成为争议的核心。
• 是否需要依赖预处理器宏来实现功能，或者是否有更简单和现代的语言可以替代。

My Favorite C++ Pattern: X Macros
C++
Chapel
Compilers
Posted on October 14, 2023.
Table of Contents
When I first joined the
Chapel
team,
one pattern used in its C++-based compiler made a strong impression on me. Since
then, Iâve used the pattern many more times, and have been very satisfied with
how it turned out. However, it feels like the pattern is relatively unknown, so
I thought Iâd show it off, and some of its applications in the
Chapel compiler
. Iâve slightly tweaked
a lot of the snippets I directly show in this article for the sake of simpler
presentation; Iâve included links to the original code (available on GitHub)
if you want to see the unabridged version.
Broadly speaking, the âX Macrosâ pattern is about generating code. If you have a
lot
of repetitive code to write (declaring many variables or classes, performing
many very similar actions, etc.), this pattern can save a lot of time, lead
to much more maintainable code, and reduce the effort required to add
more
code.
I will introduce the pattern in its simplest form with my first example:
interning strings
.
Application 1: String Interning
The Chapel compiler interns a lot of its strings. This way, it can reduce the
memory footprint of keeping identifiers in memory (every string
"x"
is
actually the
same
string) and make for much faster equality comparisons
(you can just perform a pointer comparison!). Generally, a
Context
class
is used to manage interning state. A new interned string can be constructed
using the context object in the following manner:
UniqueString
::
get
(
ctxPtr
,
"the string"
);
Effectively, this performs a search of the currently existing unique strings.
If one with the content (
"the string"
in this case) doesnât exist, itâs
created and registered with the
Context
. Otherwise, the existing string is
returned. Some strings, however, occur a lot in the compiler, to the point that
it would be inefficient to perform the whole âfind-or-createâ operation every
time. One example is the
"this"
string, which is an identifier with a lot of
special behavior in the language (much like
this
in languages such as Java).
To support such frequent flier strings, the compiler initializes them once,
and creates a variable per-string that can be accessed to get that stringâs value.
Thereâs that repetitive code. Defining a brand new variable for each string,
of which there are around 100 at the time of writing, is a lot of boilerplate.
There are also at least two places where code needs to be added:
once in the declaration of the variables, once in the code that initializes them.
[note:
A third use in the compiler is actually a variadic template defined over
character arrays. The template is defined and specialized in such a way that
you can refer to a variable by its string contents (i.e., you can write
USTR("the string")
instead of
theStringVariable
).
]
It would be very easy to accidentally modify the former but not the latter,
especially for developers not familiar with how these âcommon stringsâ are
implemented.
This is where the X Macros come in. If you look around the compiler source code,
thereâs a header file that looks something like the following:
From
all-global-strings.h
, around line 31
X
(
align
,
"align"
)
X
(
atomic
,
"atomic"
)
X
(
bool_
,
"bool"
)
X
(
borrow
,
"borrow"
)
X
(
borrowed
,
"borrowed"
)
X
(
by
,
"by"
)
X
(
bytes
,
"bytes"
)
// A lot more of these...
Whatâs this
X
thing? That right there is the essence of the pattern: the macro
X
isnât defined in the header!
Effectively,
all-global-strings.h
is just
a list, and we can âiterateâ over this list to generate some code for each
one of its elements, in as many places as we want. What I mean by this is
that we can then write code like the following:
From
global-strings.h
, around line 76
struct
GlobalStrings
{
#define X(field, str) UniqueString field;
#include
"all-global-strings.h"
#undef X
};
In this case, we define the macro
X
to ignore the value of the string (weâre
just declaring it here), and create a new
UniqueString
variable declaration.
Since the declaration is inside the
GlobalStrings
struct, this ends up
creating a field. Just like that, weâve declared a class with over 100
fields. Initialization is equally simple:
From
Context.cpp
, around line 49
GlobalStrings
globalStrings
;
Context
rootContext
;
static
void
initGlobalStrings
()
{
#define X(field, str) globalStrings.field = UniqueString::get(&rootContext, str);
#include
"chpl/framework/all-global-strings.h"
#undef X
}
With this, weâve completely automated the code for for both declaring and
initializing all 100 of our unique strings. Adding a new string doesnât require
a developer to know all of the places where this is implemented: just by
modifying the
all-global-strings.h
header with a new call to
X
, they can
add both a new variable and code to initialize it. Pretty robust!

data.title: Hann: A Fast Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search Library for Go
data.author: habedi0
data.article_summary: Hann 是一个用于 Go 语言的高性能近似最近邻搜索库，支持在高维空间中进行高效的相似性搜索。它提供了多种索引数据结构，包括 HNSW（层次导航小世界图）、PQIVF（乘积量化倒排文件）和 RPT（随机投影树）。Hann 具有统一的索引接口，支持任意维度向量的索引和搜索，并利用 SIMD（AVX）指令加速距离计算。它还支持批量插入、删除、更新向量，以及将索引保存到磁盘和加载。Hann 适用于构建向量数据库或为 Go 应用添加快速的内存相似性搜索功能。安装需 Go 1.21 及以上版本、C/C++ 编译器和支持 AVX 指令的 CPU。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一个库（或项目）的技术实现、性能比较及其使用中的技术挑战

不同观点：
• [nikolayasdf123] 认为该项目使用了SIMD (AVX)指令进行快速距离计算，技术上值得关注，但缺乏与Redis、Vertex、Elastic、FAISS等其他类似系统的性能对比 benchmarks。这表明他对其实际性能和竞争力有所保留，希望看到更多比较数据。

• [nikolayasdf123] 还提到该项目需要C或C++编译，质疑其是否只是通过FFI（外部函数接口）调用C代码。这暗示他对项目依赖C语言实现和FFI的使用方式有所疑虑，可能期待更原生的解决方案。

• [oldgregg] 对该库表示赞赏，但更关注如何用Go语言原生方式从文本生成向量，表明他关心功能扩展及Go语言生态中的实现方式。

• [neonsunset] 认为该项目本可以用C#实现却选择了Go，而Go在处理某些问题（如FFI或汇编）时表现不佳。他对Go在项目中的使用提出了批评，认为Go在解决某些问题时不如C#有效。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是项目对C/C++的依赖以及通过FFI调用C代码的必要性。部分评论者（如[nikolayasdf123]）对此有所质疑，认为这可能影响项目的简洁性和跨平台性。
• 另一个值得注意的点是关于Go语言的适用性问题，尤其是其在处理FFI或汇编等底层任务时的能力不足，这引发了[neonsunset]的批评。
• 性能比较的缺乏（如[nikolayasdf123]提到的benchmarks）也是一个讨论重点，显示出用户对该项目实际表现的关注和期待。

Hann
A fast approximate nearest neighbor search library for Go
Hann is a high-performance approximate nearest neighbor search (ANN) library for Go.
It provides a collection of index data structures for efficient similarity search in high-dimensional spaces.
Currently, supported indexes include Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW),
Product Quantization Inverted File (PQIVF), and Random Projection Tree (RPT).
Hann can be seen as a core component of a vector database (like Milvus, Pinecone, Weaviate, Qdrant, etc.).
It can be used to add fast in-memory similarity search capabilities to your Go applications.
Features
Unified interface for different indexes (see
core/index.go
)
Support for indexing and searching vectors of arbitrary dimension
Fast distance computation using SIMD (AVX) instructions (see
core/simd_distance.c
)
Support for bulk insertion, deletion, and update of vectors
Support for saving indexes to disk and loading them back
Indexes
Index Name
Space Complexity
Build Complexity
Search Complexity
HNSW
$O(nd + nM)$
$O(n\log n)$
$O(\log n)$
average case
$O(n)$
worst case
PQIVF
$O(nk + kd)$
$O(nki)$
$O(\frac{n}{k})$
RPT
$O(nd)$
$O(n\log n)$
$O(\log n)$
average case
$O(n)$
worst case
$n$
: number of vectors
$d$
: number of dimensions (vector length)
$M$
: links per node (HNSW)
$k$
: number of clusters (PQIVF)
$i$
: iterations for clustering (PQIVF)
Supported Distances
The HNSW index supports the use of Euclidean, squared Euclidean, Manhattan, and cosine distances.
If cosine distance is used, the vectors are normalized on read (before they are used in the index or for search).
Note that squared Euclidean distance is slightly faster to compute than Euclidean distance
and gives the same order of closest vectors as Euclidean distance.
It can be used in place of Euclidean distance if only the order of closest vectors to
query vector is needed, not the actual distances.
The PQIVF and RPT indexes support Euclidean distance only.
Installation
Hann can be installed as a typical Go module using the following command:
go get github.com/habedi/hann@main
Hann requires Go 1.21 or later, a C (or C++) compiler, and a CPU that supports AVX instructions.

Create and use an HNSW index (using large datasets)

Create and use a PQIVF index

Create and use a PQIVF index (using large datasets)

Create and use an RPT index

Create and use an RPT index (using large datasets)

Helper functions for loading example datasets

Extra helper functions for the examples
run_datasets.go
The code to create different indexes and try them with different datasets
Datasets
Use the following commands to download the datasets used in the examples:
make download-data
#
Only needed to run the examples that use large datasets
make download-data-large
Note that to run the examples using large datasets, possibly a machine with large amounts of memory is needed
like 32 GB or more.
Check the
data
directory for information about the datasets.
Documentation
The detailed documentation for Hann packages is available on
pkg.go.dev
.
HNSW Index
The
hnsw
package provides an implementation of the HNSW graph index introduced
by
Malkov and Yashunin (2016)
.
HNSW organizes data into multiple layers of a proximity graph, which allows fast approximate nearest neighbor searches
by greedily traversing the graph from top to bottom.
The index has the following parameters:
M
: Controls the maximum number of neighbor connections per node. Higher values improve accuracy but increase
memory and indexing time (typical range: 5–48).
Ef
: Defines search breadth during insertion and searching. Higher values improve accuracy but
increase computational cost (typical range: 10–200).
PQIVF Index
The
pqivf
package provides an implementation of the PQIVF index introduced
by
Jegou et al. (2011)
.

data.article_summary: Polypane是一款强大的网站开发和测试工具，帮助开发者在不切换上下文的情况下，全面处理网站的响应式设计、可访问性、元数据和性能等问题。它支持在同一界面查看从手机到5K显示器的各种视口，提供实时结构、元数据和无障碍检查建议。开发者可以并排查看深色和浅色模式，而无需更改系统设置。所有操作如点击、滚动、输入和样式编辑等都能在多设备间同步。该工具速度快，功能强大，深受前端开发者好评，能够发现和解决不同断点间的间距问题，并提供出色的调试工具。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Polypane浏览器的功能、定价模式、必要性以及与其他工具的比较

不同观点：
• 支持与赞赏：
  - Polypane用户（如imjackofitall、runekaagaard、jamesmkenny）表示该浏览器帮助他们提高了工作效率，尤其是响应式设计和会话管理功能。他们还赞赏了其出色的客户支持（例如Kilian在Slack上快速解决问题）。
  - 用户（runekaagaard）特别指出Polypane能够很好地模拟设备问题，而Chrome无法做到这一点。

• 质疑与比较：
  - 用户（culi、machine_ghost）质疑Polypane是否真的需要作为一个独立浏览器存在，认为Firefox开发工具或Chrome已经提供了类似功能。
  - 用户（Ataraxic）关注Polypane在不同浏览器引擎（如Safari或Mozilla）中的局限性，并提到其基于Chromium可能无法完全模拟非Chromium浏览器的问题。

• 功能与定价建议：
  - 用户（bluetidepro、sureglymop、sam_goody）对订阅模式表示担忧，希望能有一次性购买选项或学生折扣。sam_goody提出了一种折中方案，即支付一段时间的费用后继续使用但不更新。
  - 用户（cantSpellSober）询问Polypane相对于BrowserStack的功能优势，以及是否集成GenAI工具，以便向经理推销。

• 免费与替代方案：
  - 用户（tonijn）询问是否有免费替代品，而short_sells_poo则表示支持付费产品，认为免费产品通常通过数据挖掘和广告盈利。

补充讨论：
- Polypane开发者Kilian亲自回应，表示愿意回答任何问题，显示了开发者与用户之间的互动。
- 一些用户（如masto）表示在了解Polypane之前已经通过其他工具解决了类似问题，但认为Polypane本可以节省他们的时间。
- 争议焦点在于Polypane的定价模式和其相对于现有免费工具的附加价值。

data.title: VGGT: Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer
data.author: xnx
data.article_summary: VGGT（Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer）是一个由牛津大学和Meta AI合作开发的前馈神经网络，能够在数秒内从一张或多张图像中推断出场景的关键3D属性，包括相机参数、深度图、3D点图和3D点轨迹等。该模型易于安装和使用，通过克隆代码库并安装依赖项即可运行。VGGT支持自动下载预训练权重，并可在Hugging Face上手动获取。用户可以根据需要选择预测不同的属性，如相机参数、深度图和点图，并通过提供的函数将深度图转换为3D点图，或跟踪特定点的3D轨迹。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：基于Transformer的3D场景重建技术的应用、潜力和局限

不同观点：
• mk_stjames认为，结合SLAM技术后，这项技术可以通过手机实现准确、长距离的户外场景映射，超越目前需要昂贵LIDAR设备才能达到的效果。他指出当前技术在长距离场景中的漂移问题，并建议利用GPS和传感器数据进行校正。
• w-m赞赏论文的结果和呈现方式，但对"苦涩的教训"（The Bitter Lesson）感到遗憾，即通过大量数据和计算资源获得结果，而非通过创新的网络设计。他提到模型训练的巨大成本和时间。
• sgnelson希望将该技术与传统摄影测量技术结合，而不是完全取代，认为这样可以实现更好的互补效果。
• davedx对该技术的实际应用场景表示困惑，希望了解其商业或实际用途。
• bhouston对户外场景示例的真实性表示怀疑，认为某些著名地标可能已在训练集中，影响了对模型泛化能力的判断。
• porphyra指出，这项技术相比以往需要大量图像和校准的方法，能够通过较少图像重建场景，是一种进步。
• jdthedisciple对实际测试结果表示失望，指出点云重建缺失了一半的输入图像特征。
• vessenes对该技术在生成高密度点云和splats（可能指代某种图形渲染技术）中的应用潜力表示关注，并探讨了模型微调的可能性。
• maelito关心该技术是否能用于构建类似Google Earth的3D场景。
• richard___强调动态场景中相机姿态估计的需求。
• ninetyninenine认为，未来的人工通用智能（AGI）将由多个模型组合而成，这种技术可能在感知领域构成一个单一模型。
• fallingmead以调侃方式表达对实际演示视频的需求。
• amelius则对讨论中使用电气工程术语表示不满。

补充讨论：
• 该技术在户外场景中的长距离映射和动态场景中的应用是讨论的重点。
• 实际应用中的精度和效果是争议的焦点，特别是在长距离和动态场景中的表现。
• 结合SLAM或传统摄影测量技术的潜在改进方向被多次提及。
• 部分评论对模型训练的巨大成本和资源消耗表示关注。
• 对模型在不同应用场景中的具体表现和微调可能性也有一定讨论。

Overview
Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer (VGGT, CVPR 2025) is a feed-forward neural network that directly infers all key 3D attributes of a scene, including extrinsic and intrinsic camera parameters, point maps, depth maps, and 3D point tracks,
from one, a few, or hundreds of its views, within seconds

data.title: If you get the chance, always run more extra network fiber cabling
data.author: hggh
data.article_summary: 本文是博客作者Chris Siebenmann对使用过时浏览器访问其博客或wiki的用户的解释和提醒。由于2025年初高流量的爬虫（包括为LLM训练收集数据的爬虫）使用旧版浏览器用户代理，特别是Chrome的，作者采取了封锁措施。如果用户因误判而被挡，建议联系作者并提供浏览器的详细信息（如User-Agent字符串）。特别提到，使用archive.*（如archive.today, archive.ph）的用户可能因类似恶意爬虫的行为被挡，建议使用更规范的archive.org进行存档。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：网络布线、光纤安装及其相关问题和建议

不同观点：
• **布线冗余和维护**：
   - [em3rgent0rdr] 和 [msarrel] 提到光纤被动物咬坏的情况，强调布线时应预留足够的冗余线缆，以便维修时无需重新挖掘。
   - [jmacd] 分享了预埋管道并预留拉线的经验，便于未来更换光纤，避免重新挖沟。

• **光纤布线的规划和成本**：
   - [protocolture] 提到在特定情况下，如旧建筑中，重新布线成本高昂，建议在初期布线时考虑未来需求，以避免后续高昂成本。
   - [timzaman] 认为在家庭网络中使用MTP/MPO光纤布线可支持未来扩展，同时建议在家中布线时考虑PoE++需求。

• **实际安装中的遗憾和建议**：
   - [bhouston] 分享了新房安装网络端口和电源插座的经验，强调提前规划的重要性，并指出安装不足带来的困扰。
   - [JoshTriplett] 补充，建议安装管道以便将来添加新电缆。

• **光纤技术选择**：
   - [ggm] 和 [eqvinox] 讨论了光纤类型的选择，认为在2025年及以后，单模光纤（SMF）应是首选，多模光纤（MMF）已过时，除非需要连接现有MMF设备。

   - [zelon88] 提到随着WiFi技术的发展，有线网络需求减少的趋势。
   - [js2] 和 [yetihehe] 分享了实际案例，包括机房被动物侵入导致光纤故障和未布线房间成为家庭办公室的尴尬。

• **历史案例和经验教训**：

• 主要集中在光纤类型的选择上，特别是在2025年及以后是否应完全淘汰多模光纤而只使用单模光纤。

43471177.article_content:
You're using a suspiciously old browser
You're probably reading this page because you've attempted to access
some part of
my blog (Wandering Thoughts)
or
CSpace
, the wiki thing it's part of. Unfortunately
you're using a browser version that my anti-crawler precautions consider
suspicious, most often because it's too old (most often this applies to
versions of Chrome). Unfortunately, as of early 2025 there's a plague
of high volume crawlers (apparently in part to gather data for LLM
training) that use a variety of old browser user agents, especially
Chrome user agents. To reduce the load on
Wandering Thoughts
I'm experimenting with
(attempting to) block all of them, and you've run into this.
If this is in error and you're using a current version of your
browser of choice, you can contact me at
my current place at the
university
(you should be able to work out the email address
from that). If possible, please let me know what browser you're
using and so on, ideally with its exactl User-Agent string.
A special note for people using archive.*
You may be seeing this through archive.today, archive.ph, archive.is,
and so on. Unfortunately, archive.* crawls pages to archive in a way that
is impossible to distinguish from malicious actors. They use old Chrome
User-Agent values, crawl from IP address blocks that are widely distributed
and not clearly identified as theirs, and some of their IP addresses have
falsified reverse DNS entries that claim they are googlebot IP addresses
(which is something that is normally done only by quite bad actors). I
suggest that you use archive.org, which is a better behaved archival
crawler and can crawl
my blog (Wandering Thoughts)
.
Chris Siebenmann, 2025-02-17

data.title: Open-sourcing OpenPubkey SSH (OPKSSH): integrating single sign-on with SSH
data.author: PranaFlux
data.article_summary: OPKSSH（OpenPubkey SSH）是一个开源项目，旨在通过集成单点登录（SSO）技术（如OpenID Connect）简化SSH密钥管理，无需手动配置SSH密钥。它利用OpenPubkey协议将公钥添加到ID Tokens中，使其能够像证书一样使用，从而支持SSH协议的SSO认证，而无需更改现有的SSH或SSO协议。OPKSSH的优势包括提高安全性，通过使用短期有效的SSH密钥减少密钥泄露风险，并提升便利性，用户只需登录身份提供商（IdP）即可生成SSH密钥。该项目解决了传统SSH密钥管理中的安全和使用难题，特别适用于需要频繁访问和权限管理的企业环境。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过ID Tokens实现SSH认证的可行性及替代方案

不同观点：
• **zokier的观点**：认为ID Tokens不包含用户公钥，无法直接用于像SSH这样的安全协议。虽然SSH认证不一定要基于公钥，但这种方法缺乏直接性，错失了一个改进的机会。他建议可以通过GSSAPI或其他类似方法实现。
• **throw0101c的观点**：提出使用SSH证书的替代方案，通过建立内部SSH CA来实现短期证书认证，并提到一些自动化获取SSH证书的项目和商业产品。
• **_hyn3的观点**：比较了Userify的SSH密钥技术，认为其去中心化密钥和集中控制平面的方式更可靠，尤其是在认证服务器离线时。同时指出其依赖较多，增加了复杂性。
• **tptacek的观点**：赞赏这种证书认证方式，提到他们使用Teleport，具有类似的短 lived 证书认证功能，并强调其访问控制和审计日志的优势。
• **somat的观点**：希望看到如何通过SSH密钥登录网页，而非使用ID Tokens进行SSH认证。
• **password4321的观点**：提到一个支持X.509证书的OpenSSH分支，并提供相关技术文章链接。
• **bzmrgonz的观点**：关注该项目的安全性，质疑其代码构建的安全性，认为将认证过程转移到opkssh上需要进行安全审计。
• **samcat116的观点**：不确定这种方法与运行支持OIDC的SSH CA相比有何优势，认为服务器只需信任CA的密钥，而不必运行验证程序。
• **atonse的观点**：比较了这种方法与Tailscale SSH，并询问两者是否可能结合使用。
• **Aeolun的观点**：认为通过公钥返回标准和服务器端认证脚本来实现SSH登录并非新颖，自OpenID Connect发明以来就已可能实现。
• **kipz的观点**：对该技术表示赞赏，并愿意尝试。
• **znpy的观点**：指出通过AuthorizedKeysCommand等已有技术可以实现类似功能，认为这种方法并无太多新意，但对作者的实现表示肯定。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于这种新方法的实用性和创新性。部分用户认为它没有充分利用SSH协议的多认证方法特性，错失了改进机会；而另一部分用户则赞赏其创新和实用性。
• 安全性和代码审计也被多次提及，表明用户对新认证方法的安全性有较高关注。
• 多种替代方案（如SSH证书、Userify、Teleport、Tailscale SSH）被提出，展示了实现安全认证的多样性。

43470906.article_content:
Open-sourcing OpenPubkey SSH (OPKSSH): integrating single sign-on with SSH
2025-03-25
Ethan Heilman
7 min read
OPKSSH makes it easy to
SSH
with single sign-on technologies like OpenID Connect, thereby removing the need to manually manage and configure SSH keys. It does this without adding a trusted party other than your identity provider (IdP).
We are excited to announce
OPKSSH (OpenPubkey SSH)
has been open-sourced under the umbrella of the OpenPubkey project. While the underlying protocol
OpenPubkey
became
an open source Linux foundation project in 2023
, OPKSSH was closed source and owned by
BastionZero (now Cloudflare)
. Cloudflare has gifted this code to the OpenPubkey project, making it open source.
In this post, we describe what OPKSSH is, how it simplifies SSH management, and what OPKSSH being open source means for you.
Background
A cornerstone of modern access control is single sign-on
(SSO)
, where a user authenticates to an
identity provider (IdP)
, and in response the IdP issues the user a
token
. The user can present this token to prove their identity, such as âGoogle says I am Aliceâ. SSO is the rare security technology that both increases convenience â users only need to sign in once to get access to many different systems â and increases security.
OpenID Connect
OpenID Connect (OIDC)
is the main protocol used for SSO. As shown below, in OIDC the IdP, called an OpenID Provider (OP), issues the user an ID Token which contains identity claims about the user, such as âemail is
[email protected]
â. These claims are digitally signed by the OP, so anyone who receives the ID Token can check that it really was issued by the OP.
Unfortunately, while ID Tokens
do
include identity claims like name, organization, and email address, they
do not
include the userâs public key. This prevents them from being used to directly secure protocols like SSH or
End-to-End Encrypted messaging
.
Note that throughout this post we use the term OpenID Provider (OP) rather than IdP, as OP specifies the exact type of IdP we are using, i.e., an OpenID IdP. We use Google as an example OP, but OpenID Connect works with Google, Azure, Okta, etc.
Shows a user Alice signing in to Google using OpenID Connect and receiving an ID Token
OpenPubkey
OpenPubkey, shown below, adds public keys to ID Tokens. This enables ID Tokens to be used like certificates, e.g. âGoogle says
[email protected]
is using public key 0x123.â We call an ID token that contains a public key a
PK Token
. The beauty of OpenPubkey is that, unlike other approaches, OpenPubkey does not require any changes to existing SSO protocols and supports any OpenID Connect compliant OP.
Shows a user Alice signing in to Google using OpenID Connect/OpenPubkey and then producing a PK Token
While OpenPubkey enables ID Tokens to be used as certificates, OPKSSH extends this functionality so that these ID Tokens can be used as SSH keys in the SSH protocol. This adds SSO authentication to SSH without requiring changes to the SSH protocol.
Why this matters
OPKSSH frees users and administrators from the need to manage long-lived SSH keys, making SSH more secure and more convenient.
âIn many organizations â even very security-conscious organizations â there are many times more obsolete authorized keys than they have employees. Worse, authorized keys generally grant command-line shell access, which in itself is often considered privileged. We have found that in many organizations about 10% of the authorized keys grant root or administrator access. SSH keys never expire.â
Â
-
Challenges in Managing SSH Keys â and a Call for Solutions
by Tatu Ylonen (Inventor of SSH)
In SSH, users generate a long-lived SSH public key and SSH private key. To enable a user to access a server, the user or the administrator of that server configures that server to trust that userâs public key. Users must protect the file containing their SSH private key. If the user loses this file, they are locked out. If they copy their SSH private key to multiple computers or back up the key, they increase the risk that the key will be compromised. When a private key is compromised or a user no longer needs access, the user or administrator must remove that public key from any servers it currently trusts. All of these problems create headaches for users and administrators.
OPKSSH overcomes these issues:
Improved security:
OPKSSH replaces long-lived SSH keys with ephemeral SSH keys that are created on-demand by OPKSSH and expire when they are no longer needed. This reduces the risk a private key is compromised, and limits the time period where an attacker can use a compromised private key. By default, these OPKSSH public keys expire every 24 hours, but the expiration policy can be set in a configuration file.
Improved usability:
Creating an SSH key is as easy as signing in to an OP. This means that a user can SSH from any computer with opkssh installed, even if they havenât copied their SSH pri

data.author: therabbithole
data.article_summary:
这篇文章总结了生物技术和医学领域的几项重要进展：

1. **纳米孔测序**：Asimov Press的Niko McCarty介绍了一种低成本的DNA测序新方法——通过扩展DNA分子（Xpandomers）使其更易读取，提高纳米孔测序的准确性并降低成本。

2. **美国对外援助**：研究显示美国对外援助每年挽救约300万人生命，但特朗普政府取消了90%的USAID合同，包括结核病、母婴健康、HIV治疗等关键项目。

3. **非阿片类止痛药**：FDA批准了Vertex Pharmaceuticals开发的Journavx，它针对NaV1.8蛋白，有效缓解疼痛且不易成瘾，但价格较高。

4. **基孔肯雅疫苗**：FDA批准了Bavarian Nordic的新疫苗，该公司还获得优先审评券，可加快未来药物上市速度。

5. **法医元科学指南**：James Heathers出版了一本关于如何检测学术研究中错误和欺诈的书。

6. **双父小鼠**：中国研究人员通过基因技术使两只雄性小鼠的DNA结合，成功产下后代，但这些小鼠有健康问题且不育。

7. **最大生物AI模型**：Arc Institute推出了Evo 2模型，能预测DNA突变是否致病，准确率超过90%。

8. **学术撤稿问题**：2022年，学术期刊的撤稿率略高于0.2%，其中80%来自Hindawi出版社。

这些进展展示了生物技术和医学领域的最新动态和挑战。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：中国研究人员通过基因技术使两只雄性小鼠的遗传物质产生后代，以及该技术背后的伦理和科学讨论。

不同观点：
• 观点一：该技术具有科学价值。评论者[freedomben]认为这项研究非常有趣，具有突破性。研究展示了通过基因编辑技术，能够让两只雄性小鼠的遗传物质结合，并产生后代，尽管后代存在健康问题和不育。这展示了科学在生殖生物学领域的进步，尤其是在理解性染色体和生殖过程方面的潜力。

• 观点二：技术成功率低，且存在严重的健康问题。研究结果显示，在164次尝试中只有7只小鼠成功出生，且这些小鼠存在严重的健康问题，并终生不育。这表明尽管技术上可行，但其成功率低，且可能导致不健康的个体，因此距离实际应用还有很长的路要走。

• 观点三：伦理争议。虽然评论中未直接提及，但该技术引发了潜在的伦理问题。例如，是否应该在哺乳动物（包括人类）中进行这样的实验，尤其是在后代存在健康问题的情况下。该技术挑战了传统的生殖观念，可能引发关于自然生殖界限的伦理辩论。

补充讨论：
• 该实验中的技术细节，例如如何将雄性小鼠的精子重新编程为干细胞，并通过去除卵子细胞核的方式产生胚胎，显示了当前基因编辑技术在生殖领域的复杂应用。

• 该研究可能对未来同性生殖的研究提供参考，即是否可能通过类似技术实现人类同性伴侣的共同生殖，但目前实验结果显示的技术局限性和伦理问题仍需进一步讨论。

争议焦点：该技术在科学进步和伦理之间的平衡，特别是在实际应用中可能产生的健康问题和伦理挑战。

We recently released Issue 18 of Works in Progress. Read about prehistoric psychopaths, fertility on demand and the king of fruits
here
. Today on Links in Progress
Asimov Press
’s Niko McCarty and our own
Saloni Dattani
return to review more important things happening in the world of biotechnology and medicine.
1. Nanopore sequencing is a promising, low-cost alternative to traditional genome sequencing methods. Nanopores are tiny holes in a membrane. When a molecule passes through a nanopore, it disrupts an electric field. Fluctuations in the field can be ‘decoded’ to figure out whether a passing molecule was an adenine, thymine, or something else. Unfortunately, its use has been limited by poor spatial resolution.
Roche has developed a new sequencing method called
Sequencing by Expansion (SBX)
, which expands DNA molecules into larger polymer structures called Xpandomers and makes them easier to read with nanopores. If successful, SBX would improve the accuracy of nanopore sequencing and bring costs down.
2. Justin Sandefur and Charles Kenny
estimate
that
US foreign aid prevents around 3 million deaths per year at a cost of
only 0.2 percent of the US’s GNI
.
The Trump administration
has scrapped
90 percent of all USAID contracts,
including
some of the most impactful programs. The scrapped contracts seem to include all tuberculosis programs, programs supplying essential medicines for maternal and child health; programs providing HIV treatment; UNICEF’s polio vaccination program; contracts for disease outbreak prevention, detection, and response; emergency food aid; earthquake assistance and more.
3.
The FDA approved a
non-opioid painkiller
.
Journavx, developed by Vertex Pharmaceuticals, targets a protein called the NaV1.8 voltage-gated sodium channel, which transmits pain signals from sensory neurons to the brain. No other drugs on the market target this protein; existing painkillers instead bind to several other different NaV channels at once. In a phase 3 trial with 2,000 patients undergoing surgery, Journavx reduced pain as effectively as hydrocodone plus paracetamol and had fewer side effects. It also does not appear to be addictive. But the drug will cost about $233 per week; opioids cost about $12 per week.
4.
The FDA
approved
a new vaccine for chikungunya
, a mosquito-borne disease that can result in joint pain for months. The new vaccine was developed by Bavarian Nordic, the same company that manufactured the Jynneos Mpox vaccine. Bavarian Nordic have been rewarded for the results of their chikungunya vaccine with a ‘priority disease voucher,’ which will allow them the opportunity to jump the FDA review queue with another drug. Because they primarily affect poorer countries, drugs for curing tropical diseases face a limited financial market. The ‘priority disease voucher’ acts as a reward for Bavarian Nordic, who can use it to
get their next drug to market faster
.
5.
A guide to ‘
forensic metascience
’.
James Heathers, a researcher and scientific sleuth, has published a textbook explaining how to probe academic studies for potential errors, questionable research practices, and scientific fraud.
6.
Chinese researchers made mice with
two genetic fathers
.
They took sperm from male mice and reprogrammed them into stem cells, effectively ‘rewinding’ their development. Those stem cells retained only one set of chromosomes, like normal sperm, but were then fused with a second sperm’s DNA — resulting in both XX and XY sex chromosomes. The resulting DNA was injected into an egg without a nucleus, producing embryos with two paternal genomes. Out of 164 attempts, seven mouse pups were born; they survived to adulthood but had serious health problems and were infertile.
7.
Arc Institute launched the
largest AI model yet
for biology
. Called Evo 2, it was trained on 9.3 trillion nucleotides of DNA from 128,000 organisms. Evo 2 can predict whether a given mutation in a DNA sequence will be pathogenic with over 90 percent accuracy, even in instances where scientists have not previously studied that mutation in the laboratory. The model was trained on 2,000 NVIDIA H100 GPUs – about 150 times more compute than AlphaFold.
Asimov Press
covered the story
.
8.
In 2022, the retraction rate across hundreds of journals slightly exceeded 0.2 percent, but about 80 percent of these retractions came from journals owned by a single publisher: Hindawi.
This
latest
Nature
report
shows that the problem is pervasive for specific publishers and for select universities. Jining First People’s Hospital had a five percent retraction

data.title: Prospero challenge, now with more garbage collection
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了Matt Keeter发起的Prospero挑战，目标是优化一个使用Python和NumPy编写的图像计算程序，使其运行更快。原始程序在执行时会占用近60GB的内存用于存储中间变量。通过引入**liveness analysis**和**garbage collection**技术，作者成功减少了内存占用，程序运行时间从40秒缩短至10秒，且内存使用控制在1GB以内。

此外，作者尝试使用CuPy（一个基于GPU的NumPy替代品），使程序在1.5秒内完成运行。然而，在尝试处理4096x4096分辨率的图像时，由于超出GPU内存限制，程序出错。

总的来说，本文展示了通过内存优化和GPU加速两种方式显著提升程序性能的过程。

from

backwards on the program to find out when it is used for the “first” time:

=
[]

set
()

Matt also mentions the GPU. I have a 1080ti in my desktop, so let’s see if we
can make use of it.

A quick internet search reveals that CuPy should be a drop-in replacement for

此外，作者尝试使用CuPy（一个基于GPU的NumPy替代品），使程序在1.5秒内完成运行。然而，在尝试处理4096x4096分辨率的图像时，由于超出GPU内存限制，程序出错。

总的来说，本文展示了通过内存优化和GPU加速两种方式显著提升程序性能的过程。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：社区建设与邻里关系，特别是在城市环境中的实现方式

不同观点：
• [afavour] 认为城市可以实现郊区那样的社区感，但其个人经验中，郊区往往缺乏真正的互动，邻居之间很少交流。
• [tptacek] 强调通过参与地方政治可以更好地认识邻居，并建立更广泛的社区联系，而不仅仅是依赖日常的偶遇。
• [czhu12] 指出当社区微信群人数过多时，容易产生小团体和社交冷却现象，建议通过定期活动保持群组的活跃度和舒适性。
• [jcdavis] 以自身经历证明该社区的成功，表示通过参与活动，邻里关系可以从陌生人转变为友好邻居。
• [phil-lnf] 提出通过与朋友或家人住在附近来促进社区文化，并介绍了一个帮助实现这一目标的公司。
• [non-] 认为社区建设的关键在于主动行动，鼓励人们从邀请邻居喝咖啡这样的小事做起。
• [austinl] 分享了疫情期间通过定期活动建立邻里关系的成功经验，如感恩节晚餐和街道聚会。
• [melenaboija] 对比了西班牙小镇和美国城市的社区文化，指出西班牙传统上邻里互动更加自然和普遍。
• [conductr] 提到其所在社区的邻里关系因人口结构和住房密度的多样性而复杂，通过举办早餐会和龙虾宴成功促进了社区互动。
• [dr__mario] 对西班牙传统的邻里互动文化在他地出现表示赞赏。
• [ramkarthikk] 认为该帖子展示了个体在社区建设中的能动性，并通过一个故事强调了第一个追随者的重要性。
• [Duhck] 抱怨其社区的业主委员会阻碍了社区活动的举办，导致缺乏邻里互动。
• [JoshTriplett] 认为通过共同兴趣建立的社区比因地理位置偶然成为邻居的关系更为牢固和有趣。

• 地方政治和社区活动在促进邻里关系中的作用，以及不同人口结构对社区互动的影响。

• 社区活动的规模和管理问题，特别是当社区群组人数过多时如何保持互动的质量和参与度。
• 业主委员会或其他管理机构在社区活动中的角色和影响，有些人认为他们阻碍了邻里互动。

data.article_summary: 本文介绍了1997年Towa Tei与Kylie Minogue合作的歌曲《GBI (German Bold Italic)》，这首歌以字体为视角，由Minogue以轻柔、机械的嗓音演唱，伴随着简约的节拍。这首techno-pop歌曲的发行还包括一个同名字体"German Bold Italic"，由艺术家Hiro Sugiyama设计，具有厚重几何的特点，与当时的设计潮流相呼应。Towa Tei曾是Dee-Lite成员，后来专注于个人项目，而Minogue在当时已是全球知名流行歌手，勇于尝试不同音乐和视觉概念。尽管《GBI》这首歌以字体为主题独具创意，但其伴随的字体并未广泛使用或支持德语等语言。

43473358.article_content:
Sometimes we invite artists, writers, and other friends to take over
our newsletter
and write about fonts from a cultural perspective. And this time, New York-based writer and editor
Whitney Mallett
took a deep dive into the 1997 Towa Tei track
GBI (German Bold Italic),
for which Kylie Minogue sang from the perspective of a typeface.
Whitney is the editor of
The Whitney Review of New Writing
, a biannual print bulletin of new criticism, and she was also the co-editor of
Barbie Dreamhouse: An Architectural Survey
.  Below, she enlightens us on the highly under-appreciated history of Towa Tei’s data-track font release.
“I Contrast, It’s Cool”: When Kylie Minogue Was German Bold Italic
Video is loading ...
Kylie Minogue announces “I am a typeface” in a 1997 song she made with producer Towa Tei. As this lyric suggests, the techno-pop track in question,
“GBI (German Bold Italic)”
, is delivered from the perspective of a font. Minogue’s breathy, almost robotic vocals bring the absurdist premise to life, reciting declarations of design compatibility over a minimalist reverb-drenched beat.
“You will like my sense of style”
is her most oft-repeated refrain.
German Bold Italic (three words Minogue intones throughout the track with staccato punctuation) is a real typeface, which was created to accompany the musical release. To develop it, Tei tapped artist
Hiro Sugiyama
, who had that same year launched the commercial design studio Enlightenment. The high-impact techno typography not only defined the record’s text-centric cover, but a glyph set was made available as a data track on Tei’s Sound Museum CD and also downloadable from both Tei’s and Minogue’s official websites. Extra-thick and geometric, the font had something in common with the heavy black frames that were Tei’s hallmark at the time. Another line from the song:
“I contrast, it’s cool.”
When this offbeat track came out, Minogue was one of the biggest pop stars in the world. The Australian “I Should Be So Lucky” singer rose to fame as a teenager in the late 1980s for clear vocals that complemented the precision of disco and dance-pop perfectly. She’s like Donna Summer in that way, a vessel for songs that can be hugely innovative and futuristic without compromising mainstream appeal. By her fifth studio album, the eponymously titled
Kylie Minogue (1994)
, she was starting to show she was curious about experimenting with different sounds and high-concept visuals. In 1995 she collaborated on a murder ballad duet with Nick Cave, and by the time she joined forces with Tei, she was dating music video director (and Björk ex) Stéphane Sednaoui, who’s often credited with influencing Minogue’s art-pop risk-taking. Sednaoui directed the video for “GBI (German Bold Italic).” In it, Minogue is dressed like a geisha roaming the streets of Tokyo (despite Tei’s involvement, the video no doubt reads today as cultural appropriation.)
Tei was a big deal back then too. Originally from Japan, he had moved to New York to study fashion in the 1980s and became one of the founding members, along with
Lady Miss Kier
and
DJ Dmitry
, of the dance music group
Dee-Lite
. Their breakthrough hit,
“Groove is In the Heart” (1990)
, undeniably one of the decade’s defining house music tracks, peaked at #4 on the Billboard Hot 100. A few years before Tei’s collaboration with Minogue, at Dee-Lite’s height, he decided to quit the group and move back to Japan to focus on solo projects — in part because he’d suffered a back injury from a fall which affected his ability to tour. Sound Museum — which “GBI” the song and glyph set feature on — was his second solo album. In addition to Minogue, he recruited an eclectic group of artists for the project, from rappers Biz Markie and Mos Def to bossa nova royalty Bebel Gilberto. “GBI,” however, is the only song about a font.
Leading up to the turn of the millennium, typography trends included a revival of thick, rounded, condensed, futuristic san-serifs from the late ’60s and early ’70s. German Bold Italic feels part of this wave. So does
The Powerpuff Girls
logo, designed for the TV show which first aired in 1998, a year after Tei and Minogue’s song.
In the comments section of fontsinsuse.com
, the site’s editor Florian Hardwig compares German Bold Italic to
Futura Extra Bold Italic
. He points out, however, that while Futura is German, released by the Bauer Foundry in Frankfurt in 1927, Futura Extra Bold isn’t German at all: “It was added by Edwin W. Shaar for Intertype in the US in 1952, based on Paul Renner’s design. The oblique followed in 1955, made by Shaar together with Tommy Thompson.” Another user named Thiago, points out that, rather ironically, the glyph set for German Bold Italic doesn’t support the German language.
Despite being made available for anyone to download (you can still download it via
an old version of Minogue’s website
, accessible using the Wayback Machine), German Bold Italic’s only documented usage outside of Tei and Minogue’s

data.title: Borne Back Ceaselessly into the Past: Fitzgerald, Gatsby and WWI
data.author: gmays
data.article_summary: 《了不起的盖茨比》背景与一战紧密相关。作者F. Scott Fitzgerald在一战期间的经历塑造了小说中的角色和社会变迁。1917年，Fitzgerald在普林斯顿大学就读时选择参军，成为美国陆军少尉，并在堪萨斯州接受训练，期间开始写作《人间天堂》。他被派往阿拉巴马州的谢里登营地，在那里遇到了未来的妻子Zelda Sayre，她的形象启发了小说中的黛西。尽管Fitzgerald未能如愿赴法参战，但战争及其后的社会变化深刻影响了他的作品，包括《了不起的盖茨比》。小说中，盖茨比被误传为一战中的德国间谍，反映了当时社会对德奥国民的敌视和限制。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对《了不起的盖茨比》及F·斯科特·菲茨杰拉德与第一次世界大战关系的不同角度解读

不同观点：
• [shadowtree] 引用菲茨杰拉德小说《夜色温柔》中的段落，强调一战中的惨烈与不可重复性。该段落描述了一战的独特性，指出这场战争依赖于特定的历史与文化背景，尤其是欧洲中产阶级的生活方式与情感积淀，这种条件在现代无法复制。他还通过引用其他历史人物与事件来支持这一观点，认为年轻一代无法再现这种战争模式。
  
• [alabastervlog] 对《了不起的盖茨比》与一战历史背景的联系表示兴趣，并提到菲茨杰拉德个人经历与战争的关系。同时，他还介绍了与战争相关的博物馆，提供了实际参观信息，尤其是对位于堪萨斯城的博物馆的可达性进行了说明。

• [erehweb] 关注《了不起的盖茨比》中盖茨比故事的不可靠性，提出问题：评论家是否普遍认为盖茨比完全编造了自己的背景，甚至购买了黑山勋章，还是仅仅在细节上不够严谨？这一观点引发了对小说中人物叙述可信度的讨论。

• [crims0n] 从个人阅读体验出发，表达了对《了不起的盖茨比》的喜爱，认为这本书是他的文学入门读物。他强调了该书的文学价值与可读性，并指出其篇幅短小，适合在闲暇时间阅读。

Arts & Culture
Borne Back Ceaselessly Into the Past: Fitzgerald, Gatsby and WWI
Image
“The Great Gatsby,” written by F. Scott Fitzgerald in 1925, offers a vivid portrayal of post-World War I America.
Fitzgerald, and the characters in his novel, were deeply shaped by the Great War.
By placing the story in its historical context, he reveals the complex societal shifts in the United States in the years after WWI.
F. Scott Fitzgerald and WWI
Born in September 1896, Francis Scott Key (F. Scott) Fitzgerald was 20 years old and attending Princeton University in 1917. He had been courting a young girl named Ginevra King. (That failed relationship is thought to be one of the inspirations for the character Daisy in “The Great Gatsby.”) Fitzgerald was already writing for university clubs and nearing graduation
when Congress declared war.
Despite this, he chose to drop out of Princeton to join the U.S. military, accepting a commission as a second lieutenant in the U.S. Army.
Image
Photograph of F. Scott Fitzgerald from The Nassau Herald, published in 1917 by Princeton University.
Source:
Mudd Manuscript Library
The Army assigned Fitzgerald to the Officer Training Corps at Fort Leavenworth, Kansas, where he was trained as an infantry officer. He wrote his first draft for “This Side of Paradise” during this period – and (as he later told it to the Saturday Evening Post) was reprimanded for writing it instead of studying infantry tactics by his training officer, future five-star general and 34th President of the United States Dwight D. Eisenhower.
Image
A postcard showing life at Fort Leavenworth, Kansas: soldiers lining up with mess kits; soldiers having their goods and cots inspected; a practice trench; and two men having breakfast in a tent.
Object ID:
1998.58.47
Image
Photo of Lieutenant Dwight D. Eisenhower and his wife, Mamie, taken during WWI. Eisenhower never left the U.S. during WWI but was responsible for training soldiers across various camps. In the interwar years, Eisenhower continued his military career and by the outbreak of WWII, was a Brigadier General. In December 1944, he became General of the Army.
Source:
Library of Congress
In June 1918, Fitzgerald was on the move. He went with the 9th Division to Camp Sheridan, a mobilization camp just outside Montgomery, Alabama.
By day, his brigade was busy building new units,
training recruits and draftees
and preparing to ship overseas to the Western Front – typical for many of the newly-activated units of the American Expeditionary Forces (A.E.F.). By night, young officers found themselves with time on their hands to explore Montgomery and take in the social life. For Fitzgerald, this relatively calm period gave him time to edit his manuscript for “This Side of Paradise.”
Image
An oversized souvenir postcard depicting drawings of Camp Sheridan, 1917.
Object ID:
2006.74.2b
It was during one of those jaunts to Montgomery when he met his future wife, Zelda Sayre. Their stormy relationship is thought to be another inspiration for Daisy in “The Great Gatsby.” He even appropriates a quote from Zelda about their own daughter as one of Daisy’s lines.
Image
Photograph of a young Zelda Sayre as a senior in high school, 1918.
Source:
Alabama Dept. of Archives and History
“I’m glad it’s a girl. And I hope she’ll be a fool—that’s the best thing a girl can be in this world, a beautiful little fool.”
—Daisy Buchanan in “The Great Gatsby,” originally spoken by Zelda Fitzgerald
Image
Photograph of F. Scott Fitzgerald in uniform, commissioned by himself in 1917.
Source:
F. Scott Fitzgerald Archives
On Oct. 26, 1918, Fitzgerald and his unit were moved again – this time to Camp Mills on Long Island, New York, with plans to be sent to France. Fate would intervene:
the Armistice was signed on Nov. 11.
He never went “Over There.”
Fitzgerald always seemed to regret never experiencing the war firsthand, as suggested in his 1936 story “I Didn’t Get Over.” Yet World War I, its veterans and the new world that emerged from it deeply shaped his post-war writings, including “This Side of Paradise” (1920), “May Day” (1920), “The Crack-Up” (1936), “The Beautiful and the Damned” (1922) and “Winter Dreams” (1922). And of course “The Great Gatsby,” published in 1925.
Image
Original cover for "The Great Gatsby."

Based on a True Story? Historical Context for “The Great Gatsby” Characters
Jay Gatsby
The rumors fly around Gatsby’s social circle, tarnishing his reputation:
“A German spy during the war,” some say.
He is “a nephew or a cousin of Kaiser Wilhelm’s.”
There are even whispers Gatsby is a murderer connected “to Von Hindenburg.”
The novel later reveals his true identity as a U.S. WWI veteran, but at that time in history, accusations of German loyalty in the United States could ruin lives. data.author: geox
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了磷元素在生命起源中的关键作用，以及大型苏打湖（如美国加州的莫诺湖）可能是生命起源的摇篮。磷是DNA、RNA和ATP等重要分子的组成部分，但在地表较为稀缺。研究表明，生命起源前的化学反应需要极高浓度的磷，而大型无外流苏打湖通过蒸发保持磷浓度，满足了这一条件。这些湖泊由于水体蒸发，磷无法被冲走，从而积累到足够浓度，支持生命起源的化学反应。与小湖不同，大湖的磷供应足够持久，能维持生命的发展。因此，研究人员认为，大型苏打湖可能是生命起源的理想环境。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同环境下的生命起源理论，特别是碱性湖泊和碱性热液喷口与生命起源的关系。

不同观点：
• **[culi]** 认为高碱性湖泊是高生产力的生态系统，尽管适应这种极端环境的生物被视为“嗜极生物”，但也许我们这些不生活在极端环境中的生物才是真正的“嗜极生物”。他指出，在生态学中，“生产力”通常通过测量系统中的生物量增长速率来确定。

• **[gomijacogeo]** 分享了一个关于科罗拉多大学博尔德分校的Harry Brodsky讨论海洋喷口周围磷可用性的视频，将讨论引向海洋喷口和磷元素对生命起源的重要性。

• **[Sniffnoy]** 质疑磷的可用性是否是碱性湖泊作为生命起源地的唯一原因，并将其与生命起源于碱性热液喷口的理论进行比较，提醒大家碱性热液喷口与著名的“黑烟囱”不同。

• **[BobbyTables2]** 以幽默的方式提问碱性湖泊是否有电解质，属于轻松的插曲，没有提出实质性论据。

• **[m0llusk]** 支持碱性湖泊环境可能为早期生命提供条件的说法，并进一步提出地下通道和空腔也可能为早期生命提供了环境。这些地方有高温、丰富的矿物质（包括磷），以及各种相互连接的空腔，可以作为反应室甚至细胞。

• **[toast0]** 引用他人观点，戏谑地指出富含磷的大型苏打湖可能是生命起源的地方，并用可乐作比喻，继续围绕磷元素的作用展开讨论。

• **[im3w1l]** 引用了被标记为“无意义”的评论，质疑关于生命起源的推测是否有价值。他认为这种推测可以为未来的研究提供方向，如寻找早期生命的遗迹或在实验室中模拟生命起源的条件。如果这些研究有希望，可以为外星生物学提供线索，并影响未来探测器的发射方向。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于关于生命起源的推测是否具有科学价值以及如何验证这些推测。im3w1l等人认为这些推测难以验证，但也有观点认为这种推测可以指导未来的实验和探索。
• 讨论中多次提到磷元素在生命起源中的重要性，以及不同环境（碱性湖泊、碱性热液喷口、地下空腔）作为生命起源地的可能性。
