data.title: Chicago-Sized Iceberg Hid Ancient Ecosystem, Scientists Reveal
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 科学家在亚特兰大洲附近的A-84巨型冰山脱离后，发现了海底存在着丰富的生态系统。利用遥控水下机器人SuBastian，研究团队在1300米深的海底观察到大型珊瑚、海绵以及冰鱼、巨型海蜘蛛和章鱼等多种生物。这些生物群落可能已存在几十年甚至几百年。冰山的脱离让科学家有机会探索原本难以接近的海底区域。研究还显示，洋流对冰层下的生命起着关键作用。虽然冰架的消退令人担忧，但它也为科学探索提供了机会。Schmidt海洋研究所的R/V Falkor（too）研究船将继续在这一领域进行探索。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：冰鱼及其生态系统的科学发现与环境担忧

不同观点：
• [dmix] 分享了关于冰鱼（Channichthyidae）的科学发现，特别提到它们是已知唯一一种在成年阶段血液中缺乏血红蛋白的脊椎动物。他还引用了2021年2月科学家在南极威德尔海发现的大规模冰鱼繁殖地的例子，该繁殖地约有6000万个活跃巢穴，每个巢穴由一只成年鱼守护，平均每个巢穴有1,735颗卵。

• [Kon-Peki] 用幽默的方式将92平方英里的面积转换为相当于3个不到的德国城市杜塞尔多夫，以此帮助人们理解该区域的大小，没有深入讨论科学内容。

• [DidYaWipe] 以戏谑的语气提到发现了一个“原始深盘披萨，大小如Wrigley Field”，显然是在开玩笑，并没有对科学发现做实质性讨论。

Scientists scrutinizing the seafloor beneath a calving iceberg found a remarkable array of living creatures, switching up notions of how the giant chunks of ice affect their immediate environs.
The scientists investigated a region of seafloor recently exposed by the calving of a gigantic icebergâA-84âwhich is as large as Chicago. The team found a surprisingly vibrant community of critters on the seafloor below where A-84 was once attached to an ice shelf attached to Antarctica.
âWe didnât expect to find such a beautiful, thriving ecosystem,” said Patricia Esquete, the expedition’s co-chief scientist and a researcher at the University of Aveiro in Portugal, in a British Antarctic Survey
release
. “Based on the size of the animals, the communities we observed have been there for decades, maybe even hundreds of years.â
Without the 197-square-mile (510-square-kilometer) iceberg in the way, the team was able to scrutinize the seafloor at depths of 4,265 feet (1,300 meters) using the remotely operated vehicle (ROV)
SuBastian
. The team found large corals and sponges supporting other lifeforms, including icefish, giant sea spiders, and octopus.
The scientists who made the discovery were part of a team aboard the Schmidt Ocean Institute’s
R/V Falkor (too)
, a 363-foot-long (111-meter) vessel that’s regularly revealing hidden details of life at the bottom of Earth’s oceans. The vessel has previously
mapped unknown areas
of the ocean floor and even captured the
intimate breeding grounds
of octopuses.
With the icebergs covering the seafloor, organisms below the shelf cannot get nutrients for survival from the surface. The team hypothesized that ocean currents are a critical driver for life beneath the ice sheets. The team also collected data on the larger ice sheet, whose shrinking size spells concern for the animals that live beneath it.
âThe ice loss from the Antarctic Ice Sheet is a major contributor to sea level rise worldwide,â said the expedition’s other co-chief scientist, Sasha Montelli, a researcher at University College London, in the same release. “Our work is critical for providing longer-term context of these recent changes, improving our ability to make projections of future change â projections that can inform actionable policies. We will undoubtedly make new discoveries as we continue to analyze this vital data.â
Though the ice shelf disappearing is worrying, it also creates an opportunity for scientists to explore an area that is otherwise even harder to access.Â
ROV SuBastianÂ
andÂ
R/V Falkor (too)
will almost certainly make new discoveries about extreme environments where life ekes out existence before their journeys are brought to an end.

data.title: The Ethics of Spreading Life in the Cosmos
data.author: JPLeRouzic
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了定向胚种论（directed panspermia）的伦理和哲学问题，即人类是否应主动在宇宙中传播生命。文章回顾了胚种论的历史，从100多年前瑞典科学家Svante Arrhenius的星光压力推送微生物理论，到德国医生Hermann Richter的永恒生命观。20世纪中期，Carl Sagan和Iosif Shklovskii提出人类或可尝试这一方法，Michael Mautner和Greg Matloff进一步探讨了相关风险和伦理问题。近年来，Asher Soryl和Anders Sandberg重新评估了定向胚种论的伦理和潜在陷阱，提出使用小型容器装载耐极端环境的细菌孢子，通过长时间星际旅行传播生命。该想法依然充满争议，但技术上或可行，例如利用类似旅行者号等探测器的星际能力。关键问题在于是否应人为干预生命在宇宙中的传播及其潜在后果。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：太空探索与生命扩展的伦理和可行性

不同观点：
• [anigbrowl] 认为，文中所提到的太空探索计划可能只是为哲学教授创造职位。他质疑大规模生物殖民的成本和难度，并提出相比之下，像孢子或带有DNA信息的生物探针可能更具可行性。

• [smokel] 提出是否应该进行此类太空扩展，并指出在技术控制方面人类往往表现不佳。他认为不需要先解决所有问题，个人也可能积累足够资源来实现此类计划。

• [flenserboy] 支持生命扩展到宇宙的观点，认为生命会自然扩展到可生存的空间。他建议发送单细胞生物和缓步动物到可能支持生命的外星环境，但强调需事先研究以避免覆盖已有生命形式。

• [bhouston] 坚决支持将生命扩展到宇宙中，并提到自我复制航天器的概念。他对未来与其他生命形式的接触持谨慎乐观态度，并提到科幻作品对其思考的启发。

• [ycombinete] 将太空扩展的伦理问题与反出生主义的哲学辩论联系起来，引用David Benatar的著作，指出将生命带入世界（或新环境）可能是不道德的。

• [Simon_O_Rourke] 以幽默方式提出一个简单的伦理筛选标准，即根据是否曾在特定地点居住过决定是否能登上飞船，以此质疑太空移民的伦理选择。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点包括太空探索和生物殖民的伦理问题，特别是对潜在未知生命形式的影响以及人类是否有权进行这样的扩展。
• 讨论中还涉及到技术控制和个人资源积累对实现太空扩展计划的影响。
• 哲学层面的思考，如反出生主义，也被引入讨论，增加了对生命价值和扩展伦理的深度分析。

43474250.article_content:
The Ethics of Spreading Life in the Cosmos
by
Paul Gilster
|
Mar 25, 2025
|
Astrobiology and SETI
|
10 comments
We keep trying to extend our reach into the heavens, but the idea of panspermia is that the heavens are actually responsible for us. Which is to say, that at least the precursor materials that allow life to emerge came from elsewhere, and did not originate on Earth. Over a hundred years ago Swedish scientist Svante Arrhenius suggested that the pressure of starlight could push bacterial spores between planets and we can extend the notion to interstellar journeys of hardy microbes as well, blasted out of planetary surfaces by such things as meteor impacts and flung into outbound trajectories.
Panspermia notions inevitably get into the question of deep time given the distances involved. The German physician Hermann Richter (1808-1876) had something interesting to say about this, evidently motivated by his irritation with Charles Darwin, who had made no speculations on the origin of the life he studied. Richter believed in a universe that was eternal, and indeed thought that life itself shared this characteristic:
“We therefore also regard the existence of organic life in the universe as eternal; it has always existed and has propagated itself in uninterrupted succession.
Omne vivum ab aeternitate e cellula
!” [All life comes from cells throughout eternity].
Thus Richter supplied what Darwin did not, while accepting the notion of the evolution of life in the circumstances in which it found itself. By 1908 Arrhenius could write:
“Man used to speculate on the origin of matter, but gave that up when experience taught him that matter is indestructible and can only be transformed. For similar reasons we never inquire into the origin of the energy of motion. And we may become accustomed to the idea that life is eternal, and hence that it is useless to inquire into its origin.”
The origins of panspermia thinking go all the way back to the Greeks, and the literature is surprisingly full as we get into the 19th and early 20th Century, but I won’t linger any further on that because the paper I want to discuss today deals with a notion that came about only within the last 60 years or so. As described by Carl Sagan and Iosif Shklovskii in 1966 (in
Intelligent Life in the Universe
, it’s that panspermia is not only possible but might be something that humans might one day attempt.
Indeed, Michael Mautner and Greg Matloff proposed this in the 1970s (citation below), while digging into the potential risks and ethical problems associated with such a project. The idea remains controversial, to judge from the continuing flow of papers on various aspects of panspermia. We now have a study from Asher Soryl (University of Otago, NZ) and Anders Sandberg (MIMIR Centre for Long Term Futures Research, Stockholm) again sizing up guided panspermia ethics and potential pitfalls. What is new here is the exploration of the philosophy of the directed panspermia idea.
Image:
Can life be spread by comets? Comet 2I/Borisov is only the second interstellar object known to have passed through our Solar System, but presumably there are vast numbers of such objects moving between the stars. In this image taken by the NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope, the comet appears in front of a distant background spiral galaxy (2MASX J10500165-0152029, also known as PGC 32442). The galaxy’s bright central core is smeared in the image because Hubble was tracking the comet. Borisov was approximately 326 million kilometres from Earth in this exposure. Its tail of ejected dust streaks off to the upper right. Credit: ESA/Hubble.
Spreading life is perhaps more feasible than we might imagine at first glance. We have achieved interstellar capabilities already, with the two Voyagers, Pioneers 10 and 11 and New Horizons on hyperbolic trajectories that will never return to the Solar System. Remember, time is flexible here because a directed panspermia effort would be long-term, seeding numerous stars over periods of tens of thousands of years. The payload need not be large, and Soryl and Sandberg consider a 1 kg container sufficient, one containing freeze-dried bacterial spores inside water-dissoluble UV protective sheaths. Such spores could survive millions of years in transit:
…desiccation and freezing makes
D. radiodurans
able to survive radiation doses of 140 kGy, equivalent to hundreds of millions of years of background radiation on Earth. A simple opening mechanism such as thermal expansion could release them randomly in a habitable zone without requiring the use of electronic components. Moreover, normal bacteria can be artificially evolved for extreme radiation tolerance, in addition to other traits that would increase their chances of surviving the journey intact. Further genetic modifications are also possible so that upon landing on suitable exoplanets, evolutionary processes could be accelerated by a factor of ∼1000 to facilitate terraforming, eventual
43474250.article_summary: 本文探讨了定向胚种论（directed panspermia）的伦理和哲学问题，即人类是否应主动在宇宙中传播生命。文章回顾了胚种论的历史，从100多年前瑞典科学家Svante Arrhenius的星光压力推送微生物理论，到德国医生Hermann Richter的永恒生命观。20世纪中期，Carl Sagan和Iosif Shklovskii提出人类或可尝试这一方法，Michael Mautner和Greg Matloff进一步探讨了相关风险和伦理问题。近年来，Asher Soryl和Anders Sandberg重新评估了定向胚种论的伦理和潜在陷阱，提出使用小型容器装载耐极端环境的细菌孢子，通过长时间星际旅行传播生命。该想法依然充满争议，但技术上或可行，例如利用类似旅行者号等探测器的星际能力。关键问题在于是否应人为干预生命在宇宙中的传播及其潜在后果。

data.title: Show HN: Feudle – A daily puzzle game built with AI
data.author: papaolivia92
data.article_summary: Feudle是一款在线猜谜游戏，玩家需猜测前一天其他玩家提交的最热门答案。游戏规则简单：猜测热门答案，正确答案会显示在板上并附上回答数量。若三次未猜中即出局。玩家还可以提交自己的问题供未来使用，并查看个人统计数据。游戏提供每日邮件订阅功能，并允许分享结果和投票选择未来调查主题。玩家需登录Google账户以保存游戏进度和查看详细统计。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对网站或游戏的体验反馈，包括用户界面、功能建议以及技术实现等方面。

不同观点：
• **关于弹窗订阅**：
  - [nimih] 认为弹窗频率过高，令人反感，甚至影响回访意愿。
  - [skwee357] 也建议移除弹窗，认为其影响用户体验。
  - [roskelld] 理解弹窗的营销目的，但同样觉得弹窗令人反感，建议使用不那么侵入性的方式。
  - [CleverLikeAnOx] 直接称弹窗为“预先的劣化设计”（enshittification），要求移除。

• **关于输入体验**：
  - [nimih] 指出移动端自定义键盘表现不佳，存在卡顿、掉帧、不支持滑动输入等问题，尤其对有可访问性需求的用户不友好。
  - [skwee357] 也提到输入框非原生元素，导致其使用的Vimium插件拦截了输入。

• **关于答案匹配和提示**：
  - [jimmar] 认为答案匹配不够精确，例如输入“meat”时，匹配到“chicken”和“ham”是不合理的，建议对不明确的答案标记为错误。
  - [hatthew] 建议列出错误猜测，以防用户因输入错误或忘记之前猜测而困惑。

• **关于游戏设计与难度**：
  - [oliwary] 认为游戏具有挑战性，但设计合理，适合作为每日挑战游戏，同时提到玩家填写的调查问卷很有创意。
  - [nextts] 认为游戏类似于80年代的电视节目《Family Fortunes》，具有怀旧感。

• **关于技术实现与AI使用**：
  - [madarco] 分享了自己开发的类似游戏，提供了iOS和Android的下载链接。
  - [ks2408] 对游戏中的AI和技术实现表示好奇，询问哪些部分由AI生成，哪些由开发者控制，并询问开发者背景。
  - [davidbek] 对游戏中玩家答案与答案板的匹配机制表示好奇，询问其实现方式。

补充讨论：
- 评论中多次提到弹窗对用户体验的负面影响，表明这是用户普遍关注的问题。
- 输入体验和键盘问题也是移动端用户的一个主要关注点，尤其是对可访问性需求的关注。
- 部分用户对游戏的挑战性和设计给予了积极评价，但也有用户对答案匹配的准确性提出了质疑。
- 技术实现和AI的使用引起了部分用户的兴趣，表明用户对游戏背后的技术细节有一定的好奇心。

data.title: AI bots are destroying Open Access
data.author: dhacks
data.article_summary:
文章描述了互联网上正在发生的一场“战争”：AI公司为了训练大型语言模型（LLM），疯狂抓取网络上的高质量数据，目标包括图书馆、档案馆、非营利组织和学术出版商等提供优质信息的网站。这些机构正面临AI公司激进、贪婪且欺骗性的数据抓取行为，尤其是通过无休止的机器人（bots）活动。

过去，传统机器人较为礼貌，遵循网站的规则，但如今的AI机器人无视限制，耗尽服务器资源，给管理和维护这些信息资源的技术人员带来巨大压力。图书馆技术人员正在竭力防御，分享封锁名单和机器人特征，甚至通过屏蔽整个国家的IP或使用第三方服务如Cloudflare来缓解攻击，但效果有限。

这场冲突尤其影响了开放获取（Open Access）网站，例如MIT Press和OAPEN等学术资源平台，因机器人攻击导致服务中断，威胁到公共知识的保存。文章呼吁关注这一问题，以免大量有价值的书籍和信息因AI公司的数据需求而丢失。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：应对网络爬虫和AI生成内容（“AI” bots）引发的问题及解决方案

不同观点：
• [kazinator] 认为过去的爬虫很少造成问题，因为它们遵守robot exclusions和"nofollow"警告。然而，他认为这种说法已经过时，过去二十年里很少有爬虫真正遵守robots.txt。此外，nofollow并不是反爬虫的工具，而是用于告知搜索引擎不对链接内容进行排名提升。

• [pickledoyster] 提出通过法律和网络安全行动（如大量封锁IP、将SDK标记为恶意软件）来打击租用僵尸网络的爬虫活动，并建议从应用商店中清除这些SDK。

• [kragen] 建议使用BitTorrent来解决问题，认为开放获取许可和BitTorrent的对等策略能有效限制自私行为者的危害，并增强对虚假信息和链接失效的抵抗力。他还批评了监控资本主义，主张从监控资本主义手中夺回合法的互联网。

• [xnx] 质疑为何“AI”爬虫引起了如此多的关注，是因为数量庞大，还是因为AI公司各自编写自己的（不良）爬虫程序而不是使用现有的？

• [skeledrew] 认为当前的混乱是迈向语义网的必经之路，主张通过开放数据来民主化AI模型的训练，避免只有少数大公司掌握数据和结果。同时，预测未来大多数查询将通过类似Perplexity的工具进行过滤，因此设置障碍的网站将失去流量。

• [zzo38computer] 提到其HTTP服务器因LLM爬虫的不良行为而受到影响，这些爬虫发出大量无意义的请求，可能导致服务器过载。问题在于这些爬虫的糟糕表现，而非所有爬虫。

43474196.article_content:
There's a war going on on the Internet. AI companies with billions to burn are hard at work destroying the websites of libraries, archives, non-profit organizations, and scholarly publishers, anyone who is working to make quality information universally available on the internet. And the technologists defending against this broad-based attack are doing everything they can to preserve their outlets while trying to remain true to the mission of providing the digital lifeblood of science and culture to the world.
Yes, many of these beloved institutions are under financial pressures in the current political environment, but politics swings back and forth. The AI armies are only growing more aggressive, more rapacious, more deceitful and ever more numerous.
I'm talking about the voracious hunger of AI companies for good data to train Large Language Models (LLMs). These are the trillion-parameter sets of statistical weights that power things like Claude, ChatGPT and hundreds of systems you've never heard of. Good training data has lots of text, lots of metadata, is reliable and unbiased. It's unsullied by Search Engine Optimization (SEO) practitioners. It doesn't constantly interrupt the narrative flow to try to get you to buy stuff. It's multilingual, subject specific, and written by experts. In other words, it's like a library.
At last week's
Code4lib conference
hosted by Princeton University Library, technologists from across the library world gathered to share information about library systems, how to make them better, how to manage them, and how to keep them running. The hot topic, the thing everyone wanted to talk about, was how to deal with bots from the dark side.
Bots on the internet are nothing new, but a sea change has occurred over the past year. For the past 25 years, anyone running a web server knew that the bulk of traffic was one sort of bot or another. There was googlebot, which was quite polite, and everyone learned to feed it - otherwise no one would ever find the delicious treats we were trying to give away. There were lots of search engine crawlers working to develop this or that service. You'd get "script kiddies" trying thousands of prepackaged exploits. A server secured and patched by a reasonably competent technologist would have no difficulty ignoring these.
The old style bots were rarely a problem. They respected robot exclusions and "nofollow" warnings. The warning helped bots avoid volatile resources and infinite parameter spaces. Even when they ignored exclusions they seemed to be careful about it. They declared their identity in "user-agent" headers. They limited the request rate and number of simultaneous requests to any particular server. Occasionally there would be a malicious bot like a
card-tester
or a
registration spammer
. You'd often have to block these based on IP address. It was part of the landscape, not the dominant feature.
The current generation of bots is mindless. They use as many connections as you have room for. If you add capacity, they just ramp up their requests. They use randomly generated user-agent strings. They come from large blocks of IP addresses. They get trapped in endless hallways. I observed one bot asking for 200,000 nofollow redirect links pointing at Onedrive, Google Drive and Dropbox. (which of course didn't work, but Onedrive decided to stop serving our Canadian human users). They use up server resources - one speaker at Code4lib described a bug where software they were running was using 32 bit integers for session identifiers, and it ran out!
The good guys are trying their best. They're sharing block lists and bot signatures. Many libraries are routinely blocking entire countries (nobody in china could possibly want books!) just to be able to serve a trickle of local requests. They are using commercial services such as Cloudflare to outsource their bot-blocking and captchas, without knowing for sure what these services are blocking, how they're doing it, or whether user privacy and accessibility is being flushed down the toilet. But nothing seems to offer anything but temporary relief. Not that there's anything bad about temporary relief, but we know the bots just intensify their attack on other content stores.
The view of MIT Press's Open-Access site from the Wayback Machine.
The surge of AI bots has hit Open Access sites particularly hard, as their mission conflicts with the need to block bots. Consider that Internet Archive can no longer save snapshots of one of the best open-access publishers, MIT Press
because of cloudflare blocking
. (see above) Who know how many books will be lost this way?  Or consider that the
bots took down OAPEN
, the worlds most important repository of Scholarly OA books, for a day or two. That's 34,000 books that AI "checked out" for two days. Or recent outages at
Project Gutenberg
, which serves 2 million dynamic pages and a half million downloads per day. That's hundreds of thousands of downloads blocked! The link
43474196.article_summary:
文章描述了互联网上正在发生的一场“战争”：AI公司为了训练大型语言模型（LLM），疯狂抓取网络上的高质量数据，目标包括图书馆、档案馆、非营利组织和学术出版商等提供优质信息的网站。这些机构正面临AI公司激进、贪婪且欺骗性的数据抓取行为，尤其是通过无休止的机器人（bots）活动。

过去，传统机器人较为礼貌，遵循网站的规则，但如今的AI机器人无视限制，耗尽服务器资源，给管理和维护这些信息资源的技术人员带来巨大压力。图书馆技术人员正在竭力防御，分享封锁名单和机器人特征，甚至通过屏蔽整个国家的IP或使用第三方服务如Cloudflare来缓解攻击，但效果有限。

这场冲突尤其影响了开放获取（Open Access）网站，例如MIT Press和OAPEN等学术资源平台，因机器人攻击导致服务中断，威胁到公共知识的保存。文章呼吁关注这一问题，以免大量有价值的书籍和信息因AI公司的数据需求而丢失。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：航空业未来飞机设计及其技术可行性与乘客体验

不同观点：
• [icegreentea2] 认为这篇文章提到的开放式风扇（propfan/open rotor）设计并非新概念，与空客过去几年的声明没有重大区别。他指出，这种设计需要将发动机安装在后机身或采用高翼位（肩部安装或鸥翼形）。他还提到波音的下一代技术似乎集中在桁架支撑翼设计上，这也可能需要肩部安装的翅膀，并质疑这两种设计特征是否能良好结合。

• [I_dream_of_Geni] 对所谓的“新技术”持怀疑态度，指出这种“新技术”实际上至少有45年的历史。他提到自己曾参与过7J7项目（UDF-无导管风扇概念），并附上维基百科链接，认为业界只是在重新探讨过去的设计理念。

• [redrove] 从乘客体验的角度出发，批评A320系列飞机的舒适性，尤其是低成本航空公司广泛使用该机型。他指出A320的拥挤、登机时间长、卫生间条件差等问题，并表示希望更多机场支持宽体飞机或使用像Embraer E190这样的小型飞机。

补充讨论：
• 关于飞机设计的技术讨论集中在开放式风扇与桁架支撑翼设计的可行性及其相互作用，显示出业内人士对未来飞机设计方向的不同看法。
• 乘客体验的观点则反映了普通乘客对不同机型实际乘坐体验的关注，特别是在经济舱和商务舱中的实际感受差异。
• 争议焦点在于新技术的“新”是否名副其实，以及这些技术是否能真正改善航空旅行的效率和乘客舒适度。

data.article_summary: 23andMe正在申请破产，引发了对其用户数据安全的担忧。如果公司被出售，用户的基因数据可能被转移至其他公司。为保护隐私，用户可以自行删除账户数据。具体步骤包括：登录账户，进入“设置”页面，选择“23andMe数据”并点击“查看”，经过年龄验证后，选择下载数据或请求删除账户。删除过程不可逆，但部分数据如基因信息、出生日期等会因法律要求被保留。若之前选择保留基因样本，删除账户时样本也会被销毁。用户在科学研究中的数据仍会保留，但不会用于未来研究。如遇问题，可联系customercare@23andme.com。有些用户建议在删除前篡改个人信息以保护隐私，但效果不明。

News
How to delete your 23andMe data
﻿You can permanently remove your account from the troubled company’s database.
﻿You can permanently remove your account from the troubled company’s database.
by
Jess Weatherbed
Updated
Mar 24, 2025, 4:48 PM UTC
Link
Facebook
Threads
If you buy something from a Verge link, Vox Media may earn a commission.
See our ethics statement.
Image: The Verge
Jess Weatherbed
is a news writer focused on creative industries, computing, and internet culture. Jess started her career at TechRadar, covering news and hardware reviews.
23andMe has
filed for bankruptcy
, raising concerns about what will happen to the DNA-testing company and all the data it’s collected from customers over the years. In the event that 23andMe is sold, its massive genetic database may end up in the hands of a different company entirely — one that users never consented to handing their personal information over to.
If you’ve submitted your DNA to the company via its saliva-testing kits, 23andMe will typically have your genetic, ancestry, and family connections data on file, alongside any personal information that was used to create your account, including your name, address, email address, and payment information. Thankfully, the company will continue its regular operations while going through the Chapter 11 process, allowing users to access and at least partially delete their information for now.
23andMe says that
genetic data is anonymized
and stored separately from personally identifiable information such as names, addresses, and payment information. Anonymization has been known to fail in other situations, however, so here’s how you can proactively remove as much of your data as possible if you’d rather not take any chances. The process is the same across both mobile and desktop platforms.
How to remove your data from 23andMe
Log into 23andMe and select the “Settings” option under your account profile. Scroll down to the section titled “23andMe Data” and click “View.”
You’ll find this section at the bottom of the settings page.
Image: 23andMe / The Verge
You will now be asked to verify your age for security purposes. Once that’s been submitted, the next screen will provide options that will allow you to download your data, alongside a button to request the deletion of your 23andMe account.
The age verification request should appear on both mobile and desktop versions of the platform.
Image: 23andMe /
The Verge
You will then receive an email from 23andMe asking you to confirm the account deletion request.
Deleting your 23andMe account is irreversible, and you’ll permanently lose access to it once completed. If there are multiple profiles created by other users on your account then those will also be wiped unless you
transfer them to an account
that isn’t being deleted.
One of the notable issues is that this process also won’t delete
all
of your data — according to
23andMe’s privacy disclosure
, your genetic information, date of birth, and sex will be retained for an undisclosed amount of time to comply with the company’s legal obligations, alongside “limited information related to your account,” such as your email address and communications around your data deletion request.
23andMe did not answer our questions regarding what specific data actually
is
retained or deleted when a user removes their account. Some posts have appeared online that
encourage 23andMe users to scramble their data
before deletion by replacing things like name, date of birth, ethnicity, sex marker, and height with false equivalents. This will supposedly render any information that
is
retained useless, but will likely be ineffective if 23andMe only stores the data that was used to create your account — something that the company also did not clarify to
The Verge
.
As part of the account deletion process, 23andMe will destroy the genetic sample you submitted if you previously opted for it to remain in storage. Your 23andMe data will still exist in any scientific studies you consented to, but won’t be used in any future research projects. 23andMe directs customers who run into issues with the account deletion process to contact
customercare@23andme.com
for further assistance.

data.title: Lost manuscript of Merlin and King Arthur hidden inside another book
data.author: rolph
data.article_summary: 研究人员在剑桥大学图书馆发现了一份隐藏在16世纪地契登记册封皮内的中古手稿碎片，该碎片是失传已久的《梅林通俗故事》的一部分，已有700年历史。这份手稿讲述了梅林和亚瑟王早期统治的故事，其中梅林化身为盲人竖琴师，后来消失在空中，又以秃顶小孩的形象出现，并向未穿内衣的亚瑟王发布命令。梅林具有变形能力，其力量源于其母亲被魔鬼 impregnation的传说。手稿还提到梅林在战场上为亚瑟王携带旗帜，并带来了一条会喷火的龙作为秘密武器。由于采用了尖端技术，研究人员无需拆解封皮即可数字化还原并阅读这份脆弱的手稿。该发现揭示了亚瑟王传说中的一个重要续集，并提供了有关中古法语文学的重要见解。

43474692.article_content:
Lost manuscript of Merlin and King Arthur legend read for the first time after centuries hidden inside another book
11 hours ago
Share
Save
Donna Ferguson
Share
Save
Cambridge University Library
(Credit: Cambridge University Library)
An intriguing sequel to the tale of Merlin has sat unseen within the bindings of an Elizabethan deeds register for nearly 400 years. Researchers have finally been able to reveal it with cutting-edge techniques.
It is the only surviving fragment of a lost medieval manuscript telling the tale of Merlin and the early heroic years of King Arthur's court.
In it, the magician becomes a blind harpist who later vanishes into thin air. He will then reappear as a balding child who issues edicts to King Arthur wearing no underwear.
The shape-shifting Merlin – whose powers apparently stem from being the son of a woman impregnated by the devil – asks to bear Arthur's standard (a flag bearing his coat of arms) on the battlefield. The king agrees – a good decision it turns out – for Merlin is destined to turn up with a handy secret weapon: a magic, fire-breathing dragon.
For over 400 years, this fragile remnant of a celebrated medieval story lay undisturbed and unnoticed, repurposed as a book cover by Elizabethans to help protect an archival register of property deeds.
Now, the 700-year-old fragment of Suite Vulgate du Merlin – an Old French manuscript so rare there are less than 40 surviving copies in the world – has been discovered by an archivist in
Cambridge University Library
, folded and stitched into the binding of the 16th-Century register.
Using groundbreaking new technology, researchers at the library were able to digitally capture the most inaccessible parts of the fragile parchment without unfolding or unstitching it. This preserved the manuscript in situ and avoided irreparable damage – while simultaneously allowing the heavily faded fragment to be virtually unfolded, digitally enhanced and read for the first time in centuries.
Previously, it was catalogued as the story of Gawain. "It wasn't properly inventoried," says Irene Fabry-Tehranchi, the French specialist at the library. "No one had even recorded that it was in French."
Cambridge University Library
The ancient text was found stitched into the binding of a manuscript from the 16th Century (Credit: Cambridge University Library)
When she and her colleagues realised the fragment told a story about Merlin and his ability to change shape "we were really excited," she says.
The Suite Vulgate du Merlin was originally written around 1230, a time when Arthurian romances were particularly popular among noblewomen, although the fragment is from a lost copy dated to around 1300. "We don't know who wrote the text," says Fabry-Tehranchi. "We think it was probably a collaborative exercise."
It is positioned as a sequel to an earlier text, written around 1200, in which Merlin is born a child prodigy gifted with foresight and casts a spell to facilitate the birth of King Arthur, who proves his divine right to rule by pulling the sword from the stone.
"The Suite Vulgate du Merlin tells us about Arthur's early reign, his relationship with the knights of the round table and his heroic fight with the Saxons. It really shows Arthur in a positive light – he's this young hero who marries Guinevere, invents the Round Table and has a good relationship with Merlin, his advisor," says Fabry-Tehranchi.
Stylistic evidence in the text indicates the fragment was written by an unknown scribe in a northern French dialect understood by English aristocrats
It is thanks to the sequel, she says, that the story of the Holy Grail – and Merlin's place in that story – could be retold in a coherent way from beginning to end. "If the sequel was written to facilitate that, it was successful. That became the main way the story was transmitted."
Stylistic evidence in the text indicates the fragment was written by an unknown scribe in a northern French dialect understood by English aristocrats. "These are Celtic and English legends, which had circulated orally across the British Isles. But the language used when they are written down is Old French, because of the Norman Conquest."
By the 16th Century, however, Old French had fallen out of favour in England. "There was a linguistic shift to English among readers of Arthurian literature," says Fabry-Tehranchi. This may be why the fragment ended up as the book binding of an archival register: "The text had lost its appeal, so they wanted to reuse it."
Cambridge University Library
The new technology available has allowed scholars like Błażej Mikuła and Amélie Deblauwe to investigate manuscripts without damaging them (Credit: Cambridge University Library)
The library wanted to preserve the register, which was created in 1580 to record the property of Huntingfield Manor in Suffolk, as evidence of 16th-Century archival binding practices in England.

data.title: Bulletproof Sessions: Secure Session Handling Without Cookies
data.author: thunderbong
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了一种新的会话处理机制——“bulletproof sessions”，通过使用服务工作者（service worker）拦截并加密签署所有发往源服务器的请求，以增强安全性。与传统的基于会话ID、Cookie或JWT的机制不同，该方法的请求信息是动态的，无法被攻击者重放或伪造。

**主要优势**包括：
1. **防重放攻击**：每个请求包含唯一元素（如时间戳或随机数），服务器验证后拒绝重放请求。
2. **XSS防护**：私钥存储在服务工作者的隔离环境中，难以通过恶意脚本直接访问。
3. **CSRF防护**：通过包含请求特定数据，服务器自动拒绝无效或重放的请求。
4. **跨域灵活性**：签名添加在请求头中，便于跨域请求处理。

这种机制提高了安全性，特别是在防范重放攻击、CSRF和XSS方面，同时提供了跨域请求的灵活性。

主要讨论点：移动设备上每次请求都需要签名是否会影响电池寿命

不同观点：
• 观点一：签名每个请求可能会影响移动设备的电池寿命。([paulryanrogers])
  - 论据：每次请求都需要进行加密签名操作，可能会增加设备处理器的负担，从而消耗更多电量，最终影响电池寿命。

• 观点二：影响可能微乎其微，因为现代设备已经为加密操作进行了优化。
  - 论据：现代移动设备的硬件和操作系统已经对加密操作进行了高度优化，单独的请求签名不太可能显著影响电池寿命。
  - 例子：许多现有的加密通信协议（如HTTPS）已经在广泛使用，并没有明显影响设备的电池表现。

• 观点三：签名频率和具体实现方式可能是关键因素。
  - 论据：如果签名操作过于频繁，或者实现方式不够高效，可能会导致电量消耗问题。因此，优化签名实现和控制签名频率是减少电池影响的关键。
  - 例子：某些应用可能在后台频繁发送请求，导致签名操作频繁执行，进而加剧电量消耗。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于请求签名对电池寿命的影响程度，特别是硬件优化和具体实现方式的不同可能导致不同的结果。
• 一些讨论者提到，优化算法的选择和减少不必要的请求同样可以缓解电池消耗问题。
• 还有人提到，相比电池寿命，安全性可能更为重要，因此即便有轻微影响，请求签名也值得实施。

43473659.article_content:
As if there weren't enough session handling mechanisms (session id's in each URL, cookies, http only cookies, JWT tokens in the request header), let me introduce you a novel one:
having a service worker that intercepts and cryptographically signs all the requests to the origin
.
With the traditional session handling mechanisms, we have a static piece of information, usually generated on the server, which gets sent back to the server with each request.
With the bulletproof sessions concept,
the information sent back to the server is dynamic and can not be replayed or faked by an attacker
.
Here's a sequence diagram of how it works
Per-request signing provides significant benefits over cookie-based session handling, including stronger security (CSRF protection, request integrity, and non-repudiation), greater flexibility across domains, support for decentralized identity, and fine-grained access control, among others.
Here's the public repo of a proof of concept I built in nodejs for the
bulletproof sessions idea
.
The bulletproof sessions concept offers the possibility to create some very innovative applications, has the potential to simplify the whole authentication with 3rd parties space, all while offering an increase level of security for these applications.
1. Security Benefits
Session Replay attacks
Cookie-Based Sessions
Vulnerability
: Cookies are sent automatically with every request to the origin. If an attacker intercepts a session cookie (e.g., via a man-in-the-middle attack on an insecure connection), they can replay it to impersonate the user.
Danger Level
: High without mitigations. Even with HTTPS, a stolen cookie from a compromised client (e.g., via XSS or malware) can be reused until it expires or is invalidated server-side.
Mitigations
: Short-lived cookies,
Secure
and
HttpOnly
flags, and CSRF tokens reduce (but don’t eliminate) the risk.
Token-Based Sessions (e.g., JWT)
Vulnerability
: Tokens stored in
localStorage
or sent in headers can be intercepted (e.g., via XSS or network sniffing if not over HTTPS). If the token has a long expiry, it’s replayable until it’s revoked or expires.
Danger Level
: High if tokens are long-lived or not properly secured. Revocation requires server-side blacklisting, which isn’t always implemented.
Mitigations
: Short expiration times, refresh tokens, and HTTPS help, but stolen tokens remain usable until expiry.
Bulletproof sessions
:
Per-request signing with asymmetric cryptography (as discussed earlier) can significantly reduce the danger of replay attacks, offering a key advantage over cookies and tokens:
Request-Specific Data
: Each request can include a unique element—like a timestamp, nonce, or request payload—in the signed data. The server checks this, rejecting any request that reuses an old signature.
Server verifies the signature and ensures the timestamp is recent (e.g., within 5 seconds). A replayed request with an old timestamp fails.
Danger Level
: Very low. Replay attacks become impractical because each signature is single-use and time-bound.
XSS (Cross-Site Scripting) Protection
Cookies
: When set with the
HttpOnly
flag, cookies are inaccessible to JavaScript, reducing the risk of theft via XSS. However, an attacker can still make requests on behalf of the user if they hijack the page.
Tokens
: Tokens stored in
localStorage
or
sessionStorage
are vulnerable to XSS because malicious scripts can access and steal them.
Bulletproof sessions
: The private key is stored in the service worker’s isolated context or IndexedDB, making it harder for malicious scripts to access directly. However, if an attacker can interact with the service worker (e.g., via
postMessage
), they might trick it into signing malicious requests. While this offers a slight edge over tokens in
localStorage
, it’s not completely immune to XSS.
CSRF (Cross-Site Request Forgery) Protection
Cookies
: Vulnerable to CSRF unless mitigated with additional measures like CSRF tokens, as cookies are sent automatically with requests.
Tokens
: Generally less vulnerable because tokens aren’t sent automatically like cookies. However, if a system auto-attaches tokens to requests, CSRF risks could return.
Bulletproof sessions
: If the signature includes request-specific data (e.g., a timestamp, nonce, or request body), the server can reject invalid or replayed signatures. This provides inherent CSRF protection, which is a clear advantage over traditional cookies.
CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) Flexibility
Cookies
: Tricky for cross-origin requests. They require specific CORS headers (
Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
) and are often restricted, making cross-origin use cumbersome.
Tokens
: Easier to manage with CORS, as tokens can be included in headers and controlled precisely.
Bulletproof sessions
: Like token-based methods, the signature is added to a header, offering flexibility for cross-origin requests. The service worker can decide which requests to sign, potentially simplifyin

data.title: Triforce – a beamformer for Apple Silicon laptops
data.author: tosh
data.article_summary: Triforce 是一个为 Apple Silicon 笔记本（如 MacBook Pro 和 MacBook Air 的 M1/M2 系列）麦克风阵列设计的自适应波束成形器。它基于最小方差无失真响应（MVDR）算法，旨在通过用户空间实现信号与背景噪声的分离，解决麦克风阵列过于敏感和全向性的问题。该项目依赖少量外部库，如 LV2，并使用 Rust 编写。由于缺乏 SIMD 优化和宽带分解能力，当前版本在性能和效率上有限，输出为单声道，且无法实时处理立体声。项目代码基于 GPL-2.0 许可发布，并欢迎改进补丁。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：

Triforce - a beamformer for Apple Silicon laptops
Triforce implements a Minimum Variance Distortionless Response adaptive beamformer
for the microphone array found in the following Apple Silicon laptops:
MacBook Pro 13" (M1/M2)
MacBook Air 13" (M1/M2)
MacBook Pro 14" (M1 Pro/Max, M2 Pro/Max)
MacBook Pro 16" (M1 Pro/Max, M2 Pro/Max)
MacBook Air 15" (M2)
Dependencies
Triforce tries to keep dependencies to a minimum. On top of the
crates specified in Cargo.lock, you will only require:
LV2
Why?
The Apple Silicon laptops mentioned above have an array of microphones arranged
either in a triangle or in a straight line. Much like with the speakers, Apple are trying way too hard to be
fancy here, and implement an adaptive beamformer in userspace to try and isolate
the desired signal from background noise. Without beamforming, the array is far
too sensitive and omnidirectional to be at all useful. Thus, to make it useful outside
of macOS, we need a beamformer.
Expectation management
Finding accessible literature on any DSP-related topics, let alone something like
wideband adaptive beamforming, is challenging to say the least. This is an attempt
at a beamformer armed only with first year undergrad level engineering maths and some vague
idea of the principles gleaned from various webpages and PDFs. Do not expect it to
outperform Apple's implementation at this time. Patches to improve it are always welcome!
Known limitations
nalgebra does not do any explicit SIMD optimisation, relying only on LLVM auto-vectorisation.
Performance and efficiency of matrix math routines are not very good.
Following from that, we are not doing wideband decomposition due to the added computational
burden. Without SIMD/NEON support, this is simply too slow for a realtime audio plugin.
Output is mono only. Much like with wideband decomposition, adding additional matrix processing
to fake stereo output would be too computationally intensive

43461701.article_summary: Triforce 是一个为 Apple Silicon 笔记本（如 MacBook Pro 和 MacBook Air 的 M1/M2 系列）麦克风阵列设计的自适应波束成形器。它基于最小方差无失真响应（MVDR）算法，旨在通过用户空间实现信号与背景噪声的分离，解决麦克风阵列过于敏感和全向性的问题。该项目依赖少量外部库，如 LV2，并使用 Rust 编写。由于缺乏 SIMD 优化和宽带分解能力，当前版本在性能和效率上有限，输出为单声道，且无法实时处理立体声。项目代码基于 GPL-2.0 许可发布，并欢迎改进补丁。

主要讨论点：围绕宗教组织（特别是基督复临安息日会）及其历史、伦理实践的讨论

不同观点：
• CalRobert认为，Whitecoat行动中的士兵志愿者是在知情并自愿的情况下参与实验的，且实验遵循了适当的伦理程序。他还提到自己曾参与基督复临安息日会的经历，认为该教会在医疗领域有贡献，但也存在一些保守的宗教观念，如年轻地球创造论。他同时表示怀念教会的社区感，并指出当时的教会对婚姻平等等问题持较为开放的态度。

• aredox指出，在同一历史时期，一些实验遵循了伦理程序，而另一些则没有，这反映出即使在当时，人们对于不道德的人体实验也存在反感和抵制。他将Whitecoat行动的伦理实践与其他不道德的实验进行了对比。

• mullingitover认为，基督复临安息日会已经从原本坚定的道德立场（如对堕胎和疫苗的开放态度）转变为与主流右翼福音派相似的立场。他通过自己的经历说明，早期的教会在堕胎等问题上持较为中立的态度，而如今的教会则更多受到社交媒体和极端观点的影响，变得更为保守和激进。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是基督复临安息日会的演变，特别是其在堕胎和疫苗等问题上的立场变化。mullingitover认为，教会已经从原本的“宗派”角色转变为“教派”，在道德立场上做出了妥协以适应主流社会，但如今却越来越接近右翼福音派的立场。

• CalRobert对教会的社区感和音乐传统表示怀念，并认为社会可以从安息日的文化实践中受益。他认为当时的教会对婚姻平等等问题持开放态度，而mullingitover则认为如今的教会已经发生了变化，不再具备这种开放性。

• aredox的评论强调了历史背景下的伦理实践，指出了同一时期不同实验在伦理上的差异，反映了当时社会对实验伦理的不同态度。

data.title: AI browser assistant extensions probably beaming everything to the cloud
data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: 一篇由多国研究人员撰写的预印本论文揭示，许多作为浏览器扩展的生成式AI助手存在隐私风险，可能会收集和传输用户的敏感数据，包括健康和学生信息，这可能违反美国法规如HIPAA和FERPA。研究分析了十款Chrome扩展，包括Sider、Monica和ChatGPT for Google，发现这些扩展通常将网页内容和用户输入发送至远程服务器，有时甚至共享给第三方追踪器。这些数据可用于定向广告或模型训练，进一步威胁用户隐私。与苹果的局部处理不同，这些扩展大多依赖服务器端API处理数据，增加了信息泄露的可能性。研究强调，用户需警惕这些扩展的数据处理行为。

Applications
15
You know that generative AI browser assistant extension is probably beaming everything to the cloud, right?
15
Just an FYI, like
Thomas Claburn
Tue 25 Mar 2025
//
08:31 UTC
Generative AI assistants packaged up as browser extensions harvest personal data with minimal safeguards, researchers warn.
Some of these extensions may violate their own privacy commitments and potentially run afoul of US regulations, such as
HIPAA
and
FERPA
, by collecting and funneling away health and student data.
A group of computer scientists from University of California, Davis in the USA, Mediterranea University of Reggio Calabria in Italy, University College London in the UK, and Universidad Carlos III de Madrid in Spain set out to analyze the privacy practices of browser extensions that use AI to do things like produce summaries of webpages or answer questions about content.
The academics – Yash Vekaria, Aurelio Loris Canino, Jonathan Levitsky, Alex Ciechonski, Patricia Callejo, Anna Maria Mandalari, and Zubair Shafiq – describe their findings in
this pre-print paper
, titled: "Big Help or Big Brother? Auditing Tracking, Profiling, and Personalization in Generative AI Assistants."
Using
network traffic analysis tools
, such as mitmproxy, the team studied ten generative AI Chrome Extensions: Sider, Monica, ChatGPT for Google, Merlin, MaxAI, Perplexity, HARPA, Wiseone, TinaMind, and Copilot.
Despite the use of familiar terms like ChatGPT, Google, and Copilot in the titles of these extensions, the makers of these extensions are unaffiliated with Google, Microsoft, or OpenAI.
What the academics found is not entirely surprising given the long history of privacy and security problems in the Chrome extension ecosystem. For one thing, this add-on software typically has the power to inspect and modify the pages you visit. In the case of these assistants, they send off your data, such as the webpage you're on, to remote AI services for processing and harvesting. If that page has anything sensitive on it, off it goes into the internet.
When you think about it, the risk seems obvious, but these academics have taken the time to document it so that one no longer has to make assumptions. Which is nice.
"In our study, we emphasize that not only do these assistants collect users' highly sensitive data," Yash Vekaria, a graduate student researcher at UC Davis and corresponding author of the report, told
The Register
Monday, "but that this information is also shared with their own servers as well as third-party trackers, which can be further utilized to target highly personalized and sensitive ads to the user.
"Our paper tries to emphasize that in the age of AI, the already poor privacy of Chrome extensions can be further exploited by generative AI assistants, which can use this information to profile users over time and then personalize their responses for the user – which could be highly sensitive. The data collected about the user could be used by these assistants to further train their models and may have inadvertent consequences."
Rather than using local in-browser models – a capability Apple has touted for its
not-fully-implemented
Apple Intelligence system – most of these (90 percent) third-party AI extensions rely on server-side APIs for processing. And according to the researchers, these APIs might be used by the add-on software without explicit user interaction.
By processing, we mean, you're on a page with the extension enabled, and you type a query into the add-on about the webpage, or you request a task such as summarization, and the data and request are fired off to a remote API, with the results shown in the extension. The issue here is: How much data is sent off, and could anything be done to limit the transfer of sensitive information?
"When invoked, these browser assistants collect and share webpage content, often the full HTML DOM [document object model] and sometimes even the user’s form inputs, with their first-party servers," the researchers state in their paper. "Some gen-AI browser assistants also share identifiers and user prompts with third-party trackers such as Google Analytics."
This information collection and sharing has been documented in some instances on webpages that contain sensitive health or personal information, such as the web forms used to submit medical data or social security numbers.
Vekaria said his group tested the extensions on a university health portal after authenticating with a personal account.
"We observed that full webpage content with HTML DOM (including the user's personally identifiable information, and sensitive health conditions, medical history, etc) was collected by Sider, Merlin, and Harpa; while other extensions (Monica, ChatGPT for Google, MaxAI, and Wiseone) collected textual data in plain text (ie, not HTML; but page text, page title, page URL)."

data.title: NSA warned of vulnerabilities in Signal app a month before Houthi strike chat
data.author: jasoncartwright
data.article_summary: 本文报道了美国国家安全局（NSA）在2025年2月向员工发出的安全警告，指出加密通讯应用Signal存在漏洞，可能被用于拦截敏感信息。这一警告是在《大西洋月刊》披露国防部长佩特·赫格斯意外通过Signal聊天向记者透露对也门胡塞武装的作战计划后发出的。赫格斯在美军行动前两小时，不小心在群聊中分享了有关武器、目标和时间的详细信息。尽管NSA提醒不要在Signal上分享任何非公开信息，但包括国家安全顾问迈克·沃尔兹在内的多名特朗普政府高官被指参与了该聊天。CIA局长和国家情报总监在国会作证时否认聊天中包含机密或敏感的行动细节。此事引发国会民主党人的强烈批评，并要求展开调查。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于Google上个月报告的攻击是否是NSA警告中所提及的攻击，以及是否应记录通过Signal进行的涉及消失消息的敏感对话。

不同观点：
• 第一个讨论点是确认该攻击是否为NSA警告中提到的攻击。一名用户引用Google的博客和NSA的完整文件链接，确认此攻击正是NSA警告中提到的那个。这表明用户关注具体事件和官方警告之间的关联性。

• 另一个讨论点是关于通过Signal进行对话时使用消失消息的功能。用户"anigbrowl"认为，虽然大家关注的是安全性，但更严重的问题是使用消失消息。该用户主张，尽管某些对话或会议记录可能需要保密，但绝对应该被记录下来，以保证透明度和问责性。

补充讨论：
• 一个值得注意的细节是，用户"anigbrowl"对Signal消失消息功能在敏感对话中使用的担忧，反映了对隐私工具在不同情境下应用效果的质疑。这种观点强调了在安全通信工具使用中，记录和透明度的重要性，尤其是在可能涉及公共利益或安全的事务中。

• 争议的焦点在于安全性和透明度之间的平衡。一方认为安全和隐私保护至上，另一方则认为在特定情况下，透明度和记录更为重要。这种对立可能引发对政策和工具使用的更广泛讨论。

43475624.article_content:
Latest on Yemen bombing group chat
Latest details on Trump officials' group chat with journalist about Yemen bombing
18:37
The National Security Agency sent out an operational security special bulletin to its employees in February 2025 warning them of vulnerabilities in using the encrypted messaging application Signal, according to internal NSA documents obtained by CBS News.
News of the NSA bulletin comes amid the continued fallout from an explosive
article
published Monday
in The Atlantic. The publication's editor-in-chief, Jeffrey Goldberg, detailed how Defense Secretary
Pete Hegseth
inadvertently disclosed war plans to him in an encrypted
Signal
chat group two hours before the U.S. military launched attacks against Houthi militia in Yemen. Goldberg wrote that Hegseth's messages included "precise information about weapons packages, targets, and timing."
The NSA is an arm of the Defense Department and specializes in signals intelligence — which is derived from electronic transmissions — and cybersecurity. The agency is responsible for monitoring, collecting and processing information and data for U.S. national security interests.
The unclassified but for-official-use-only
documents provided to CBS News
by a senior U.S. intelligence official are entitled "Signal Vulnerability" and were sent out the month before Goldberg was accidentally added to the
group chat
allegedly by national security adviser Mike Waltz.
"A vulnerability has been identified in the Signal Messenger Application. The use of Signal by common targets of surveillance and espionage activity has made the application a high value target to intercept sensitive information," the internal bulletin begins.
The bulletin warned of
Russian
professional hacking groups employing phishing scams to gain access to encrypted conversations, bypassing the end-to-end encryption the application uses.
The bulletin also underscored to NSA employees that third-party messaging applications such as
Signal
and Whatsapp are permitted for certain "unclassified accountability/recall exercises" but not for communicating more sensitive information.
NSA employees were also warned to not send "anything compromising over any social media or Internet-based tool or application," and to not "establish connections with people you do not know."
CBS News contacted the NSA for comment but did not receive a reply prior to publication.
On Tuesday, National Intelligence Director Tulsi Gabbard and CIA Director John Ratcliffe, both of whom were reportedly in the Signal group chat,
testified
before a Senate panel.
"There was no classified material that was shared in that Signal chat," Gabbard told lawmakers. But the NSA bulletin advises that even information that is not categorized as classified should not be shared on Signal, advising users not to share "unclassified, nonpublic" information on the messaging platform.
Ratcliffe said Signal "is a permissible use" application that has been approved by the White House for use by senior officials. The group chat, Ratcliffe said, was a "mechanism for communicating between senior level officials but not a substitute for using high side or classified communications."
Both Ratcliffe and Gabbard were asked by Democratic Sen. Martin Heinrich of New Mexico whether the Signal conversation included information on "weapons packages, targets or timing." Ratcliffe replied, "Not that I'm aware of," and Gabbard said, "Same answer and defer to the Department of Defense on that question." Both said they had no knowledge of the chat including operational details of the strike in Yemen.
Arden Farhi
contributed to this report.

data.title: Show HN: LinkedIn sucks, so I built a better one
data.author: fliellerjulian
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对职业社交平台（特别是与LinkedIn对比）的功能、设计和用户体验的看法

不同观点：
• **支持简化功能，专注于求职和招聘基本需求**：
  - DeathArrow认为平台应简单直接，只需提供基本的求职和招聘功能，如发布简历和标示求职状态，不需要额外的视频或复杂功能。
  - neilv反对在简历中加入照片，认为这可能导致歧视问题，并指出LinkedIn虽然流行，但也有很多缺点。
  - davedx也反对增加视频内容，认为这不会改善用户体验。

• **支持通过内容和网络效应提升个人品牌**：
  - janalsncm建议通过技术博客或项目展示来突出个人能力，而不是依赖照片或视频。
  - vector_spaces指出算法推荐和活跃用户展示有助于增加平台的社会证明效应，但也提到新用户上手时需要更明确的指引和互动机制。
  - adabyron建议建立有价值的小型讨论组，以促进深度交流，并认为应避免LinkedIn那样的社交feed带来的干扰。

• **对平台设计的不同期望**：
  - oytis质疑设计一个让所有人都“突出”的平台是否可行，认为这样只会增加用户的工作量，且对招聘方也不利。
  - smeej指出LinkedIn对那些职业路径不直线的人不友好，每次修改简历很麻烦。
  - 8mobile希望有一个更简洁的LinkedIn版本，而不是增加更多社交功能。

• **对视觉展示的争议**：
  - neilv和confooseddd都反对在简历或个人资料中过度强调照片和视觉元素，认为工作成果才是关键，平台应专注于客观的内容展示。
  - scosman建议从美观和易用的作品集入手，吸引用户创建和分享个人页面，而不是直接与LinkedIn竞争网络效应。

补充讨论：
• **用户网络与平台吸引力**：
  - iancmceachern指出平台的成功关键在于能否持续吸引新客户，而不仅仅是平台本身的功能。
  
• **其他反馈**：
  - runlaszlorun认为现有职业社交平台如LinkedIn不尽如人意，支持新平台的创建。
  - venusenvy47对URL的误读提供了一个轻松的评论，虽与核心讨论无关，但显示了用户对平台名称和品牌的敏感性。

争议焦点：平台是否应增加视觉和视频内容以帮助用户“突出”，还是应保持简洁、专注于文本和客观成果的展示。

data.title: Microsoft's many Outlooks are confusing users – including its own employees
data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: 微软的多种Outlook版本让用户感到困惑，甚至连公司员工也不例外。微软老兵Scott Hanselman幽默地建议了一些新变体，如Outlook (Zero Sugar)和Outlook (Caffeine Free)，以突出这一问题。目前，用户可能同时拥有新版Outlook和Outlook (Classic)，后者支持到2029年。尽管微软希望用户转向新版，但新版缺少许多经典版的功能，且不支持企业常用的COM插件。这种多个相似选项并存的情况可能导致用户混淆，并引发管理上的复杂性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对微软新旧Outlook及其相关产品的体验和争议

不同观点：
• **支持适应新Outlook的用户**：  
  - 用户[Alupis]提到，虽然新Outlook在界面和功能上有些令人困惑，且部分按钮和选项不够直观，但经过一段时间的适应后，逐渐习惯了这种变化。  
  - 尽管新界面需要重新学习，但这是软件升级的一部分，用户认为可以接受。

• **反对新Outlook的用户**：  
  - 用户[focusedone]强烈批评新Outlook的附件处理方式，尤其是只能将文件保存到OneDrive，而不能选择任意本地位置，严重影响了工作效率。  
  - 用户[mrweasel]表示不理解微软为何不直接提供经典Outlook版本，反而强制推广一个“劣化”的版本，尤其在用户已经为“好版本”付费的情况下。  
  - 用户[deelowe]认为Outlook在处理基本任务时（如搜索、会议安排等）非常混乱，相比Google Workspace，Outlook显得非常糟糕。

• **对微软整体产品策略的批评**：  
  - 用户[transcriptase]对比苹果公司，指出微软缺乏对用户体验的把控，认为微软内部缺乏能够抵制愚蠢和混乱设计决策的人。  
  - 用户[yuters]对微软365（现称为Microsoft 365）的多个版本和命名感到困惑，认为整个产品线极其混乱。

• **技术性问题与漏洞**：  
  - 用户[Kwpolska]提到新Outlook的加载问题，认为一个桌面邮件客户端不应该需要互联网连接才能显示最近的邮件。  
  - 用户[EarthIsHome]指出Outlook通知功能的一个长期未修复的漏洞，即点击通知后邮件会在其他窗口后面打开。

• **对微软生态系统的复杂性感到不满**：  
  - 用户[xg15]提到，任何使用微软账户登录的第三方产品都需要通过多个微软自有域名进行交互，这种复杂的架构让用户体验非常混乱。

• **对经典产品的怀念与其他工具的推荐**：  
  - 用户[vincent-manis]提到自己使用Thunderbird，感觉错过了Outlook发展中的关键历史。  
  - 用户[CrimsonCape]寻找类似于VoidTools 'Everything'的邮件应用，希望有一个专注于速度和功能的邮件客户端，而不是过于注重UI设计。

补充讨论：
- 用户对微软产品命名和版本管理的困惑，如Teams和.NET的命名问题，进一步加剧了对微软整体产品策略的不满。  
- 部分用户提到经典Outlook的功能强大，特别是MAPI编程接口的灵活性，对新版Outlook的“简化”和功能削弱表示不满。

43474707.article_content:
Applications
40
Microsoft's many Outlooks are confusing users – including its own employees
40
Redmond veteran proposes Zero Sugar and Caffeine Free variants
Richard Speed
Tue 25 Mar 2025
//
13:15 UTC
Baffled by the plethora of Outlook options out there? You aren't alone. Microsoft veteran Scott Hanselman posted a list of some more variants that could be used to do the same thing.
It's a problem common to several Microsoft products. A file needs to be opened, but which app should be used? Should it be Outlook New, or Outlook (New)? With tongue firmly in cheek, Hanselman listed some more options: Outlook (Zero Sugar), Outlook (Caffeine Free), and so on.
Hanselman, Developer Community veep at Microsoft, also included Outlook '95, although to our mind the peak came with the version of Outlook in Office 97. A happier, more trusting time when security was less important.
While users can create multiple
Outlook profiles
to store email account details and data locations, Hanselman's
post
on Bluesky highlights an issue facing many users of Microsoft's software: which incarnation of the application to use.
Teams users often find themselves presented with a variety of applications – Microsoft Teams and Microsoft Teams (Personal), for example, can often appear side by side in the system tray.
As for Outlook, users are likely to have multiple versions installed. Microsoft
forced the new version onto devices as part of a Windows update
and renamed the previous version to Outlook (Classic) so the pair could run side by side. While support for the Classic version of Outlook will persist until at least 2029, Microsoft would like users to move to the new version despite it lacking many of its predecessor's functions.
According
to Microsoft: "The new Outlook for Windows, built upon modern service architecture, is inspired by the Outlook web experience." It also does not support the COM add-ins used by many enterprises to glue corporate workflows together.
Oops, they did it again: Microsoft breaks Outlook with another dubious update
Even Windows 10 cannot escape the new Outlook
New Outlook marches onto Windows 10 for what little time it has left
Outlook is poor for those still on Windows Mail, Calendar, People apps by end of year
Currently, the new Outlook is at the opt-in stage and is off by default. It will then proceed to an opt-out stage, where users must actively switch back to the Classic experience before the Cutover stage, after which reversal is no longer possible. Microsoft says it will give administrators at least 12 months' notice before this is implemented in production rings.
Existing perpetual installations of classic Outlook "will continue to be supported until at least 2029,"
according
to Microsoft.
There is a cautionary tale about
what happened
when a soft drinks company tried to replace a well-liked product with a "new" version and renamed the previous preferred version as "classic."
The list posted by Hanselman – who is also
notable
for tips on managing Microsoft's personal information manager – is amusing, but also highlights the perils of having multiple, similarly functioning options to do the same thing, and the potential for confusing users.
Outlook (Stable and Fast) anyone? ®

To my great surprise, I just realised it's been more than two and a half years since I last wrote a journal post for this project! Very lax of me, and apologies to all for the lack of more regular updates.
The project has been surging along, and we now have more than 7,000 observations, which is fantastic to see. We also recently surpassed 2,000 project members, thanks in part to some regular mentions of the project in recent iNat blog posts (eg observation of the week).
So for all the newer members, I'll run through the project rules again:
1 . Any observations you add must be the first photograph(s) of that species anywhere. If an observation is the first one for that species to be uploaded to iNat, but other photos of that species from an earlier point in time already exist anywhere elsewhere online/in print, then that observation should not be added to the project. This is the biggest source of observations that I have to remove from the project. So your observation must be both the first photograph of that species on iNat and also the first anywhere.
If you encounter an observation of a species that is older than one already in the project, add it, but please message me so I can remove the one that no longer qualifies as oldest.
2 . Your photograph must be of a living individual. A number of observations have been added that depict things like empty mollusc shells, dead fishes, pinned insects, etc. Whilst these are of course valuable observations, they are not eligible for the project.
3 . If the male and female of a species are sexually dimorphic, then both are valid to be added to the project. So too if a species has distinct life stages (eg caterpillar/chrysalis/butterfly), they are all valid to be separately added to the project (assuming the other rules apply). Ditto for plants; if one observation shows the first ever photos of flowers, and another the first ever of fruits, they are both ok to add to the project. Please make sure, however, that the first two rules are also followed in these cases.
The project is very much self-sustaining now, with users adding observations to it every day, and there are a number of users in particular who have added many IDs and/or added records to the project, so huge thanks to everyone involved. I'd like to especially highlight the recent efforts of
@borisb
, who has contributed tremendously (IDing and adding) in the world of beetles and has been a very vocal advocate for the project, letting users know each time he adds one of their observations.

data.title: Optimizing ML training with metagradient descent
data.author: ladberg
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种基于元梯度下降（Metagradient Descent, MGD）的方法，用于优化大规模机器学习模型的训练过程。作者提出了一种高效计算元梯度的算法，并引入了一个"平滑模型训练"框架，使得利用元梯度进行有效优化成为可能。实验表明，MGD在数据集选择和抵御数据中毒攻击方面显著优于现有方法，并且能够自动找到具有竞争力的学习率调度策略。该方法为优化模型训练配置提供了新途径。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于机器学习中超参数优化问题的复杂性以及对相关数学优化理论的讨论。

不同观点：
• [munchler] 认为在实际的机器学习问题中，超参数优化非常复杂且困难。每个训练运行需要很长时间，超参数之间互相影响且对硬件非常敏感，微小的配置调整可能会导致极大的性能差异。这种情况下，没有对问题领域的深入理解很难有效地搜索超参数空间。

• [jn2clark] 提出了“学习如何学习”（learning to learn）的先前工作，并询问该文章为何没有引用相关研究（如论文 https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.04474）。这暗示可能存在已有文献中的方法可以用于解决当前讨论的超参数优化问题。

• [MITSardine] 对文章本身进行了深入的数学分析，指出形如 $f : x \to \text{argmin}_y g(x,y)$ 的函数通常不光滑，甚至可能不连续。此外，优化算法通常只能收敛到局部最小值，而非全局最小值。即使在数学上定义良好的情况下，数值计算中的浮点精度问题也会导致实际求解中的困难。MITSardine 还对文章中的符号和定义提出了质疑，认为文章在讨论如何正则化此类函数方面没有给出足够深入的解决方案，并提出了替代符号和定义的建议。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是超参数优化的实际复杂性以及是否已有其他研究（如“学习如何学习”）可以提供更好的解决方案。[munchler] 强调了实际操作中的难度，而 [jn2clark] 则指向了可能被忽视的相关研究。

• [MITSardine] 详细讨论了优化问题的数学性质，特别是函数 $f$ 的非光滑性和数值计算中的问题，并提出了对文章符号和定义的改进建议。这表明在实际应用中，理论上的优化问题比文章所讨论的更加复杂。

• 讨论中还涉及了具体的数学符号和技术细节问题，如 $\Delta_f$ 符号的使用以及定义中的技术选择，反映了在学术讨论中对精确性和符号一致性的关注。

总体而言，讨论围绕超参数优化的复杂性、已有研究的相关性以及数学优化中的理论问题展开，并包含了对文章具体内容的技术性建议。

Abstract:
A major challenge in training large-scale machine learning models is configuring the training process to maximize model performance, i.e., finding the best training setup from a vast design space. In this work, we unlock a gradient-based approach to this problem. We first introduce an algorithm for efficiently calculating metagradients -- gradients through model training -- at scale. We then introduce a "smooth model training" framework that enables effective optimization using metagradients. With metagradient descent (MGD), we greatly improve on existing dataset selection methods, outperform accuracy-degrading data poisoning attacks by an order of magnitude, and automatically find competitive learning rate schedules.

• [munchler] 认为在实际的机器学习问题中，超参数优化非常复杂且困难。每个训练运行需要很长时间，超参数之间互相影响且对硬件非常敏感，微小的配置调整可能会导致极大的性能差异。这种情况下，没有对问题领域的深入理解很难有效地搜索超参数空间。

• [jn2clark] 提出了“学习如何学习”（learning to learn）的先前工作，并询问该文章为何没有引用相关研究（如论文 https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.04474）。这暗示可能存在已有文献中的方法可以用于解决当前讨论的超参数优化问题。

• [MITSardine] 对文章本身进行了深入的数学分析，指出形如 $f : x \to \text{argmin}_y g(x,y)$ 的函数通常不光滑，甚至可能不连续。此外，优化算法通常只能收敛到局部最小值，而非全局最小值。即使在数学上定义良好的情况下，数值计算中的浮点精度问题也会导致实际求解中的困难。MITSardine 还对文章中的符号和定义提出了质疑，认为文章在讨论如何正则化此类函数方面没有给出足够深入的解决方案，并提出了替代符号和定义的建议。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是超参数优化的实际复杂性以及是否已有其他研究（如“学习如何学习”）可以提供更好的解决方案。[munchler] 强调了实际操作中的难度，而 [jn2clark] 则指向了可能被忽视的相关研究。

• [MITSardine] 详细讨论了优化问题的数学性质，特别是函数 $f$ 的非光滑性和数值计算中的问题，并提出了对文章符号和定义的改进建议。这表明在实际应用中，理论上的优化问题比文章所讨论的更加复杂。

• 讨论中还涉及了具体的数学符号和技术细节问题，如 $\Delta_f$ 符号的使用以及定义中的技术选择，反映了在学术讨论中对精确性和符号一致性的关注。

总体而言，讨论围绕超参数优化的复杂性、已有研究的相关性以及数学优化中的理论问题展开，并包含了对文章具体内容的技术性建议。

data.title: Ruby, Ractors, and lock-free data structures
data.author: ksec
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了在Ruby中实现并发数据结构的方法，目标是展示如何在全局可变状态下实现真正的并行处理（当前Ruby内置功能不支持）。文章涉及Ruby、Rust和C等语言，但并非必须精通。示例代码可在GitHub上找到，运行这些代码需要较新版本的Ruby（最好是可本地编译的主分支）、Rust和C编译器。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Ruby中的Ractor库的应用与挑战

不同观点：
• **Gibibit的观点**：Gibibit最初对Ractor的认知与Rust的Ractor库混淆了，他认为Rust的Ractor库非常优秀，特别是引入了Erlang/OTP的gen_server actors，值得Rust开发者关注。他对Ruby中的Ractor库文档进行了澄清。
• **Dpflan的观点**：Dpflan提到Mike Perham正在尝试利用Ractor构建可扩展的作业系统，并指出Ractor编程的难点，比如无法访问词法作用域或闭包变量，这使得Ractor编程变得复杂，甚至像是一种新的Ruby方言。他还将Ractor与Goroutines进行了类比，指出学习曲线可能类似。
• **T-writescode的观点**：T-writescode对Ractor是否真正遵循了actor模型提出疑问，尤其是邮件箱机制是否已经解决。他担心人们在使用Ractor时可能强迫actor模型遵循不合适的并行编程范式。同时，他对文章中过多提及Rust表示不解。
• **Kodablah的观点**：Kodablah提到他们的Ruby项目因使用Google Protobuf库而无法使用Ractor，因为该库不是Ractor安全的，并且无法要求用户不使用官方的Protobuf库。

补充讨论：
• **Rco8786的观点**：Rco8786认为，一个生产就绪的Ractor安全数据结构库将大大推动Ractor的采用，解决目前许多人遇到的主要障碍。

争议焦点：
• Ractor是否真正实现了actor模型，特别是邮件箱机制是否完善。
• Ractor编程的复杂性，特别是对词法作用域和闭包变量访问的限制，使得Ractor编程变得困难。
• 在Ruby项目中使用Ractor时，现有库（如Google Protobuf）的兼容性问题。

This story is about concurrent data structures in the context of Ruby. The goal here is to demonstrate how true parallelism can be achieved with global mutable state (which at the time of writing, is not supported by built-in Ruby primitives).
Familiarity with Ruby, Rust, C, (and a bit of other tooling) is nice to have, but hopefully not mandatory.
The repository with code examples can be found
on GitHub

data.title: Svelte: $derived can now be overwritten
data.author: jedeusus
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要介绍了Svelte项目中一个重要的代码合并（PR）：使派生值（derived values）变为可写。该合并由Rich-Harris在2025年3月21日完成，涉及将8个提交合并到主分支。文章详细说明了如何在提交PR前确保其合理性，包括引用相关问题、创建RFC以及进行测试和文档更新。此外，还提供了有关更改的文档预览和Playground链接。代码变更将在下一个版本中发布，类型为次要更新。讨论中有人担心使派生值可写可能会违背用户期望并影响优化，但也有开发者指出变量仍可设为只读，且派生值本质上具有可变性。最终，该PR被成功合并并关闭了相关问题。

data.title: Sell yourself, sell your work
data.author: ColinWright
data.article_summary: 文章强调，仅仅完成出色的工作并不足够，还需要主动宣传和分享，才能让世界受益并实现个人价值的最大化。作者指出，许多人虽然技术出色，但不愿意花时间撰写报告或分享成果，导致他们的工作无法被外界了解。因此，为了让他人知道并利用你的工作成果，必须克服对“宣传”的抵触心理，积极传播自己的成就。简而言之，做好工作后，还需要有效地“推销”自己和自己的工作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：是否应该公开和宣传自己的项目和作品，以及这样做是否是实现作品和个人价值的前提。

不同观点：
• **支持公开和宣传**：Simonw 认为，记录和分享项目非常重要，尤其是通过博客或GitHub，这样不仅能防止项目过时，还能让更多人受益。他还提到自己后悔没有记录早期项目。Gyello 也分享了自己通过为亲友创建项目并展示这些项目所获得的满足感，尽管这些项目没有公开发布。

• **反对强制公开**：Henchman21 和 Iaaan 持反对意见，认为不是所有作品都必须公开或商业化才能体现其价值。Iaaan 强调，人们有权选择是否分享自己的创作，而不应被外界压力左右。Henchman21 进一步指出，作品的价值不一定在于商业化，人类努力的价值超越金钱。

• **强调内在价值**：Sashank_1509 引用了Albert Jay Nock的《Isiah’s Job》一文，认为真正卓越的工作不需要通过宣传来体现其价值，时间会证明其意义。Bravetraveler 和 Ryandrake 也认为，可靠性和个人的内在满足感比宣传更为重要，做好工作自然会有人关注。

• **中立或实用主义**：Boznz 和 Stocknoob 持中立态度，认为宣传与否取决于个人喜好和需求。Boznz 提到自己不擅长营销，但意识到记录和分享项目可能带来机会。Stocknoob 建议年轻程序员专注于自己的兴趣，而不是自我宣传，除非他们喜欢这样做。

补充讨论：
• **个人品牌和商业化**：Webprofusion 和 Rednafi 提到公开项目和写作有助于建立个人品牌，可能会带来职业机会。然而，Rednafi 也警告不要过度销售，否则可能适得其反。

• **批判商业化压力**：Bjornsing 指出，人们往往忽视了从他人工作中筛选出有价值的部分，而不是被营销牵着走。Maxlin 则用比喻说明，人类生活的意义在于自我满足，而非对外展示。

争议焦点：作品的价值是否需要通过公开和商业化来体现，以及是否应由外界压力决定个人是否应该分享自己的创作。

Doing technically brilliant work may be enough for your
personal
gratification, but you should never think it's enough. If you lock
yourself in a room and do the most marvellous work but don't tell
anyone, then no one will know, no one will benefit, and the work
will be lost. You may have derived
personal satisfaction from it,
but as far as the wider world is concerned, you may as well not have
bothered. For the world to benefit from your work, and therefore for
you to benefit
fully
from your work, you have to make it known.
In short, you have to "advertise".
I've dealt with any number of technically brilliant people who produce
outstanding work. The majority of them never bothered to write down
their work and communicate it to others - report writing is too boring,
uninteresting, and hard. And irrelevant. Or so they thought.

data.title: Devs say AI crawlers dominate traffic, forcing blocks on entire countries
data.author: LinuxBender
data.article_summary:
软件开发者Xe Iaso遭遇亚马逊的AI爬虫流量攻击，导致其Git服务频繁不稳定和停机。尽管采取了多种防御措施，爬虫仍通过伪造用户代理和使用住宅IP代理绕过限制。Iaso最终创建了名为"Anubis"的系统，要求浏览器在访问前解决计算谜题，以此阻挡爬虫。然而，这种方法也给合法用户带来了延迟问题。

这一问题在开源社区广泛存在，许多项目的基础设施因AI爬虫而过载，导致服务不稳定和带宽成本上升。例如，Fedora Pagure项目不得不屏蔽巴西的所有流量，GNOME GitLab则采用了类似Anubis的系统，结果显示大部分请求是自动化的。

开源项目通常资源有限，面对AI爬虫的侵扰，维护者们感到负担沉重。例如，Inkscape项目的Martin Owens提到，他们的问题不仅来自传统的DDoS攻击，还包括一些公司无视规则、伪造浏览器信息。

社区对AI公司占用大量资源的行为感到不满，认为这些公司不尊重公共资源，且对受影响项目的诉求反应迟钝。

不同观点：
• **公司应采取更协作的方式进行数据抓取**：tedunangst认为，公司应该采取更协作的方式，比如限速数据抓取，以免压垮目标网站。如果目标网站在抓取后下线，那反而是“功能”。
• **机器人流量的快速攻击现象**：Nckpz分享了自己新项目在24小时内遭到大量垃圾表单提交攻击的经历，尽管没有对外宣传，但机器人迅速攻击了服务器。
• **激进的AI机器人对内容网站的影响**：ipaddr提到，由于激进的AI机器人，他们不得不关闭多个内容网站，这些机器人无视robots文件，导致服务器宕机。
• **特定AI机器人造成的DoS攻击**：rco8786描述了由Anthropic的ClaudeBot引发的DoS攻击，导致网站带宽超限，必须手动处理。

补充讨论：
• **反机器人措施的有效性与浏览器垄断问题**：userbinator指出，复杂的JS反机器人措施可能加剧浏览器垄断，建议使用简单HTML表单提问，以防止LLM（大型语言模型）破解。
• **对机器人检测和应对策略的建议**：edoloughlin提出了一种调皮的策略，即检测到AI机器人时，向其提供随机数据，让它们也感受到痛苦。
• **开源许可证的更新需求**：ANarrativeApe质疑是否需要根据当前机器人滥用行为更新开源许可证，以使这种滥用行为公开化。
• **创建私有网络的讨论**：haswell考虑创建一个类似“亲友”的私有网络，以重获发布信息的自由。
• **国家封锁和爬虫监管**：ggm认为，国家封锁是懒惰且不实用的，爬虫应该支付“愚蠢税”或被监管。
• **对不同类型网站的影响**：grotorea质疑这种现象是否仅影响非营利网站，并担心更严格的登录墙会导致网络内容向深层网络迁移。

争议焦点：
• **如何有效管理机器人流量和数据抓取行为**，包括技术手段（如反机器人措施）和政策手段（如爬虫监管、许可证更新）。
• **机器人流量的快速攻击和DoS攻击的普遍性及其对不同类型网站的影响**。

Software developer Xe Iaso
reached a breaking point
earlier this year when aggressive AI crawler traffic from Amazon overwhelmed their Git repository service, repeatedly causing instability and downtime. Despite configuring standard defensive measures—adjusting robots.txt, blocking known crawler user-agents, and filtering suspicious traffic—Iaso found that AI crawlers continued evading all attempts to stop them, spoofing user-agents and cycling through residential IP addresses as proxies.
Desperate for a solution, Iaso eventually resorted to moving their server behind a VPN and creating "Anubis," a custom-built proof-of-work challenge system that forces web browsers to solve computational puzzles before accessing the site. "It's futile to block AI crawler bots because they lie, change their user agent, use residential IP addresses as proxies, and more," Iaso wrote in a
blog post
titled "a desperate cry for help." "I don't want to have to close off my Gitea server to the public, but I will if I have to."
Iaso's story highlights a broader crisis rapidly spreading across the open source community, as what appear to be aggressive AI crawlers increasingly overload community-maintained infrastructure, causing what amounts to persistent distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks on vital public resources. According to a
comprehensive recent report
from LibreNews, some open source projects now see as much as 97 percent of their traffic originating from AI companies' bots, dramatically increasing bandwidth costs, service instability, and burdening already stretched-thin maintainers.
Kevin Fenzi, a member of the Fedora Pagure project's sysadmin team,
reported on his blog
that the project had to block all traffic from Brazil after repeated attempts to mitigate bot traffic failed. GNOME GitLab implemented Iaso's "Anubis" system, requiring browsers to solve computational puzzles before accessing content. GNOME sysadmin Bart Piotrowski
shared
on Mastodon that only about 3.2 percent of requests (2,690 out of 84,056) passed their challenge system, suggesting the vast majority of traffic was automated. KDE's GitLab infrastructure was temporarily knocked offline by crawler traffic originating from Alibaba IP ranges, according to LibreNews, citing a KDE Development chat.
While Anubis has proven effective at filtering out bot traffic, it comes with drawbacks for legitimate users. When many people access the same link simultaneously—such as when a GitLab link is shared in a chat room—site visitors can face significant delays. Some mobile users have reported waiting up to two minutes for the proof-of-work challenge to complete, according to the news outlet.
The situation isn't exactly new. In December, Dennis Schubert, who maintains infrastructure for the Diaspora social network,
described
the situation as "literally a DDoS on the entire internet" after discovering that AI companies accounted for 70 percent of all web requests to their services.
The costs are both technical and financial. The Read the Docs project reported that blocking AI crawlers immediately decreased their traffic by 75 percent, going from 800GB per day to 200GB per day. This change saved the project approximately $1,500 per month in bandwidth costs, according to their blog post "AI crawlers need to be more respectful."
A disproportionate burden on open source
The situation has created a tough challenge for open source projects, which rely on public collaboration and typically operate with limited resources compared to commercial entities. Many maintainers have reported that AI crawlers deliberately circumvent standard blocking measures, ignoring robots.txt directives, spoofing user agents, and rotating IP addresses to avoid detection.
As LibreNews reported, Martin Owens from the Inkscape project
noted
on Mastodon that their problems weren't just from "the usual Chinese DDoS from last year, but from a pile of companies that started ignoring our spider conf and started spoofing their browser info." Owens added, "I now have a prodigious block list. If you happen to work for a big company doing AI, you may not get our website anymore."
On Hacker News, commenters in threads
about the LibreNews
post last week and a
post on Iaso's battles
in January expressed deep frustration with what they view as AI companies' predatory behavior toward open source infrastructure. While these comments come from forum posts rather than official statements, they represent a common sentiment among developers.
As one Hacker News user
put it
, AI firms are operating from a position that "goodwill is irrelevant" with their "$100bn pile of capital." The discussions depict a battle between smaller AI startups that have worked collaboratively with affected projects and larger corporations that have been unresponsive despite allegedly forcing thousan

data.article_summary: 本文讨论了如何通过改进Unix终端中的命令历史搜索功能来提高工作效率。作者指出，许多人由于不熟悉快捷操作而浪费时间在重复输入命令上。虽然Bash等壳允许使用Ctrl-r进行子字符串搜索，但这种方法较为局限。作者推荐结合使用Ctrl-r和工具fzf，实现模糊搜索并同时显示多个匹配结果，大大提升了查找命令的速度和准确性。作者亲身体验表明，这一组合显著提高了其工作效率，并促使他更大胆地使用复杂命令。最后，作者还提到发现了另一个工具skim，相比fzf更符合其需求。尽管如此，作者认为无论选择哪个工具，都能显著提升Unix用户的效率。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： shell历史搜索工具的比较与改进建议

不同观点：
• **支持Atuin的多设备同步功能**：[jakebasile]认为Atuin非常有价值，尤其是在多台设备上使用时，可以保持历史记录同步，还可以按主机或目录进行筛选。
• **推荐zsh插件**：[northisup]建议使用zsh的zle插件，如history-search-multi-word和fast-syntax-highlighting，认为这些插件提供了良好的性能和语法高亮功能。
• **McFly的智能搜索**：[devjam]推荐McFly，它可以根据工作目录和最近执行的命令进行智能搜索和实时优先级排序。
• **fzf与bash自动补全的整合需求**：[worldsayshi]希望fzf能与bash自动补全整合，以获得更像代码补全的体验，并提到fzf-tab可能是一个解决方案，但仅适用于zsh。
• **对功能过载的担忧**：[fsckboy]担心新功能会打破原有的用户习惯，尤其是对Emacs快捷键的依赖，并提到Linux中的一些功能逐渐消失，如中键粘贴。
• **Atuin与fzf/skim的比较**：[3r7j6qzi9jvnve]认为Atuin的模糊匹配不如fzf/skim，更倾向于使用skim的shell整合功能。
• **推荐hstr**：[bramgn]推荐hstr，认为这是一个很好的历史搜索工具，尽管自己没有广泛使用其他工具。
• **zsh-histdb的优点**：[Hobadee]使用zsh-histdb，并赞赏它显示返回状态和执行命令的目录功能。
• **Atuin的网络安全问题**：[joshka]解释Atuin的网络功能可以完全编译出来，并且历史记录是端到端加密的，认为其安全性足够好。

补充讨论：
• **共享历史记录的价值**：[larusso]认为共享历史记录在不同窗口/标签之间很重要，但对一些人来说可能存在争议，尤其是当重复执行某些命令时。
• **改进历史记录的功能建议**：[wodenokoto]希望历史记录能显示命令执行的位置、是否失败以及添加常用命令/收藏。
• **Bacon替代重复命令执行**：[joshka]提到Bacon可以替代重复执行的命令，如cargo test。
• **对新手的批评**：[SrslyJosh]批评不熟悉基础shell命令的人，并建议学习bash/zsh/sh以及基本工具如grep、sed、awk等。

争议焦点：
• **新功能与用户习惯的冲突**：一些用户（如[fsckboy]）担心新功能会破坏原有的用户习惯，尤其是对Emacs快捷键的依赖。
• **工具的选择与偏好**：不同用户对工具的偏好不同，如Atuin、fzf、zsh插件、McFly和hstr，各有优缺点。

总结：
评论主要围绕shell历史搜索工具的功能、改进建议以及用户习惯的冲突展开。不同用户根据自己的需求和偏好推荐了不同的工具，如Atuin、zsh插件、McFly和hstr，并提出了一些功能改进建议，如整合fzf与bash自动补全、显示命令执行位置和是否失败等。同时，也有用户对新功能与原有用户习惯的冲突表示担忧。

I spend an awful lot of my day in Unix terminals running shell commands. For
some reason, the variance in efficiency between different people when using the shell
is huge: I know people who can run rings around me, and Iâve come across
more than one paid professional who doesnât use the âupâ key to retrieve the
previous command.
I chose that last example very deliberately: most of the commands most of us
run in the shell are highly repetitive. I typically run around 50-100 unique
(i.e. syntactically distinct) shell commands per working day
[1]
â but
Iâll often run a tiny subset of those commands (e.g.
cargo test
) hundreds of
time in a single day.
Since many command-line tools have hard-to-remember options, we can save huge
chunks of time â not to mention make fewer errors â if we can search our
shell history to find a previous incantation of a command we want to run. In
this post Iâm going to show how, with little effort, searching shell
history can look like this:
[Video]
Searching shell history
Larger Unix shells such as Bash have long allowed users to search through their
shell history by pressing
Ctrl-r
and entering a substring. If I (in order)
executed the commands
cat /etc/motd
then
cat /etc/rc.conf
, then
Ctrl-r
followed by âcatâ will first match
cat /etc/rc.conf
; pressing
Ctrl-r
again
will cycle backwards for the next match which is
cat /etc/motd
. I almost
never used this feature, because substring matching is too crude.
For example, I may know the command I want is
cat
, the leaf
name Iâm looking for is
motd
but I donât remember the directory: substring
matching canât help me find what Iâm looking for. Instead, I regularly used
grep
(with wildcards) to search through my shellâs history file instead.
For me, the game changer was pairing
Ctrl-r
with
fzf
, which brought two changes. First,
matching is âfuzzyâ, so I can type âc moâ and
cat /etc/motd
will be
matched. Second, multiple matches are shown at once. Typing âcatâ will show
me several
cat
commands, allowing me to quickly select the right
incantation (which may not have been the most recent).
Itâs difficult for me to overstate how powerful a feature this is. Few things
in life make me as happy as pressing
ctrl-R
then typing â
l1
â and having a 100
character command-line execution that runs a complicated debugging tool, with
multiple environment variables set, whose output gets put in
/tmp/l1
appear
in my terminal.
Using
Ctrl-r
and fzf roughly doubled my efficiency in the shell
overnight. Interestingly, it had an even greater long term effect: I became a
more ambitious user of shell commands because I knew I could outsource my
memory to fzf. For example, since itâs now very easy to recall past commands, I
no longer set global environment variables, which had previously caused me
grief when I forgot about them
[2]
. Now I set environment variables on a
per-command basis, knowing that I can recall them with
Ctrl-r
and fzf.
For many years my favoured shell was zsh. When I later moved from zsh to fish,
Ctrl-r
and fzf was the first thing I configured; and when I moved back to zsh
[3]
, and redid my configuration from scratch,
Ctrl-r
and fzf was again the first
thing I got working (shortly followed by
autosuggestions
). If you
take nothing else from this
post than â
Ctrl-r
and fzf are a significant productivity boon for Unix
usersâ, then I will have done something useful.
No tool, of course, is perfect. A
couple of months back I somehow stumbled across
skim
, an fzf-alike that out-of-the-box
happens to suit me just a little bit better than fzf. The differences
are mostly minor, and you wonât go far wrong with either tool. That said,
I find that skimâs matching more often finds the commands I want quickly,
I prefer skimâs UI, and I find it easier to install skim on
random boxes â small advantages, perhaps, but enough for switching to be
worth it for me.
Doing even better
Finding Skim encouraged me to quickly look around to see what else in this sphere might
improve my productivity. I quickly came across
Atuin
, which is a much
more sophisticated shell history recording mechanism: the video on its front
page showed a much nicer matching UI than I had previously considered possible.
However, I quickly realised Atuin wasnât for me or, at least, wasnât easily for
me.

data.title: Show HN: A website for sharing the "Good, Bad, and Why"s of urban spaces
data.author: kappasan
data.article_summary: 《Community Atlas of Urban Phenomena》是一个让用户分享和标记城市中各种现象的平台，用户可以根据体验将现象标记为"Good"（好）、"Bad"（坏）、"Why"（为什么）等标签，并添加评论和照片。内容涵盖设计、艺术、文化、交通、基础设施、技术、安全、健康、自然、环境、商业等多个方面。用户发布的帖子示例包括对特别建筑、城市设施、交通问题等的评价，如"1000日元卡住了"、"イベント会場へのナビゲーション"（活动会场的导航）、"マンホール周りの印"（井盖周围的标记）等。平台还提供按地区、时间、标签等筛选功能，但存在一些功能不完善的问题，如评论功能不稳定，开发者承诺在下一版本中改进。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一个网站的功能、内容和可访问性的多方面讨论

不同观点：
• sinuhe69认为，增加自动翻译功能将使网站对更广泛的受众开放，提高可访问性。
• sgc指出，在Linux上的Firefox浏览器使用时，图片无法在详情页加载，需要借助谷歌翻译来阅读网站内容，并提供了相关页面的链接。
• cc101对网站上展示的某张海报表示不满，认为其包含种族和文化偏见的内容，并对此种内容被容忍感到不安。

补充讨论：
• ripley12对网站表示赞赏，并计划在有空时添加关于温哥华的相关条目。
• bythreads表示喜欢网站的简洁设计，并提到AI机器人可能会喜欢抓取该网站。
• chachan表达了对网站的怀旧情感，认为这是他怀念的互联网风格。
• upghost分享了自己在探索该网站时，发现了iOS的翻译功能变得更好了，并对网站开发者表示感谢。
• kappasan作为原贴作者（OP），说明了注册表单要求填写电子邮件地址只是作为用户ID使用，非有效地址也可以，但提醒如果忘记密码将无法重置。
• mc3301表示自己有空时会添加许多关于日本的相关条目。
• riffic认为网站很像"模式语言"(Pattern Language)，并希望这种网站在他所在的地区流行起来，同时提供了维基百科上关于"模式语言"的链接。

争议焦点：
• cc101提出的种族和文化偏见问题，与其他用户对网站内容的积极评价形成对比，表明在内容审核和包容性方面存在潜在争议。

43465740.article_summary: 《Community Atlas of Urban Phenomena》是一个让用户分享和标记城市中各种现象的平台，用户可以根据体验将现象标记为"Good"（好）、"Bad"（坏）、"Why"（为什么）等标签，并添加评论和照片。内容涵盖设计、艺术、文化、交通、基础设施、技术、安全、健康、自然、环境、商业等多个方面。用户发布的帖子示例包括对特别建筑、城市设施、交通问题等的评价，如"1000日元卡住了"、"イベント会場へのナビゲーション"（活动会场的导航）、"マンホール周りの印"（井盖周围的标记）等。平台还提供按地区、时间、标签等筛选功能，但存在一些功能不完善的问题，如评论功能不稳定，开发者承诺在下一版本中改进。

• chachan表达了对网站的怀旧情感，认为这是他怀念的互联网风格。

data.title: Ollama Models Atom Feed
data.author: mdp2021
data.article_summary: Simon Willison创建了一个GitHub Actions和GitHub Pages的Atom订阅源，用于抓取Ollama的最新模型数据。由于Ollama是笔记本电脑上运行模型的简便方式，新模型发布值得关注。他通过将示例HTML粘贴到Claude中，并请求生成一个Python脚本以转换为Atom格式，从而构建了该抓取工具。文章还提供了他们一起编写的脚本链接，并提及了一些近期其他文章。发布时间为2025年3月22日。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：RSS/Atom  feed 的优化建议以及对大语言模型（LLM）能力评估的讨论

不同观点：
• **RSS/Atom feed 条目数量问题**：[mdp2021] 认为目前的 RSS/Atom feed 条目数量过多（超过160条），建议缩短时间窗口，将条目数量减少到10条左右，以提高更新效率。同时，提出可以提供一个“完整版”的XML用于首次下载，之后用“精简版”进行日常更新。
  
• **"pulls" 值的无意义**：[mdp2021] 指出在 "proper" RSS feed 中，"pulls" 值没有实际意义，属于冗余或误导性信息，应予以修正。

• **对大语言模型能力评估的兴趣**：[mdp2021] 对 Simon 使用 Claude 构建网页抓取工具表示好奇，并提出是否有人维护一个对各 LLM 能力进行基准测试或非正式评估（如轶事或经验性）的列表，以帮助了解各模型的强项和弱项。

补充讨论：
• **对 Claude 的使用案例**：[mdp2021] 特别提到 Simon 选择使用 Claude 构建特定任务的工具，暗示了对不同 LLM 模型在实际应用中表现的关注和潜在比较兴趣。

• **技术细节的关注**：[mdp2021] 对 feed 条目数量和 "pulls" 值的关注显示出对技术细节的重视，希望通过优化这些细节提升使用体验。

争议焦点：
• 当前 RSS/Atom feed 的条目数量和更新频率是否合理，是否有必要提供两种版本的 feed 以平衡用户需求和系统负载。

data.author: thenerdhead
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：新冠病毒是否仍然具有较大影响

不同观点：
• 观点一：新冠病毒依然具有严重影响。WorldPeas分享了自己的经历，表示自己再次感染了新冠，并且症状和第一次感染时一样严重。这表明至少对某些个体而言，新冠病毒的威胁依然存在，并非已经完全无害。
• 观点二：未明确表述但可推断出的潜在反对意见可能是，新冠病毒对大部分人来说已经不再像以前那么严重，可能有人认为随着疫苗和群体免疫，病毒的危害已经减弱。然而，WorldPeas的个人经历提供了反例，显示出病毒仍可能对某些人造成严重影响。

补充讨论：
• WorldPeas强调自己的经历是个人案例（n=1），说明他意识到单个个例不能代表整体情况，但他的分享仍然指出了新冠病毒在某些情况下仍可能具有严重影响。
• 评论中提到“anecdotal”（轶事性），表明作者承认这仅是个别现象，可能不具备广泛的统计意义，但这种个人经历在讨论中依然具有价值，尤其是在讨论公共健康问题时。

data.article_summary: 本文介绍了与YouTube相关的多项信息和功能。内容包括关于YouTube的介绍、新闻发布、版权声明、联系方式、创作者信息、广告、开发者合作、条款规定、隐私政策、安全指南以及YouTube的使用方式和全新功能测试。此外，还提到NFL Sunday Ticket的服务。文章末尾注明版权为2025年Google LLC所有。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Ghidra与LLM（大型语言模型）集成的效果和实用性

不同观点：
• mdaniel认为之前Ghidra与LLM集成的案例展示出了良好的效果，并分享了一个视频链接（https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42860849）作为参考，显示出对这种集成持积极态度。

• Malimite提到了一篇关于iOS和macOS反编译工具的文章（https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42829402），这可能暗示了在特定平台上应用此类工具的潜力，虽然未明确表态，但提供了另一个视角来审视Ghidra与LLM的结合。

• brokensegue则基于自己的经验，对直接将Ghidra内容复制到LLM并期望其自动解析的效果表示怀疑。他指出这种方法并不总是成功，并建议为这类集成工作制定一些基准以衡量效果，显示出对实际效果的质疑。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于Ghidra与LLM集成在实际应用中的有效性。mdaniel看到了积极的案例，而brokensegue则基于个人经验提出了质疑，认为缺乏明确的成功标准和基准。

• 不同评论者提供了外部资源链接，为讨论提供了更多背景信息和具体案例，帮助更全面地理解Ghidra与LLM集成的应用场景和潜在问题。

• brokensegue的建议指出了一个实际问题，即在技术应用中，需要有明确的衡量标准和基准来评估新工具和方法的有效性。
