Charles Yang is the executive director for the
Center for Industrial Strategy
, a bipartisan think tank focused on industrial policy. Previously, he served as an AI and Supply Chain Policy Advisor at the Department of Energy and was an ML Engineer at an AI hardware startup in San Francisco. Today, he’s here to present some excerpts from
his research
into how Admiral Hyman Rickover built the nuclear navy.
Strategic competition demands more than technological innovation — it requires building industrial power. The U.S. is realizing the damage done by decades of underinvestment in the nation’s industrial base, which now jeopardizes its ability to compete on the global stage. Today, the production capacity of
Chinese shipyards is over 200 times that of US shipyards
, and China has used its
chokehold on critical mineral processing as leverage
to retaliate against US sanctions.
A new bipartisan consensus is emerging around the need for industrial policy — from the passage of the CHIPS and Science Act, to the recent bipartisan introduction of the
SHIPS for America Act
and the
Critical Minerals for the Future Act
.
As Congress steps into this more active role, policymakers should learn from the successes of our past. Nearly 75 years ago, Admiral Hyman G. Rickover, “Father of the Nuclear Navy”, pioneered a bold program to develop and operationalize nuclear power in the Navy. Under his leadership, the U.S. government harnessed the power of the atom, building the world’s first nuclear-powered submarine and the world’s largest fleet of nuclear reactors for civilian power.
Lessons From the Past
Rickover spent his entire career in the Navy and is still the longest-serving naval officer in US history. He spent the first 20 years of his career as an electrical engineer, where he honed a strong technical foundation and unique management style. In 1946, he was assigned a 1-year tour of duty at the Oak Ridge site of the Manhattan Project. Rickover immediately recognized the transformative potential of nuclear technology — he spent the rest of his career building the “Nuclear Navy,” which ensured US strategic dominance of the high seas for the rest of the 20th century.
Within the span of 10 years, Rickover created an entire office dedicated to nuclear propulsion, and successfully launched the world’s first nuclear-powered submarine without cost overruns. He conclusively demonstrated the strategic importance of nuclear propulsion in a timeframe no one thought possible and helped the US beat the Soviets to nuclear propulsion for submarines by 3 years. His institutional legacy is the US Navy’s safe construction and operation of nuclear reactors.
As the US gears up for another strategic competition, Rickover’s story can offer helpful lessons for aspiring technocrats. Oftentimes, industrial policy is framed in terms of legislation, but Rickover demonstrates that industrial policy is as much about policy as it is about strong leadership.
USS Enterprise, the world’s first nuclear-powered aircraft carrier.

.
Talent, Training, and Management
Rickover spent an inordinate amount of time focused on interviewing personnel —
he made the final hiring decision for every naval officer who applied to serve on a nuclear submarine until he retired
. And he was an unorthodox interviewer, screening for high agency individuals who could think on their feet — literally! To test their composure, Rickover famously made candidates sit in a chair with the front two legs shortened as he loomed over them during questioning.
The infamous “Rickover chair”
One interview account:
For one interviewee who said he liked hiking, Rickover asked him if he had ever hiked the nearby “Goat Mountain”. When he said he had not, Rickover told him to bring him proof he had climbed it by tomorrow morning and he would be hired. It turns out that Goat Mountain was the peak of a structure for mountain goats in a zoo. He went to the zoo, asked a tourist to take his picture, jumped into the enclosure, and climbed to the top. He’s hired the next day!
But it didn’t end at the interview process — Rickover believed in continued technical training for his staff and in building out a talented workforce base for this new technology:

He required each officer and engineer he hired to submit a self-study plan demonstrating mastery of advanced texts in metallurgy, physics, and chemistry, along with field trips to AEC facilities, totaling 854 hours of study or 16 hours per week. 43450884.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了美国如何通过借鉴海军上将海曼·里科弗（Hyman Rickover）建设核海军的经验，来应对当前的战略竞争。里科弗通过强大的领导力和技术创新，建立了世界上第一支核动力潜艇舰队，确保了美国在20世纪海上战略优势。文章强调，美国当前需要通过工业政策重振其工业基础，以应对中国在造船业和关键矿产加工领域的领先地位。国会已通过多项法案，如《CHIPS与科学法案》和《SHIPS for America Act》，但里科弗的经验表明，工业政策不仅依赖立法，还需要强有力的领导和人才培养。里科弗亲自面试每一位申请核潜艇职位的军官，并通过严格的培训计划，确保他们掌握必要的技术知识，从而建立了一支高素质的技术团队。文章总结，在面对新的战略竞争时，里科弗的成功经验对现代政策制定者具有重要借鉴意义。

data.article_summary:
文章主要介绍了Qwen2.5-VL-32B-Instruct模型的发布及其特点和性能表现。该模型基于之前的Qwen2.5-VL系列进行了优化，特别在以下几个方面有显著提升：

1. **对齐人类偏好**：调整输出风格，提供更详细、格式更好的答案。
2. **数学推理能力**：解决复杂数学问题的准确性显著提高。
3. **细粒度图像理解和推理**：在图像解析、内容识别和视觉逻辑推理方面更加精确。

性能方面，Qwen2.5-VL-32B-Instruct在多模态任务（如MMMU、MMMU-Pro、MathVista）中表现优异，甚至超过了更大规模的模型（如Qwen2-VL-72B-Instruct）。此外，该模型在纯文本任务中也达到了顶级性能。

文章还提供了几个示例，展示模型在图像理解和数学推理任务中的具体应用，如计算卡车到达时间和解决几何角度问题。

总的来说，Qwen2.5-VL-32B-Instruct在多模态和文本任务中均表现出色，得到了广泛关注和好评。

Introduction
#
At the end of January this year, we launched the Qwen2.5-VL series of models, which received widespread attention and positive feedback from the community. Building on the Qwen2.5-VL series, we continued to optimize the model using reinforcement learning and open-sourced the new VL model with the beloved 32B parameter scale under the Apache 2.0 license —
Qwen2.5-VL-32B-Instruct
. Compared to the previously released Qwen2.5-VL series models, the features of this 32B VL model are as follows:
Responses More Aligned with Human Preferences
: Adjusted the output style to provide more detailed, better-formatted answers that align more closely with human preferences.
Mathematical Reasoning
: Significant improvement in the accuracy of solving complex mathematical problems.
Fine-grained Image Understanding and Reasoning
: Enhanced accuracy and detailed analysis in tasks such as image parsing, content recognition, and visual logic deduction.
Performance
#
Extensive benchmarking against state-of-the-art (SoTA) models of comparable scale,
Qwen2.5-VL-32B-Instruct
has demonstrated superiority over baselines, e.g., Mistral-Small-3.1-24B and Gemma-3-27B-IT, even surpassing the larger
Qwen2-VL-72B-Instruct
. Notably, it achieves significant advantages in multimodal tasks such as
MMMU
,
MMMU-Pro
, and
MathVista
, which focus on complex, multi-step reasoning. On
MM-MT-Bench
, a benchmark emphasizing subjective user experience evaluation,
Qwen2.5-VL-32B-Instruct
outperforms its predecessor
Qwen2-VL-72B-Instruct
by a substantial margin.
In addition to excelling in visual capabilities, Qwen2.5-VL-32B-Instruct has also achieved top-tier performance in pure text capabilities at the same scale.
Demo Cases
#
Fine-grained Image Understanding and Reasoning
Next
User
I am driving a large truck on this road, and it is now 12 o’clock. Can I reach a place 110 kilometers away before 13 o’clock?
Qwen2.5-VL-32B
To determine whether you can reach a place 110 kilometers away before 13:00, we need to analyze the information provided:
Current Time
: It is 12:00.
Distance to Destination
: 110 kilometers.
Speed Limit for Trucks
: The speed limit sign indicates that the maximum speed for trucks is
100 km/h
.
Step-by-Step Analysis:
#
1.
Calculate the Required Travel Time
#
The formula to calculate travel time is:
\[
\text{Time} = \frac{\text{Distance}}{\text{Speed}}
\]
Given:
Distance = 110 km
Maximum Speed = 100 km/h
Substitute the values:
\[
\text{Time} = \frac{110 \text{ km}}{100 \text{ km/h}} = 1.1 \text{ hours}
\]
2.
Convert Time to Hours and Minutes
#
1.1 hours is equivalent to:
\[
1 \text{ hour} + 0.1 \times 60 \text{ minutes} = 1 \text{ hour} + 6 \text{ minutes} = 1 \text{ hour and } 6 \text{ minutes}
\]
3.
Determine Arrival Time
#
If you start at 12:00 and it takes 1 hour and 6 minutes to travel 110 kilometers, your arrival time will be:
\[
12:00 + 1 \text{ hour and } 6 \text{ minutes} = 13:06
\]
4.
Compare with Target Time
#
You want to arrive before 13:00. However, based on the calculations, you will arrive at 13:06, which is
after
13:00.
Conclusion:
#
Given the speed limit of 100 km/h for trucks, it is
not possible
to reach a place 110 kilometers away before 13:00.
Thus, the final answer is:
\[
\boxed{\text{No}}
\]
Mathematical Reasoning
Next
User
As shown in the figure, the straight lines AB and CD intersect at point O, OD bisects ∠AOE, ∠BOC = 50.0, then ∠EOB = ()
Qwen2.5-VL-32B
Problem Analysis
#
We are given the following information:
Straight lines $ AB $ and $ CD $ intersect at point $ O $.
$ OD $ bisects $ \angle AOE $.
$ \angle BOC = 50^\circ $.
We need to find $ \angle EOB $.
Step-by-Step Solution
#
Step 1: Understand the given information and relationships
#
Since $ AB $ and $ CD $ are straight lines intersecting at $ O $, the angles around point $ O $ sum up to $ 360^\circ $.
The vertically opposite angles are equal. Therefore:
$$
\angle AOD = \angle BOC \quad \text{and} \quad \angle DOB = \angle COA.
$$
Given $ \angle BOC = 50^\circ $, we have:
$$
\angle AOD = 50^\circ.
$$
Step 2: Use the angle bisector property
#
It is given that $ OD $ bisects $ \angle AOE $. This means:
$$
\angle AOD = \angle DOE.
$$
Since $ \angle AOD = 50^\circ $, we have:
$$
\angle DOE = 50^\circ.
$$
Step 3: Determine $ \angle AOE $
#
The angle $ \angle AOE $ is the sum of $ \angle AOD $ and $ \angle DOE $:
$$
\angle AOE = \angle AOD + \angle DOE = 50^\circ + 50^\circ = 100^\circ.
$$
Step 4: Use the straight line property
#
Since $ AB $ is a straight line, the angles on a straight line sum up to $ 180^\circ $. Therefore:
$$
\angle AOE + \angle EOB = 180^\circ.
$$
Substituting $ \angle AOE = 100^\circ $, we get:
$$
100^\circ + \angle EOB = 180^\circ.
$$
Solving for $ \angle EOB $:
$$
\angle EOB = 180^\circ - 100^\circ = 80^\circ.
$$
Final Answer
#
$$
\boxed{80}
$$

data.article_summary: 本文讲述了美国神父雷吉纳尔德·福斯特（Reginald Foster）的独特职业生涯。1970年，福斯特因其出色的拉丁文能力被梵蒂冈相中，负责撰写教宗的拉丁文信件，尽管他的上级 initially 反对。福斯特在梵蒂冈工作了四十年，以其非凡的拉丁文才华和不拘一格的个性闻名。他不仅在教会内推广拉丁语教育，还因其直言不讳引发争议，例如在纪录片《宗教的荒谬》中批评教会的某些做法。尽管他的言论引起一些不满，但由于健康原因和即将退休，他最终安然离开职位。福斯特被誉为过去半个世纪最具影响力的拉丁语教师，他的教学方法独特且富有感染力，改变了众多学生对拉丁语的认识。

主要讨论点：关于拉丁语学习、教学方法及对Reginald Foster的纪念与讨论

不同观点：
• Schoen和Akshayshah分享了对Reginald Foster的亲身学习经历，强调Foster是一位非常有魅力的老师，他的教学影响了许多学生继续以不同方式教授拉丁语。Schoen还指出，文章没有提到Foster在2020年去世。
• Dang提供了与Foster去世相关的新闻链接，并引用了之前关于Foster的讨论，提供了背景信息。
• Dhosek讨论了自己重建拉丁语知识的过程，特别是通过使用晚期拉丁语材料如Beeson的《中世纪拉丁语入门》和《武加大圣经》。他提到自己通过手动翻译圣经来提高拉丁语水平，但并不追求完全流利。

• Jun8提出了关于当前在古希腊语方面具有相似能力的人的问题，但没有深入讨论。
• Cbm-vic-20提到将浏览器语言设置为拉丁语的趣味实验，Koshkin提供了学习早期印欧语言的资源链接。
• Slyall分享了教皇本笃十六世用拉丁语宣布辞职时，在场许多人未能理解的轶事。
• Gnabgib引用了之前关于Foster的讨论链接，提供更多讨论背景。
• Dhosek补充了Foster去世的相关信息，并提到Foster相关书籍的后续出版情况。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了多种拉丁语学习资源和方法，包括书籍、应用程序和在线社区，反映出不同学习者对拉丁语学习的兴趣和投入。
• 争议焦点不明显，但Foster的教学方法与传统语法教学法之间的对比是隐含的讨论主题，反映出不同教学理念之间的潜在分歧。

43457202.article_content:
I
n
1970, the Procurator General of the Discalced Carmelite Order, Finian Monahan, was summoned to the Vatican for a meeting. The subject of the meeting was a promising young American priest by the name of Reginald Foster. The head Latinist of the Vatican’s State Department had tapped Foster to write papal correspondence, which was at the time composed entirely in Latin. Foster wanted the job but was bound by a vow of obedience, and the decision would be made by his superiors. Monahan intended to resist. Foster, thirty years of age, had proven himself to be both supremely intellectually gifted and utterly reliable—a precious thing at a time when the Catholic Church’s religious orders were hemorrhaging priests. Monahan thought Latin was a dead end. He didn’t want to lose one of his best to a Vatican department that would only get less and less important every year. He said Foster would go to the Vatican “over my dead body.”
Foster remembers the meeting vividly. “So we arrive there, and we’re ushered into this office, and who do we find there but Ioannes Benelli,” Foster says, using Benelli’s Latin name, as was customary at the Vatican at that time. He continues:
Benelli was Paul
VI
’s hatchet man—whenever he wanted something to get done, he called on Benelli. He was very energetic—got things done, and no nonsense. Everyone was terrified of him. I was too, and now here we were in the room with him, and he turns to Monahan and says, “This is Foster?” The General said yes. Then Benelli said, “Thank you very much, we won’t be needing you anymore.” And he took me by the hand and brought me down to the State Department and that was the end of that. Monahan didn’t say a word. I was now working for the Pope, and it was like I was more or less out of the Carmelite Order. A lot of the time the Order didn’t even really know what I was doing.
Foster would spend the next forty years at the Vatican, part of a small team of scribes who composed the pope’s correspondence, translated his encyclicals, and wrote copy for internal church documents. His somewhat unique position between the Carmelite Order and the Vatican bureaucracy meant that in fact he had a great deal of freedom for a priest. Later in his career his loose tongue—some in the church called it a loose cannon—would attract the notice of journalists looking for interesting copy. “Sacred language?” he said when asked about Latin as the “sacred language” of the church. “In the first century every prostitute in Rome spoke it fluently—and much better than most people in the Roman Curia.” The Minnesota
Star Tribune
quoted him as saying “I like to say mass in the nude,” which caused a small Curial kerfuffle (Foster claims he was misquoted). He appeared in Bill Maher’s movie
Religulous
, which featured him agreeing with the proposition that the Vatican itself was at odds with the message of Jesus, that the pope should not be living in a palace, and that hell and “that Old Catholic stuff” was “finished” and “gone.” Foster says the pope received complaints from bishops and cardinals about his appearance. “They said ‘Who is this Latinist of yours and what the hell is he doing?’ They would have fired me for sure. But by the time the film came out I was sick and a few months away from retirement anyway. So they just waited it out and let me go quietly.” He had already been fired from his post at the pontifical Gregorian University for allowing dozens of students to take his classes without paying for them.
B
es
ides being the Pope’s Latinist and “one of the Vatican’s most colorful characters” (as the Catholic News Service called him), Foster has been a tireless champion of Latin in the classroom. Indeed, Foster’s greatest legacy may be as a teacher. “The most influential Latin teacher in the last half-century is Reggie Foster,” says Dr. Nancy Llewellyn, professor of Latin at Wyoming Catholic College. “That’s not just my opinion—that’s a fact. For decades, he had the power to change lives like no other teacher in our field. I saw him for an hour in Rome in 1985 and that one hour completely changed my life. His approach was completely different from every other Latin teacher out there, and it was totally transformative.”
A humanist par excellence.
A humanist par excellence, Latin for Foster was not something to be dissected by linguistic analysis or serve as the raw data for a theory of gender or poetics: it was a language, a medium of human connection. I first met Foster in 1995, at his summer school, and couldn’t get enough: I returned seven times. No one on Earth was reading as much Latin as he and his students were, but he was more like an old-school newspaper editor than an academic: he wanted the
story
. But for that you actually had to know Latin, and know it well. Foster was ruthless about ignorance, and equally ruthless about anything that to him looked like mere academic posturing. “I don’t care about your garbage literary theory!” he barked at his students one day. “

data.title: Evolving Scala
data.author: pjmlp
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了Scala语言的未来发展方向，强调了持续创新的必要性。尽管Scala的热度已不如2010年代，但它在技术上比十年前更加成熟，拥有更稳固的基础和更广泛的生态系统。文章指出，Scala的核心价值在于结合了**安全**和**便利**，以及面向对象与函数式编程的融合。然而，随着其他语言的进步，Scala必须在保持优势的同时，解决其弱点，特别是在新手入门体验上进行改进。

未来，Scala的开发重点将包括：在**不牺牲便利**的前提下提高**安全性**，如引入捕获检查、显式空值、安全初始化等功能；以及在**保证安全**的前提下增加**便利**，如引入枚举、可选括号、命名元组等。文章还提到，数据字面量聚合的讨论正在进行中，但尚未有定论。Scala需要不断前进，以保持其吸引力和相关性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Scala 编程语言的现状、优缺点以及其未来发展。

不同观点：
• epolanski 认为 Scala 3 的开发者不断添加新功能，导致工具和社区难以跟上。他主张停止开发新功能，专注于现有生态系统，因为当前语言已经非常优秀。他还指出，Scala 作为学术研究项目的一部分，开发者往往忽视社区的反馈。
• nikitaga 持积极态度，认为 Scala 非常享受和高效，特别是在团队开发中。虽然 Scala 2 到 Scala 3 的过渡期有些艰难，但现在使用 Scala 3 非常顺利，语言和生态系统都在向好的方向发展。
• ryandvm 提出在组织中使用 Scala 可能是一个“危险信号”，因为这可能意味着过多的技术争论和不切实际的技术决策，尤其是对那些不熟悉函数式编程的人。
• cardanome 认为其他语言（如 Java）已经赶上来了，Scala 的独特优势不再明显，虽然 Scala 仍然很棒，但它的流行度难以大幅提升。
• flakiness 回顾了 Scala 在一些项目（如 Apache Spark 和 Akka）中的成功应用，但也指出 Scala 的影响力在缩小。
• openplatypus 对 Scala 的评价积极，虽然承认其不流行，但在某些项目中表现出色，同时也提到库升级路径的痛苦。
• DeathArrow 认为 Scala 失去了过去的势头，现在人们对它的兴趣减少。
• dmos62 表示 Scala 在他的工具包中不再有位置，因为其他语言在特定领域表现更好。
• yard2010 认为 Scala 是他工作过的最棒的语言，提供了很多有价值的范式。
• true_blue 承认 Scala 的流行度下降，但对 Scala 向更易于初学者入门的方向发展持积极态度。
• isjustintime 对 Scala 的现状感到遗憾，认为它被局限在一些特定领域，如 Spark。
• minebreaker 抱怨 Scala 的 IDE 支持差，但赞赏 IntelliJ 团队正在改进 Scala 3 的支持。
• GardenLetter27 认为 Scala 的编译时间过长，甚至比 Rust 还要糟糕。
• ios-sux 对 Scala 的未来持谨慎乐观态度，认为它可能会像 COBOL 一样在特定领域继续存在。
• linotype 怀念过去使用 Scala 的时光，并希望其他语言能引入 Scala 的一些优秀特性。

补充讨论：
• Scala 的功能丰富和强大与其复杂性和社区分裂的争议并存。
• 对 Scala 工具链（如 IDE 支持和编译时间）的批评和改进希望。
• Scala 在函数式编程和并发处理方面的独特优势与其他语言的赶超对比。
• Scala 在实际项目中的成功应用与在更广泛行业中应用的局限性。

争议焦点：Scala 是否应继续开发新功能，还是应专注于现有生态系统的完善和普及。

43468972.article_content:
Evolving Scala
Monday 24 March 2025
Martin Odersky and Haoyi Li
BLOG
There is always ongoing discussion about the future direction of the Scala language.
How fast should it move?
What needs to be improved?
Should the language change at all?
This article discusses how
Scala must keep evolving
, why that evolution is necessary, and what directions we expect that evolution to take.
We hope that this will cover many of the frequently asked questions on the direction of the Scala language, and help the community understand where the language will go in the months and years to come.
Summary
Although Scala is no longer riding the wave of hype it had in the mid-2010s, by most surveys the language maintains its position just outside the list of mainstream languages.
From a technical perspective, the core language and ecosystem have improved greatly over the past decade.
In many ways Scala is on much better foundations today than it was 10 years ago.
Scala has a history of leading the way for the rest of the programming field.
In exchange for a bit less polish and stability than mainstream languages, people chose Scala to get next decadeâs language features today.
The value of Scala has always been the unique combination of
safety
and
convenience
that these language features have enabled, and its fusion of
object oriented
and
functional
programming ideas that can elegantly accommodate these features.
But other languages are also improving, and so Scala must continue to innovate, improving on both its strengths and weaknesses with a particular focus on the newcomer onboarding experience.
There are of course ongoing issues, especially around IDE support and the learnability of the ecosystem, and there will always be concerns about tooling, compatibility, and migration cost as a language evolves.
But Scala has no choice but to move forward if it is to maintain its appeal and relevance in the years to come.
Where Scala stands today
Although the hype has died down, popularity-wise Scala is about where it has always been: not quite in the mainstream, but with far greater adoption than more niche languages.
For example, the RedMonk Language Rankings had Scala in
14th place in 2014
and
still in 14th place 10 years later in 2024
.
In those years, the programming landscape changed significantly: Swift replacing Objective C, the emergence of Go and Kotlin and Dart and Rust, the decline of CoffeeScript and Perl.
Yet throughout this Scalaâs place remains unchanged.
Although individuals in the community come and go, Scala as a whole seems to be holding strong with a solid base of enthusiasts.
Technically, Scala is on stronger foundations than it was 10 years ago.
The ecosystem has matured and the various Reactive or Pure-FP styles have found their audiences.
Alternative styles like the
Scala Toolkit
and the
com.lihaoyi
platform are now available.
New build tools like
Scala-CLI
and
Mill
have emerged, and developer tools like
Scalafmt
and
Scalafix
have become widely used.
IDEs remain a pain point, but we expect them to improve over the course of 2025.
Heavy use of symbolic operators has thankfully fallen out of style.
Scala has always been a language on the leading edge, proving the viability of language features like lambdas, records, and pattern matching that were adopted 10â15 years later by Java, Python, and other mainstream languages.
It remains to be seen which current Scala features the mainstream languages will adopt 10-15 years from now.
Where is Scala going?
In this section, we will discuss some areas where the core Scala developers will focus their efforts.
Safety and convenience: pick two
Scala has always been a hybrid language.
The fusion of object-oriented and functional styles was often talked about.
But its other fusion has been of
safety
and
convenience.
Traditionally, âscriptingâ languages like Python were unsafe but convenient, while âapplicationâ languages like Java were safe but inconvenient.
Scala was the first to prove that you can do both in the same language.
More modern languages like Swift or Kotlin have progressed in this direction as well, the idea was unheard of when Scala first started.
However, the programming landscape has not stood still for the last two decades.
Much of what used to be unique to Scala is now common.
All modern languages provide generics, type inference, lambdas, records, pattern matching, and other such features.
To continue to attract users, Scala must continue to innovate in both directions:
Increasing safety
without compromising convenience: features like
capture checking
,
explicit nulls
,
safe initialization
,
multiversal equality
.
Increasing convenience
without compromising safety: features like
enums
,
optional braces
,
named tuples
.
A discussion about
aggregate data literals
has sparked a lot of interest, although it is still too early to see what will come out of it.
The Scala ecosystem is broad and diverse, but we think these twin goals are the common thre

本文讨论了Scala语言的未来发展方向，强调了持续创新的必要性。尽管Scala的热度已不如2010年代，但它在技术上比十年前更加成熟，拥有更稳固的基础和更广泛的生态系统。文章指出，Scala的核心价值在于结合了**安全**和**便利**，以及面向对象与函数式编程的融合。然而，随着其他语言的进步，Scala必须在保持优势的同时，解决其弱点，特别是在新手入门体验上进行改进。

未来，Scala的开发重点将包括：在**不牺牲便利**的前提下提高**安全性**，如引入捕获检查、显式空值、安全初始化等功能；以及在**保证安全**的前提下增加**便利**，如引入枚举、可选括号、命名元组等。文章还提到，数据字面量聚合的讨论正在进行中，但尚未有定论。Scala需要不断前进，以保持其吸引力和相关性。

data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary:
欧洲航天局（ESA）正邀请提案，以引入竞争机制，促进欧洲发射市场的多元化发展，目标是培育一个类似美国的多方竞争行业。根据“欧洲发射器挑战”计划，ESA将选择公司从2026年至2030年运输ESA及其他欧洲政府载荷，且这些公司需在2028年前展示升级发射载具。该挑战对所有欧洲发射企业开放，ESA采取了更为市场化的方式，不干涉企业具体组织形式，仅要求提供“欧洲发射服务”。

目前，欧洲仅依赖阿里安航天公司发射卫星，而该挑战旨在培育更多私营竞争者。ESA未设定性能或可重复使用性要求，但希望限制竞争者数量以有效分配资金。ESA计划为每个挑战者提供高达1.69亿欧元资助，但需说服各国政府出资支持。与美国相比，欧洲在吸引风投资本和政府支持商业航天方面相对落后。

The European Space Agency is inviting proposals to inject competition into the European launch market, an important step toward fostering a dynamic multiplayer industry officials hope, one day, will mimic that of the United States.
The near-term plan for the European Launcher Challenge is for ESA to select companies for service contracts to transport ESA and other European government payloads to orbit from 2026 through 2030. A second component of the challenge is for companies to perform at least one demonstration of an upgraded launch vehicle by 2028. The competition is open to any European company working in the launch business.
"What we expect is that these companies will make a step in improving and upgrading their capacity with respect to what they’re presently working," said Toni Tolker-Nielsen, ESA's acting director of space transportation."In terms of economics and physics, it’s better to have a bigger launcher than a smaller launcher in terms of price per kilogram to orbit."
"The ultimate goal is we should be establishing privately-developed competitive launch services in Europe, which will allow us to procure launch services in open competition," Tolker-Nielsen said in an interview with Ars.
From one to many?
ESA and other European institutions currently have just one European provider, Arianespace, to award launch contracts for the continent's scientific, Earth observation, navigation, and military satellites. Arianespace operates the Ariane 6 and Vega C rockets. Vega C operations will soon be taken over by the Italian aerospace company Avio. Both rockets were developed with ESA funding.
The launcher challenge is modeled on NASA's use of commercial contracting methods beginning nearly 20 years ago with the agency's commercial cargo program, which kickstarted the development of SpaceX's Dragon and Northrop Grumman's Cygnus resupply freighters for the International Space Station. NASA later applied the same model to commercial crew, and most
recently for commercial lunar landers
.
Uncharacteristically for ESA, the agency is taking a hands-off approach for the launcher challenge. One of the few major requirements is that the winners should offer a "European launch service" that flies from European territory, which includes the French-run Guiana Space Center in South America.
Europe's second Ariane 6 rocket lifted off March 6 with a French military spy satellite.
Credit:
European Space Agency
"We are trying something different, where they are completely free to organize themselves," Tolker-Nielsen said. "We are not pushing anything. We are in a complete service-oriented model here. That’s the principal difference between the new approach and the old approach."
ESA also isn't setting requirements on launcher performance, reusability, or the exact number of companies it will select in the challenge. But ESA would like to limit the number of challengers "to a minimum" to ensure the agency's support is meaningful, without spreading its funding too thin, Tolker-Nielsen said.
"For the ESA-developed launchers, which are Ariane 6 and Vega C, we own the launch system," Tolker-Nielsen said. "We finished the development, and the deliverables were the launch systems that we own at ESA, and we make it available to an operator—Arianespace, and Avio soon for Vega C—to exploit."
These ESA-led launcher projects were expensive. The development of Ariane 6 cost European governments more than $4 billion. Ariane 6 is now flying, but none of the up-and-coming European alternatives are operational.
Next steps
It's taken a while to set up the European Launcher Challenge, which
won preliminary approval from ESA's 23 member states
at a ministerial-level meeting in 2023. ESA released an "invitation to tender" soliciting proposals from European launch companies Monday, with submissions due by May 5. This summer, ESA expects to select the top proposals and prepare a funding package for consideration by its member states at the next ministerial meeting in November.
The top factors ESA will consider in this first phase of the challenge are each proposer's business plan, technical credibility, and financial credibility.
In a statement, ESA said it has allotted up to 169 million euros ($182 million at today's exchange rates) per challenger. This is significant funding for Europe's crop of cash-hungry launch startups, each of which have raised no more than a few hundred million euros. But this allotment comes with a catch. ESA's leaders and the winners of the launch challenge must persuade their home governments to pay up.
Let's take a moment to compare Europe's launch industry with the United States.
There are multiple viable US commercial launch companies. In the United States, it's easier to attract venture capital, the government has been a more reliable proponent of commercial spaceflight,

data.article_summary: "vibe-http" 是一个小型 HTTP 服务器，它将 HTTP 请求转发给 OpenAI 的 ChatGPT API，并返回生成的响应，使每个网站访问者的体验各不相同。为减少混乱，之前的请求和响应会作为上下文传递给 ChatGPT。该项目托管在 https://vibehttp.com/，用户可以通过创意路径访问不同内容，如 `/kevin/what-is-the-meaning-of-life`，甚至可以尝试子域名如 `news.vibehttp.com`。用户如果不喜欢当前页面，可以刷新重新生成。要本地运行，需设置 OPENAI_API_KEY 并执行 `go run main.go`。项目主要使用 Go 语言，包含少量 HTML。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI生成教育材料工具的评价与改进建议

不同观点：
• **积极支持与赞赏**：
  - 多位用户（如[mellosouls], [pratikshelar871], [julienmarie]）对该工具的整体功能表示赞赏，认为它能够大幅节省教师准备材料的时间，尤其是在生成演示文稿和测验题目方面表现出色。
  - [julienmarie] 特别指出，该工具在员工培训方面也有潜力，尤其是结合内部文档生成培训材料。
  - [tda] 提到，尽管AI生成的内容质量一般，但相比某些现有的低质量材料，AI工具仍然具有一定的优势。

• **批评与担忧**：
  - [cube00] 对AI生成内容的质量提出严厉批评，认为生成的文本内容空洞且重复，甚至在测验题目中出现错误，误导学生。
  - [zelon88] 对隐私和安全问题表示严重关切，强调必须在教育工具中妥善处理用户数据，建议尽快发布隐私政策和使用条款。
  - [ujkiolp] 对工具的教育效果持怀疑态度，认为学生需要补充其他学习材料，暗示AI工具不能完全替代传统教学。

• **功能改进建议**：
  - [pratikshelar871] 建议通过与其他学习管理系统（LMS）的集成来增加用户接受度，避免繁琐的采购流程。
  - [babyent] 提出增加学生实时协作功能，使学生可以在小组任务中共同使用该工具。
  - [_puk] 和 [pbhjpbhj] 都提到允许教师上传和分享他们优化后的幻灯片，从而形成一个资源共享的社区，并探讨了通过这些资源获利的可能性。
  - [vunderba] 建议专注于“互动活动”功能以区分市场，并提到可以借鉴其他类似工具（如TeachMateAI, Magic School AI）。
  - [gus_massa] 提出两个具体的UI设计建议，包括减少文本量和改进颜色搭配。

• **市场竞争与定位**：
  - [vunderba] 提到教育领域已有不少类似工具，建议探索员工培训市场以避开竞争激烈的K-12教育市场。
  - [fanssex] 提到一个类似的工具Pageon.ai，并对该工具背后的公司提出一些商业策略上的质疑，提醒大家谨慎使用。

补充讨论：
- 用户普遍关注工具的内容质量和用户体验，尤其是在AI生成文本的准确性和幻灯片设计的视觉效果上。
- 多个用户提到隐私和数据安全问题，特别是在教育领域处理学生个人信息时，强调了发布明确的使用条款和隐私政策的必要性。
- 对于市场定位，有用户建议探索教育领域外的其他潜在市场，如企业员工培训。

争议焦点：
- 核心争议在于AI生成内容的质量是否足够可靠以支持日常教学需求。一些用户认为AI生成的材料可以作为有力的教学辅助工具，而另一些用户则认为其内容空洞且容易出错，不能完全依赖。

  - [zelon88] 对隐私和安全问题表示严重关切，强调必须在教育工具中妥善处理用户数据，建议尽快发布隐私政策和使用条款。
  - [ujkiolp] 对工具的教育效果持怀疑态度，认为学生需要补充其他学习材料，暗示AI工具不能完全替代传统教学。

• **功能改进建议**：
  - [pratikshelar871] 建议通过与其他学习管理系统（LMS）的集成来增加用户接受度，避免繁琐的采购流程。
  - [babyent] 提出增加学生实时协作功能，使学生可以在小组任务中共同使用该工具。
  - [_puk] 和 [pbhjpbhj] 都提到允许教师上传和分享他们优化后的幻灯片，从而形成一个资源共享的社区，并探讨了通过这些资源获利的可能性。
  - [vunderba] 建议专注于“互动活动”功能以区分市场，并提到可以借鉴其他类似工具（如TeachMateAI, Magic School AI）。
  - [gus_massa] 提出两个具体的UI设计建议，包括减少文本量和改进颜色搭配。

• **市场竞争与定位**：
  - [vunderba] 提到教育领域已有不少类似工具，建议探索员工培训市场以避开竞争激烈的K-12教育市场。
  - [fanssex] 提到一个类似的工具Pageon.ai，并对该工具背后的公司提出一些商业策略上的质疑，提醒大家谨慎使用。

补充讨论：
- 用户普遍关注工具的内容质量和用户体验，尤其是在AI生成文本的准确性和幻灯片设计的视觉效果上。
- 多个用户提到隐私和数据安全问题，特别是在教育领域处理学生个人信息时，强调了发布明确的使用条款和隐私政策的必要性。
- 对于市场定位，有用户建议探索教育领域外的其他潜在市场，如企业员工培训。

争议焦点：
- 核心争议在于AI生成内容的质量是否足够可靠以支持日常教学需求。一些用户认为AI生成的材料可以作为有力的教学辅助工具，而另一些用户则认为其内容空洞且容易出错，不能完全依赖。

HOME
Tech
Aircraft Detection at Planetary Scale
Adam Van Etten
March 19, 2025
•
5
min read
Tech
Tech
Introduction
On a typical day, there are greater than 10,000 aircraft (commercial, private, and military) in flight at any given time. The precise departure (point A) and destination (point B) locations, as well as the timing of flight activity, provide critically important information for myriad industries. For instance, in the defense and intelligence sector, being able to identify how many aircraft were stationed at one foreign government’s airbase (point A) and how many are gone the next day may reveal insights as to why an allied government’s airbase (point B) just received a new fleet on their tarmac.
On the commercial side, understanding how many aircraft landed in a city on a specific day can help predict economic trends and assess the impacts of world events - such as the quantity of aircraft present for large sporting or entertainment events. Satellite imagery is a powerful information source for this type of aircraft detection. Combine automated satellite scans of airfields with a global news reporting large language model, and you can start to get a feed of insights, linking the patterns of politics and economies with global air traffic.
Scale
Aircraft detection with satellite imagery is nothing new. In fact, aircraft detection on the tarmac is an archetypal use case for remote sensing machine learning. Until now, though, aircraft detection has been limited to a select number of airfields with sporadic coverage and cadence. Planet’s satellites, on the other hand, scan all of Earth’s landmass on a near-daily basis, so we are now able to mitigate those limitations, leveraging novel machine learning techniques with global PlanetScope coverage to drastically scale global aircraft detection.
The need for greater scale in aircraft detection is difficult to overstate. More than one hundred thousand commercial and military flights take place each day, as planes transport people and cargo to nearly fifty thousand airports across the globe. Some sites collect and share publicly available data on this complex matrix of movement. But not every flight is recorded, and not every plane is public.
Monitoring aircraft activity is vital for economic, defense, and intelligence purposes, but current methods rely on tedious and expensive processes, especially at scale. The rapid pace of geopolitical developments and sheer volume of data means that analyzing airfields manually is no longer feasible, especially in conflict/sensitive zones where aircraft movements aren’t publicly reported.
Planet’s new Aircraft Detection Analytic Feed automates daily detection of aircraft by leveraging a machine learning model trained using PlanetScope and SkySat data. It precisely identifies aircraft ≥25 meters in length or wingspan across airfields globally. It represents the first attempt at global detection of large aircraft on a near-daily basis and offers a scalable solution for analysis at scale. This presents a massive and unprecedented opportunity for analysts with or without geospatial expertise. Historical daily counts of aircraft broken down by size and location enables pattern-of-life analyses to be conducted, highlighting when anomalous behavior is detected. This can indicate events taking place or even actions to come.
Keep reading for more information and
register for our upcoming webinar
.
Our Approach
Our Aircraft Detection service leverages a supervised object detection model, trained on PlanetScope imagery to detect aircraft at rest on an airfield/airport tarmac. Precise labeling of aircraft can be a challenging task in medium-resolution PlanetScope imagery, so we use high-resolution SkySat imagery collected within 3 minutes of a PlanetScope scene (see Figure 1). This approach enables us to label on high-resolution imagery, then apply those high fidelity labels to medium-resolution PlanetScope data. The vast majority of aircraft are static on a 3-minute timeframe, but around ~2% of aircraft move between the two collections, and we remove those labels in our quality control phase.
Figure 1. SkySat aircraft labels are applied to concurrent PlanetScope imagery.
With this approach, we collected over 800 concurrent (or “crossover”) image pairs for labeling. After significant experimentation with many different model architectures, we determined that aircraft <25m in length or wingspan are too small to be reliably detected in medium resolution imagery, so we elected to focus on aircraft this size or greater. Splitting the dataset into 85% training / 15% testing, we generated a training dataset consisting of ~15,000 labels, roughly evenly split between civilian and military types. This is by no means an enormous dataset, so expansion of the label corpus would likely yield a performance boost.
Figure 2. Airfield locations in the labeled dataset.
Figure 3. Observation dates, covering multiple years and every season. A concert

data.title: Show HN: My iOS app to practice sight reading (10 years in the App Store)
data.author: rooster117
data.article_summary: **Notes - Sight Reading Trainer**是一款针对iOS的音乐识谱训练应用，适合从初学者到有经验的音乐人。主要功能包括：多种互动练习、通过MIDI或麦克风输入、自定义难度、全面的乐理知识（如音符时值、升降调等）、进度追踪、歌曲练习和目标设定。最新版本修复了MIDI输入和麦克风使用问题。用户评价高达4.8星，称赞其易用性和有效性，但有用户指出缺乏系统的升降调训练。该应用免费，且不强制付费解锁内容，广受好评。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对某钢琴学习应用的评价与建议

不同观点：
• [赞赏观点] 
  - 多名用户（gustanas, ppetty, mortar, hackerdood, appsDev）对应用的设计、功能和用户体验表示赞赏。他们特别提到应用的ASO（应用商店优化）策略成功，包括清晰的截图、相关关键词和优秀的评价。
  - 一些用户（gustanas, ppetty）虽然不是音乐家，但也对应用的专业性和专注度表示钦佩。

• [功能需求与改进建议]
  - pil0u：询问应用是否可以通过麦克风识别音符（do ré mi）。
  - mmacvicarprett：建议增加从乐谱生成音符的功能，以便更贴近实际演奏需求。
  - tianshuo：提出两点建议，一是增加逻辑性更强的音符模式，二是增加节拍器和按时间按音符的功能。
  - pseudosaid：希望增加导入MIDI文件的功能。
  - xlii：提出三点建议，一是生成更和谐的音符序列，二是自动进入下一个课程，三是增加无辅助练习模式。此外，还提出增加“咖啡订阅”选项以支持开发者。
  - roydivision：希望增加吉他支持。

• [其他体验反馈]
  - palla89：对应用使用C,D,E等音符而不是实际音符表示困惑，并询问是否可以更改。
  - block_dagger：指出应用商店描述中的错别字。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：
  - xlii提到音符是否随机生成的问题，认为有时音符组合不和谐，建议利用LLM（语言模型）生成更和谐的音符序列。
  
• 其他值得注意的讨论点：
  - LVB询问麦克风输入在复杂练习中的效果，以及是否需要购买经济实惠的MIDI键盘以获得更好的练习体验。
  - tianshuo表示愿意帮助开发者改进应用，并提供了联系方式。
  - xlii分享了自己的特殊教育需求，并表示应用帮助其建立了眼肌链接，展现了应用对不同用户需求的适应性。

data.title: Researchers search for more precise ways to measure pain
data.author: Petiver
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：疼痛的主观性、测量方法及其在医学实践中的应用

不同观点：
• [j_bum] 认为疼痛包含感觉辨别和情感情绪两个主要成分，且两者可以独立或同时发生。他质疑基于生物标志物的疼痛测量，特别是对情感情绪成分的测量，担心这会使医生更加怀疑患者的主观疼痛体验，尤其对主要经历情感成分的患者不利。他还提到医疗系统中对患者疼痛的不信任问题，例如女性和药物滥用历史患者更易被忽视。

• [GarnetFloride] 强调急性和慢性疼痛的区别，并指出不同性别对疼痛的反应差异。他认为医生对男性疼痛的重视程度高于女性，尤其是有色人种女性的疼痛常被忽视。他还提到，描述疼痛对工作的影响比其他描述更能引起医生的注意。

• [PaulKeeble] 提出在实际医疗中，疼痛评分6是患者获得医疗关注的最佳数值。他指出，由于缺乏生物标志物和阿片类药物的撤回，许多慢性疼痛患者得不到有效治疗，医疗系统中对疼痛的偏见和污名化严重。

• [gaoshan] 分享了跨文化描述疼痛的困难，指出在不同文化中对疼痛的描述可能不被医生理解，这可能影响疼痛评估和治疗。

• [lijok] 强调准确的疼痛测量机制在兽医学中的重要性，指出由于缺乏准确的疼痛评估，许多动物被过早地安乐死，主人常常怀疑是否决定过早。

• [shadowtree] 强调疼痛的时间维度对慢性疼痛评估的重要性，指出持续和一致的疼痛会引发严重的心理和生理反应，这种体验难以被外人理解。

• [perching_aix] 认为尽管疼痛测量技术尚不完善，但发展这些技术是必要的。他担心未来可能出现因设备无法检测到疼痛而引发争议的情况。

• [pugworthy] 分享了自身经历，指出在心脏病发作时对疼痛评分的不确定性，并提到医生对疼痛评分的不同看法。

• [Fin_Code] 认为患者对疼痛的自我报告本质上是不可靠的，因为疼痛是相对的，受个人经验和耐受力影响。

• [_DeadFred_] 指出即使有了疼痛测量工具，人们的反应可能仍然是漠不关心，并分享了个人对母亲慢性疼痛的忽视经历，质疑疼痛测量的实际意义。

• [m3kw9] 认为心理因素可以放大疼痛感受，例如对针头的恐惧会使实际疼痛更严重。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于如何客观有效地测量疼痛，特别是情感情绪成分的疼痛，以及如何在医疗实践中减少对患者疼痛的不信任和偏见。
- 跨文化和跨性别对疼痛的理解和描述差异也是讨论的重要部分。
- 疼痛测量技术的发展及其在兽医学和人类医学中的应用前景被认为是具有革命性潜力的，但也伴随着实际应用中的挑战和争议。

data.title: CO2 laser enables long-range detection of radioactive material
data.author: EA-3167
data.article_summary: 研究团队使用短脉冲CO₂激光器实现了距离放射性物质10米远的远程探测，这一距离比以往方法远十倍以上。传统探测器如盖革计数器只能在放射性物质附近检测其释放的粒子，而新方法通过检测空气电离产生的带电粒子进行远距离探测。CO₂激光引发电子雪崩效应，生成微等离子体并散射激光，通过测量散射光实现探测。该技术在核灾难响应和核安全领域具有潜力，未来可能扩展到超过100米的探测距离，但CO₂激光器的体积较大，现场应用仍具挑战。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于研究论文中提出的微等离子体辐射检测方法的可行性、应用及其局限性

不同观点：
• [adrian_b] 分享了研究论文的免费预印本链接，介绍了利用微等离子体和CMOS相机进行辐射检测的技术。

• [PaulHoule] 提到该技术让他联想到可以在大气压下工作的**电离室**，暗示可能存在其他类似技术，该技术并非全新概念。

• [magnat] 对论文中描述的"远程探测"提出质疑，指出由于CMOS相机必须靠近辐射源放置，质疑该技术是否能真正称为**长距离探测器**。这是对技术应用范围的批评。

• [ziknard] 以轻松的语气指出，该技术可能很容易被简单的物理屏障（如大号塑料容器）**阻挡**，暗示其在实际应用中的局限性。

• [ggm] 以调侃语气表示**TSA（美国运输安全管理局）**可能会购买这种技术，暗示其在安检等领域的潜在应用价值。

• [keepamovin] 表示自己早就预料到这种技术是可行的，暗示对该研究结果并不意外，可能认为该技术创新性不足。

• [neuroelectron] 表示自己不是核科学专家，但对该技术被描述为一种**基础的辐射检测方式**感到疑惑，质疑为何这种方法没有更早被发现和应用，涉及到对技术原创性和发现时间的疑问。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于该技术是否真的能称为**长距离探测器**，特别是[magnat]对文中描述的"远程 sensing"提出了直接质疑。
• 其他评论多以调侃和质疑为主，涉及到技术的实际应用效果和创新性，如[ziknard]对技术易被阻挡的批评和[ggm]对TSA采购的调侃。
• [neuroelectron]的评论则反映了对该技术基础性和发现时间的疑问，暗示可能存在对研究创新性的高期待。

43441082.article_content:
Detectors and sensors
Detectors and sensors
Research update
CO
2
laser enables long-range detection of radioactive material
19 Mar 2025
Remote detection
The ability to locate radioactive material at distances greater than the range of emitted particles could play an important role in nuclear disaster response and nuclear security. (Courtesy: Shutterstock/fewerton)
Researchers have demonstrated that they can remotely detect radioactive material from 10 m away using short-pulse CO
2
lasers – a distance over ten times farther than achieved via previous methods.
Conventional radiation detectors, such as Geiger counters, detect particles that are emitted by the radioactive material, typically limiting their operational range to the material’s direct vicinity. The new method, developed by a research team headed up at the
University of Maryland
, instead leverages the ionization in the surrounding air, enabling detection from much greater distances.
The study may one day lead to remote sensing technologies that could be used in nuclear disaster response and nuclear security.
Using atmospheric ionization
Radioactive materials emit particles – such as alpha, beta or gamma particles – that can ionize air molecules, creating free electrons and negative ions. These charged particles are typically present at very low concentrations, making them difficult to detect.
Senior author
Howard Milchberg
and colleagues – also from Brookhaven National Laboratory, Los Alamos National Laboratory and Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory – demonstrated that CO
2
lasers could accelerate these charged particles, causing them to collide with neutral gas molecules, in turn creating further ionization. These additional free charges would then undergo the same laser-induced accelerations and collisions, leading to a cascade of charged particles.
This effect, known as “electron avalanche breakdown”, can create microplasmas that scatter laser light. By measuring the profile of the backscattered light, researchers can detect the presence of radioactive material.
The team tested their technique using a 3.6-mCi polonium-210 alpha particle source at a standoff distance of 10 m, significantly longer than previous experiments that used different types of lasers and electromagnetic radiation sources.
“The results are highly impressive,” comments
EunMi Choi
from the Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology in South Korea. Choi’s team had used a
gyrotron source to detect radioactive materials
back in 2017.
“The researchers successfully demonstrated 10-m standoff detection of radioactive material, significantly surpassing the previous range of approximately 1 m,” she says.
Milchberg and collaborators had previously used a
mid-infrared laser in a similar experiment
in 2019. Changing to a long-wavelength (9.2 μm) CO
2
laser brought significant advantages, he says.
“You can’t use any laser to do this cascading breakdown process,” Milchberg explains. The CO
2
laser’s wavelength was able to enhance the avalanche process, while being low energy enough to not create its own ionization sources. “CO
2
is sort of the limit for long wavelengths on powerful lasers and it turns out CO
2
lasers are very, very efficient as well,” he says. “So this is like a sweet spot.”
Imaging microplasmas
The team also used a CMOS camera to capture visible-light emissions from the microplasmas. Milchberg says that this fluorescence around radioactive sources resembled balls of plasma, indicating the localized regions where electron avalanche breakdowns had occurred.
By counting these “plasma balls” and calibrating them against the backscattered laser signal, the researchers could link fluorescence intensity to the density of ionization in the air, and use that to determine the type of radiation source.
The CMOS imagers, however, had to be placed close to the measured radiation source, reducing their applicability to remote sensing. “Although fluorescence imaging is not practical for field deployment due to the need for close-range cameras, it provides a valuable calibration tool,” Milchberg says.
Scaling to longer distances
The researchers believe their method can be extended to standoff distances exceeding 100 m. The primary limitation is the laser’s focusing geometry, which would affect the regions in which it could trigger an avalanche breakdown. A longer focal length would require a larger laser aperture but could enable kilometre-scale detection.
Choi points out, however, that deploying a CO
2
laser may be difficult in real-world applications. “A CO₂ laser is a bulky system, making it challenging to deploy in a portable manner in the field,” she says, adding that mounting the laser for long-range detection may be a solution.

data.title: Mruby/C and picoruby: high level langs in low-level devices?
data.author: rahil627
data.article_summary: PicoRuby 是一个专为单片微控制器设计的微型 Ruby 实现，具有小巧的资源占用（ROM 256 KB，RAM 128 KB 或更少）和高度的可移植性，依赖标准 C 库。它支持 Raspberry Pi Pico 等微控制器板，并提供 API 文档和演示视频。PicoRuby 基于 mruby/c 虚拟机，可用于 PRK Firmware 等项目，并可通过 WebAssembly 运行。其构建需要 C 工具链和 Ruby 3.0 以上版本，支持交叉编译。项目仍在开发中，采用 MIT 许可，并受到 Ruby Association 资助。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在微控制器上使用高级语言的优缺点，以及对具体语言如MicroPython、picoruby等的评价和选择。

不同观点：
• [throwaway81523] 认为MicroPython非常流行，并且适用于能够处理它的设备，如具有256KB闪存和32KB RAM的设备。他还提到其他语言如Lua、Hedgehog Lisp和uLisp，并建议在资源非常有限的情况下使用Forth或交叉编译语言以避免垃圾回收机制。

• [jononor] 表示喜欢MicroPython开发，尤其因为它容易与C语言结合使用。他认为在微控制器开发中，有时需要使用低级语言来充分利用设备性能。

• [aidog] 对picoruby非常感兴趣，认为它是mruby/C的更小实现，并分享了一个关于在Raspberry Pi Pico上运行Ruby REPL的视频链接，展示了picoruby在其他微控制器上的移植。

• [calebh] 介绍了自己开发的Juniper语言，强调在小型设备上运行高级代码的可能性，包括在栈上分配闭包等技术细节。

• [xutopia] 提供了picoruby的文档链接，供有兴趣的人进一步查阅。

• [TkTech] 再次推荐MicroPython，指出它在该领域目前占据主导地位，并提供了GitHub链接。

• [rahil627] 提出一些人不喜欢C语言，而另一些人则拥抱并热爱它。他质疑在微控制器上使用复杂语言如Ruby的必要性，并表示对pico实现的维护感到欣慰。

• [actionfromafar] 提到了Shedskin Python到C++编译器，作为一个相关的工具选项。

• [bsder] 认为256KB ROM和128KB RAM并不算小，指出这比1990年前大多数计算机的存储容量还大，并提到RAM和闪存的大小直接影响微控制器的价格。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是C语言的使用。有些人不喜欢C语言，而另一些人则认为它是充分利用微控制器性能的必要工具。
• 对不同语言在微控制器上的适用性存在不同看法，例如MicroPython的流行度与picoruby的小巧实现，以及在资源非常有限情况下的最佳选择。
• 讨论中还涉及历史和经济因素，如存储容量与价格的关系，这影响了语言选择和硬件设计。

PicoRuby
PicoRuby is an alternative mruby implementation which is:
Small foot print
ROM: 256 KB (depending on build config)
RAM: 128 KB or less (depending on app code)
(Figures in 32 bit architecture)
Portable
Depends on only standard C library such as glibc, Newlib or Newlib-nano
Reference microcontroller boards
Raspberry Pi Pico - Arm Cortex-M0+, 264 KB RAM, 2 MB Flash
API documentation with some demo videos
https://picoruby.github.io/
Depends on
mruby/c (mrubyc/mrubyc)
: Another implementation of mruby virtual machine

PRK Firmware
: Keyboard firmware for Raspberry Pi Pico

43451760.article_summary: PicoRuby 是一个专为单片微控制器设计的微型 Ruby 实现，具有小巧的资源占用（ROM 256 KB，RAM 128 KB 或更少）和高度的可移植性，依赖标准 C 库。它支持 Raspberry Pi Pico 等微控制器板，并提供 API 文档和演示视频。PicoRuby 基于 mruby/c 虚拟机，可用于 PRK Firmware 等项目，并可通过 WebAssembly 运行。其构建需要 C 工具链和 Ruby 3.0 以上版本，支持交叉编译。项目仍在开发中，采用 MIT 许可，并受到 Ruby Association 资助。

data.title: Gemini 2.5 Pro reasons about task feasibility
data.author: intellectronica
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者尝试使用AI模型Gemini 2.5 Pro创建一个虚拟合成器，目标是重现90年代末的ReBirth RB-338合成器。然而，AI经过分析后认为该任务过于复杂，无法一次性完成，并详细解释了原因，包括项目所需的专业知识和开发时间。不同于一般AI的失败尝试，Gemini主动停止了任务，并建议提供一个简化的概念起点，包括基本代码和UI元素。经过协商，AI最终生成了一个简化但可运行的合成器。这一行为展示了AI在判断任务可行性方面的进步。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在处理复杂任务、生成创意内容及面对无法直接解决的问题时的表现和潜力

不同观点：
• **SimonW**：分享了自己使用Gemini 2.5 Pro处理复杂编码任务的积极体验，并提供了具体例子，但也提到在公开平台分享这类成果存在被质疑的风险，如例子可能被认为是 trivial 或不现实的。
• **Tkgally**：受SimonW的启发，展示了Gemini 2.5 Pro生成音乐合成器的成果，并详细描述了生成过程和推理路径，强调了模型在创造性和意外性方面的潜力。
• **Wiz21c**：指出LLM与传统程序不同，由于输入空间巨大，用户难以完全探索其功能，因此LLM可以在很长一段时间内带来惊喜。
• **Jrvarela56**：提出未来LLM可以分解复杂请求为可处理的子请求，通过协调多个子组件来解决问题，并认为这是构建AGI（人工通用智能）的关键。
• **Ofirtwo**：关注LLM在无法通过参考用户解决智力任务时的表现，希望模型能深入探索问题并最终承认无法解答，而不是立即将问题抛回给用户。
• **Coolgoose**：幽默地建议下一步是教会LLM拖延。
• **Retrofuturism**：质疑某些任务被拒绝是否仅仅是由于系统提示决定了这些请求可能会消耗过多资源并导致失败。
• **Menzoic**：分享了GPT-4在零 shot 提示下进行类似“谈判”的经历，模型通过迭代方法继续任务。
• **Vladmdgolam**：提到在使用o1-pro生成回文时，模型会识别不可能的情况并给出具体例子。

补充讨论：
• **Trash_cat**：对输入提示的具体内容表示好奇，暗示提示的设计可能对结果有重要影响。

争议焦点：
• 对LLM生成结果的原创性和意外性的评价存在分歧，部分人认为模型可能只是重复已有知识（如StackOverflow上的内容），而其他人则强调其创造性和潜力。
• 关于LLM面对无法解决的问题时应如何表现，存在不同期待，部分人希望模型能深入探索并最终承认无法解答，而不是简单地将问题抛回用户。

... in which a surprisingly reflective AI tells me no (for good reasons) ...
Mar 26, 2025
Share this post

Share
After spending some time this morning generating various pictures of monkeys I got bored and decided to ask Gemini 2.5 Pro to create a virtual synthesizer for me. My initial ambition was to get a recreation of the famous ReBirth RB-338 virtual synth from the late 90s, and I have gathered a pretty good spec and instructed the AI to recreate it in HTML and Javascript.
What happened next is surprising and significant. Gemini did its “thinking” schtick. During its thinking session it reached the conclusion that this task is not feasible in one shot. It then stopped and explained that to me.
Thinking Excerpt:
…
Feasibility Assessment:
Creating a complete and fully working reproduction of ReBirth RB-338 is an enormous undertaking, likely requiring months or even years of development by an experienced team. It involves deep knowledge of digital signal processing (DSP), web audio APIs (like Tone.js), UI development, and the specific nuances of the original hardware ReBirth emulated.
Limitations:
Complexity: The scope is far beyond what can be generated in a single response. It's a full-scale software development project.
Accuracy: Achieving authentic emulation, especially for the TB-303 filter, is extremely challenging. Tone.js provides building blocks, but the specific tuning and interaction of components require significant DSP expertise.
…
Conclusion: It is not feasible to generate a complete, fully working reproduction of ReBirth RB-338 as requested in a single response. The complexity and scope are too large.
Alternative Approach:
I can provide a basic structural outline and some simplified example code snippets demonstrating key concepts using HTML, JavaScript, and Tone.js to illustrate how one might start building such a project. This would include:
Basic HTML structure.
Setting up Tone.js.
A very simplified representation of one TB-303-style synth with a few controls (e.g., cutoff, resonance).
A very simplified 16-step sequencer.
Basic UI elements (e.g., simple buttons/sliders).
This will not be a ReBirth clone, but rather a conceptual starting point.
…
I have never seen an LLM do this. Typically, if I request something that can’t be achieved, the AI will just try and fail miserably. Gemini 2.5 Pro’s ability to reason about what it can and cannot do is a powerful and important new type of behaviour.
Anyway, not one to take no for an answer, I negotiated, and Gemini did produce a simpler but nevertheless fully working and fun synthesizer.
Give it a try
.

data.title: All Clothing Is Handmade (2022)
data.author: panic
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了手工制作服装的特殊价值以及对成衣质量的误解。作者讲述了自己制作被子和衣服的经历，强调了定制服装的情感联系。文章指出，所有服装本质上都是手工制作的，无论是在家中自制还是工厂生产。作者批评了人们对廉价成衣质量的偏见，尤其是对来自某些国家的服装。文章解释，成衣质量的好坏取决于品牌在材料选择、剪裁、设计和生产速度等方面的决策，而非生产地工人的技能。文章最后质疑了对东亚国家服装生产能力的刻板印象，呼吁重新思考我们对成衣质量和生产者的评价方式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：服装质量、生产外包、自动化与手工制作的比较，以及服装行业的经济与社会影响。

不同观点：
• alabastervlog认为，现代服装质量下降，尤其是与20世纪中期的服装相比，现代商品的耐用性大打折扣，质疑官方通胀指标的准确性，怀疑所谓的经济进步只是商品变差的结果。
• andrewvc指出，手工制作的皮具等商品可以通过使用优质材料达到比大多数奢侈品牌更高的质量，但工业化生产通过机器大规模生产，虽然质量略低，但成本更可控。奢侈品牌可能故意让商品不那么耐用，以促进重复购买。
• squeedles分享了自制服装的经验，强调自制衣物虽然质量高且独特，但耗时长，难以规模化生产。同时指出现代工业化生产通过压缩成本牺牲了服装质量。
• fificon以男性内衣为例，指出现代商品设计似乎有意降低耐用性，怀疑是企业为了促进重复消费而做出的优化。
• tialaramex和aeneasmackenzie讨论了服装生产中的自动化与人工参与，指出虽然一些步骤已经机械化，但人工仍然在服装制造的多个环节中不可或缺。

• AStonesThrow表达了对现代服装质量的失望，指出新衣服的质量差且难以修复，认为现代消费品设计上存在促使快速更换的倾向。

• 外包和全球化生产对服装质量的影响是多个评论者关注的焦点，特别是第一世界和第三世界工人的待遇和技能比较。
• 奢侈品牌是否故意降低产品耐用性以增加销售是另一个争议点，部分评论者认为这是企业策略的一部分。
• 服装生产的自动化与手工制作之间的质量和成本差异被详细讨论，特别是手工制作在现代消费文化中的位置。

43450515.article_content:
All Clothing Is Handmade
2022-10-29
quilts
The idea for this quilt came to me several years ago. Besides making quilts, I make some of my own clothes and occasionally make clothes for people in my life. I made my own wedding dress and one for a college friend as well (and never doing that again).
There’s something special nowadays about something that was made or tailored just for you, whether it was done by a friend/family member or something you had made. When I was a kid, my father gave my mother a birthday gift of what was essentially a copy of her favorite dress, made by a local seamstress. The style was pretty basic, but not being sold in stores at that time. I’m sure it was quite expensive. It was very thoughtful, she loved and wore the dress for ages, until her cancer surgeries made its fit uncomfortable.
But while I love the personal connections of bespoke/self-made clothing, I want to push back a bit against some language that occurs when people (myself included) talk about store-bought clothing, especially cheaper clothing. Whether it’s the nice Lands End flannel shirt I’m wearing as I write this, or the one my husband is wearing that I made for him, or the TikTok influencer’s Shein t-shirt that rips when she tries it on… all clothing is handmade.
I made this quilt using worn textiles from friends, family, and some folks in my church and scraps from my own projects. It’s got a piece of fabric from my wedding dress and others from one of my mom’s favorite dresses. There’s a couple of my husband’s old dress shirts, bits of my father’s ties, the lining of my little sister’s worn jacket, highlights from a friend’s tunic, bits of baby dresses, another friend’s dress shirt, and more. There’s a couple little pieces of leftover fabric from that same flannel shirt my husband is wearing right now.
I pieced it ages ago, I can’t quite even remember… 2020? It’s a wonky quilt, dozens of fabrics that were never meant to sit side-by-side. A little leather just for fun and frustration. It took forever to figure out how I wanted to quilt it (large stitches with long strokes, colors matching as best I could in the blocks themselves) and then to get to it, but I’m very glad that it’s done and I can share it now.
Who Controls Clothing’s Quality
21st century textile production happens on a massive scale, one that keeps ramping up and has enormous environmental costs. The quality of mass-market textiles has dropped noticeably since the 1990s, which were also a noticeable drop from the 1970s.
When people talk about this change in quality, the language often carries a set of assumptions. These assumptions are often both geographically and racially coded. “This t-shirt was made in Honduras” or “This blouse was made in Cambodia” imply things about their quality and often subtly, sometimes not-so-subtly, attached to the people actually doing the work.
But even if one assessed ten thousand blouses made in Cambodia for their quality, any negative findings say nothing about the talents or potential of Cambodian garment workers as a whole or relate to, say, American garment workers. What they reflect instead are:
The brand’s choice of materials:
Where did the cloth come from and how was it made?
What kind of thread are they using? (Thread can make a major difference in the longevity of a garment. The recent trend of lowering thread quality to save money is why the crotch of your new pants split after a month when the last pair you got of these same pants lasted a solid 5 years.)
The cutting setup:
How many layers of fabric are being cut together?
How much time do the workers have to operate cutting tools?
How likely are things to slip and slide during the cutting process?
The actual garment design. Before a garment is made, especially in a mass-production context, decisions about construction need to be made including:
How are the seams finished?
What’s the stitch length?
How are buttons attached?
The speed at which it is being made:
Is the garment worker sewing 30 seams an hour? 60? 100?
What happens when there’s an error?
What kind of breaks does the worker get? Really?

43450515.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了手工制作服装的特殊价值以及对成衣质量的误解。作者讲述了自己制作被子和衣服的经历，强调了定制服装的情感联系。文章指出，所有服装本质上都是手工制作的，无论是在家中自制还是工厂生产。作者批评了人们对廉价成衣质量的偏见，尤其是对来自某些国家的服装。文章解释，成衣质量的好坏取决于品牌在材料选择、剪裁、设计和生产速度等方面的决策，而非生产地工人的技能。文章最后质疑了对东亚国家服装生产能力的刻板印象，呼吁重新思考我们对成衣质量和生产者的评价方式。

争议焦点：
• 现代商品质量下降的原因是通胀计算不准确还是生产商故意降低质量以增加利润。
• 外包生产对工人和商品质量的影响，以及全球化生产中的道德问题。

data.article_summary: 柏林马里恩多夫的ringberlin校区正在建设欧洲最大的创客空间，由硬件加速器和硬科技创新中心MotionLab.Berlin运营。该项目占地17,000平方米，包含工坊、现代化机器设备、联合办公空间和测试区域，旨在促进研究、科学、创业和文化等领域的创新与合作。柏林市政府提供约3600万欧元资助，总投资额超过6000万欧元。该项目是柏林工业城市总体规划的一部分，旨在通过创新和合作推动工业生产发展，并将成为循环经济的典范。创客空间还将推动硬科技和深科技的创新，助力柏林成为国际工业中心。

Skip to main content

Europe’s largest makerspace
Berlin, 21 March 2025 –
The future is being shaped in Berlin in Mariendorf, among other places, more precisely on the
ringberlin
model campus. In Hall 2, a collaborative startup centre is currently being built, Europe’s largest makerspace for founders, startups, SMEs and many other creators.  It has now been announced who the operator of the new makerspace will be. The leading national hardware accelerator and renowned hard-tech innovation hub
MotionLab.Berlin
will be taking on this promising project in the future.
A lot of potential in a lot of space: With 17,000 m², the listed Hall 2, with its impressive combination of existing and new buildings, offers stakeholders from research, science, entrepreneurship, business, culture and politics, among others, sufficient space to launch innovations, enter into collaborations and engage in dialogue with one another. The aim of the new campus is to make future-oriented synergies visible and usable. Users have access to ideal conditions with workshops, a modern machine infrastructure, coworking and office space, maker garages and test areas. Direct access to Berlin’s public transport, e-mobility services and sharing concepts should also enable the community to reach the site as car-free as possible and to use it in an environmentally friendly manner. Hall 2 is currently being modernised and expanded in accordance with its status as a listed building, providing more than 5,000 people with innovative space for thought and action. For this purpose, the State of Berlin, through the
Senate Department for Economic Affairs, Energy and Public Enterprises
, is providing GRW funds amounting to around 36 million Euro to promote the regional economic structure. The total investment volume amounts to more than 60 million Euro.
The new operator MotionLab.Berlin was announced in the presence of the State Secretary Dr. Severin Fischer, the
District Mayor of Tempelhof-Schöneberg Jörn Oltmann
and the CEO of Berlin Partner Dr. Stefan Franzke at the venue itself.
Dr. Stefan Franzke, Managing Director of Berlin Partner, expressed his satisfaction: “It is great to see how ringberlin is increasingly gaining appeal. The planned makerspace will soon be one of the largest startup centres in Europe. In the future, decisive impulses and innovations will emanate from here that will further strengthen Berlin as an international industrial centre. Berlin Partner has supported the projects of ringberlin and MotionLab from the very beginning. We are therefore all the more pleased about the joint project and look forward to further cooperation for the Berlin location.”
As a leading ecosystem, MotionLab.Berlin drives deep tech innovation and major technological developments. The Innovation Hub offers companies access to infrastructure and a suitable environment to implement projects and develop professionally. The aim of Co-founder and Managing Partner Fridtjof Gustavs is to create an open and CO2-neutral campus with the new makerspace, where hard-tech and deep-tech innovations are brought from the launch pad to the road to success.
ringberlin is part of the
Masterplan Industrial City Berlin (MPI).
The MPI was updated by the Berlin Senate in August 2022 for the period 2022 to 2026 and aims to promote the development of industrial production in Berlin through innovation, cooperation and networking as well as the creation of suitable framework conditions. As a flagship project of the MPI, ringberlin is set to become a representative example of circular economy with a supra-regional impact. A fitting
MPI Deep Dive entitled “Circular Value Creation in the Construction Industry,”
held at ringberlin in July 2024, brought together key stakeholders and offered participants the opportunity to combine knowledge transfer and exchange.
The organisation in the form of conception, coordination and communication was supported by the
Coordination Office for Circular Economy, Energy Efficiency and Climate Protection in Companies (KEK)
and with the involvement of Berlin Partner.

data.title: How to protect your phone and data privacy at the US border
data.author: beardyw
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了如何在美国边境保护手机和数据隐私。由于宪法在边境地区的保护较弱，美国海关和边境保护局（CBP）可以检查你的设备，包括手机。为降低风险，专家建议：

1. **决定是否配合检查**：提前考虑是否愿意在入境时解锁手机。拒绝可能导致设备被没收或更长时间的盘查。
2. **关闭手机和面部识别**：入境前关闭手机和面部识别功能。
3. **不要擦除手机数据**：这可能引起怀疑。
4. **加密数据并使用强密码**：增加破解难度。
5. **将数据移至云存储**：减少本地存储的敏感信息。

每个人的风险评估不同，取决于移民身份、旅行历史和手机数据敏感性。提前准备可以有效保护隐私。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国边境数据隐私与安全问题，以及应对措施

不同观点：
• Latexr：担心无故被拘留的风险比数据隐私更大，建议不要前往美国，因为美国传达了不欢迎外来者的信号。
• Surac：将数据从手机转移到云端实际上还是将数据交给了美国，因为云服务仍在美国控制下。
• Btbuildem：提到有人因线上活动（如社交媒体帖子）被拘留，建议删除不常用的社交媒体账户，并质疑主要社交平台是否保留长期的删除记录供政府访问。
• Havoc：建议在"可疑国家"使用一次性手机，但认为即便如此，美国政府可能仍通过云端获取数据。
• Postepowanieadm：指出将数据存于云端使得政府无需物理接触设备即可获取数据。
• Londons_explore：提出将手机邮寄到美国，到达时使用一次性手机或不带手机，以避免数据被检查。
• Harvy9：认为不应从大众媒体获取技术建议，提到文章链接到的EFF（电子前沿基金会）更有参考价值。
• Beardyw：引用EFF律师的观点，认为应假设美国政府完全不可控，甚至无害的旅行也可能导致非公民的设备被搜查。
• Pluc：质疑为何一直提交无法阅读的链接。
• Timeon：认为非公民最安全的选择是避免前往特定国家（如美国）。
• Hoseja：讽刺英国人也提出类似观点。
• Mschuster91：建议欧盟、印度和中国对美国旅客实施类似措施，以让美国国会意识到问题严重性。
• Jamesgasek：个人经历表示最近通过提华纳海关时未遇到此类搜查，认为普通旅客不必过于担心。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于美国边境搜查和数据隐私的实际风险，部分人认为风险被夸大，而其他人则建议采取极端措施规避风险。
• 讨论中反复提到云存储和数据隐私的关系，以及如何在旅行时保护个人数据的不同策略。
• 部分评论质疑媒体报道的真实性和普遍性，并提到个人经历与媒体报道的差异。
• 还有建议通过国际反制措施向美国施加压力以改变政策。

How to protect your phone and data privacy at the US border
With reports of people being turned away at airports over messages found on devices, here’s what to do to minimize risks

Welcome to
Opt Out
, a semi-regular column in which we help you navigate your online privacy and show you how to say no to surveillance. The last column covered
what to do with your 23andMe account after the company filed bankruptcy
. If you’d like to skip to a section about a particular tip, click the “Jump to” menu at the top of this article.
If you’re a visa or green card holder with plans to travel to the US, reports of people being turned away at airports over messages found on their devices might be prompting you to second-guess your travel plans. You might be asking whether Customs and Border Protection (CBP) can search your phone, whether you can opt out and what you should do to minimize your risks.
The short answer is that yes, CBP can search your devices. Constitutional protections are generally weaker at US borders, including airports. You can try to opt out, but depending on your specific circumstances, you might not be willing to risk the potential ramifications of not complying, which can include the confiscation of your devices.
Privacy experts say everyone should conduct a personal risk assessment – which should include your immigration status, travel history and what data you might have on your phone. There’s not a one-size-fits all solution because data that may seem sensitive to some may not be to others, depending on your circumstances. That assessment might affect your calculus of whether to push back if CBP attempts to search your phone, for instance, or how much you want to lock down your devices before heading to the airport.

at an airport in Texas because immigration officers found texts that were critical of Trump on his phone.

If you’re a US citizen, you must be admitted into the country. That said, some jurisdictions allow CBP to work with the FBI or local police to advance domestic investigations, so there are still some risks of your devices being searched for domestic reasons.

Before you travel, start to prepare for the possibility of being pulled into secondary screening. data.title: Heap-overflowing Llama.cpp to RCE
data.author: retr0reg
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了作者Patrick Peng对Llama.cpp项目中的堆溢出到远程代码执行（RCE）漏洞的深入研究和利用过程。作者花费了约两周时间研究Llama.cpp的RPC和内存管理实现，发现其具有独特的堆管理系统，传统的ptmalloc利用方法无法奏效。在进一步的30小时研究中，作者探索了该项目的内存安全补丁和缓解措施，最终成功实现RCE。

Llama.cpp的RPC组件用于分布式大型语言模型推理，其内存管理系统基于glibc的malloc和ptmalloc，但针对张量处理进行了优化。作者详细描述了内存分配过程及其复杂性，包括通过alloc_buffer命令分配内存和处理Tensor数据结构。

尽管最初认为可以轻松利用write-what-where和read-what-where漏洞，但Llama.cpp的严格安全检查和整数溢出防护使得利用变得困难。经过不懈努力，作者最终找到了独特的利用方法，成功绕过所有防护。本文不仅展示了技术细节，还分享了作者在二进制漏洞研究中的乐趣和成就感。

data.title: Understanding DNS Resolution on Linux and Kubernetes
data.author: fanf2
data.article_summary:
本文探讨了Linux和Kubernetes上的DNS解析机制，特别是针对Kubernetes中出现的警告信息："DNSConfigForming ... Nameserver limits were exceeded, some nameservers have been omitted"。Kubernetes通过DNS进行服务发现，当创建服务如"foo"时，Kubernetes自动生成DNS记录（如foo.bar.svc.cluster.local），使得Pod可以通过该名称访问服务。

在Linux中，DNS配置主要通过`/etc/resolv.conf`文件进行，其中定义了 nameserver 和搜索域。系统默认只使用第一个nameserver，超时后才会尝试下一个。搜索域用于自动扩展不完全限定域名（如"hello"会依次尝试hello.example.com、hello.example.net等）。该文件有以下限制：最多3个nameserver、6个搜索域，以及可通过`ndots`选项调整查询行为。

此外，`/etc/nsswitch.conf`文件定义了系统解析主机名的顺序，包括本地文件（如`/etc/hosts`）、mDNS（如`.local`域名）和DNS。Kubernetes环境中的DNS问题通常涉及这些配置的交互和限制。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Unix系统中的DNS解析机制及相关配置的合理性，Kubernetes中的DNS使用，以及私有域名使用的规范性。

不同观点：
• [zokier] 认为传统的UNIX系统没有运行本地的DNS resolver守护进程，而是通过`resolv.conf`和`nsswitch.conf`文件进行配置，这种方式有些奇怪。他指出，使用守护进程不仅可以简化配置，还可以实现系统范围内的DNS缓存，这在过去网络速度较慢的时代应该更有价值。同时，他觉得名称解析被嵌入到libc中显得不太寻常，因为Unix系统通常为各种功能都提供了守护进程。

• [szszrk] 讨论了Kubernetes中DNS解析的一个具体现象，即它会将A-B-C-D.N.pod.cluster.local解析为A.B.C.D，只要A.B.C.D是一个有效的IP地址且N是一个存在的命名空间。他对这种设计的实际用途表示困惑，并提出几个可能的用途，包括测试奇怪的DNS配置、为TLS证书颁发提供支持（尽管某些服务如Let's Encrypt禁止这种做法），以及在反向代理配置中使用单一IP和端口为多个服务提供支持。

• [AndyMcConachie] 则关注私有域名的使用，指出人们不应使用`.local`或`.dev`作为私有域名。他解释说，`.dev`是一个实际的顶级域名（TLD），而`.local`是用于多播DNS的。他提到ICANN已经声明永远不会将`.internal`委派出去，并建议使用`.internal`作为私有用途。他还表明自己是一份关于此问题的Internet草案的合著者，因此存在一定偏见。

补充讨论：
- Kubernetes的DNS解析机制引发的实际用途讨论，尤其是对复杂DNS配置和TLS证书颁发的支持。
- 关于私有域名使用的规范性问题，尤其是`.local`、`.dev`和`.internal`的选择与ICANN的政策。
- 对UNIX系统中DNS解析设计的历史背景和替代方案的思考，特别是为何名称解析被嵌入到libc而不是通过守护进程实现。

43451861.article_content:
~jpetazzo/
Understanding DNS resolution on Linux and Kubernetes
Tweet
I recently investigated a warning message on Kubernetes that said:
DNSConfigForming ... Nameserver limits were exceeded, some nameservers have been omitted
. This was technically a Kubernetes
event
with
type: Warning
, and these usually indicate that there’s something wrong, so I wanted to investigate it.
This led me down a pretty deep rabbit hole about DNS resolution on Linux in general and Kubernetes in particular. I thought it might be helpful to others to explain how this all works, just in case you have to troubleshoot a DNS issue some day (and as we now,
it’s always DNS
) on Linux or on Kubernetes.
Kubernetes DNS in theory
Kubernetes provides DNS-based service discovery. When we create a service named
foo
in namespace
bar
, Kubernetes creates a DNS entry,
foo.bar.svc.cluster.local
, that resolves to that service’s
ClusterIP
.
Any pod in the cluster can resolve
foo.bar
or
foo.bar.svc
and obtain that service’s
ClusterIP
. Any pod in the same
bar
namespace can even just resolve
foo
to obtain that
ClusterIP
.
This means that when we write code that will run on Kubernetes, if we need to connect to a database, we can put
db
as the database name (instead of hardcoding an IP address) or e.g.
db.prod
if we want to connect to service
db
in namespace
prod
.
This is convenient, because a similar mechanism exists in e.g. Docker Compose; which means that we can write code, test it with Docker Compose, and run it in Kubernetes without changing a single line of code. Cool.
Now, how does that work behind the scenes?
DNS resolution on Linux (level 1: resolv.conf)
At a first glance, DNS resolution on Linux is configured through
/etc/resolv.conf
. A typical
resolv.conf
file can look like this:
nameserver 192.168.1.1
nameserver 192.168.1.2
search example.com example.net
This defines two DNS servers (for redundancy purposes; but in many cases you will only have one) as well as a “search list”. This means that if we try to resolve the name
hello
, here is what will happen:
first, we look for
hello.example.com
if that name doesn’t exist, we look for
hello.example.net
if that name doesn’t exist, we look for
hello
if that name doesn’t exist, we report an error (like
Name or service not known
)
By default, only the first name server is used. The other name servers are queried only if the first one times out. This means that all name servers must serve exactly the same records. You cannot have, for instance, one name server for internal domains, and another one for external domains! If you send a query to the first server, and that server replies with “not found” (technically, an NXDOMAIN reply), the second server will not be queried - the “not found” error will be reported right away.
(Note: it is possible to use the option
rotate
, in which case name servers are queried in round-robin order to spread the query load. Name servers still need to have the same records, though; otherwise DNS replies might be inconsistent and that will cause some
very weird
errors down the line.)
There are some limits and “fine print”:
we can specify up to 3 name servers (additional name servers will be ignored);
we can specify up to 6 search domains;
the
ndots
option can be used to change whether (and when) to try the search list first, or an “initial absolute query” (i.e.
hello
without the search domain).
You can see extra details in the
resolv.conf(5)
man page, which explains for instance how to change timeout values, number of retries, and that kind of stuff.
DNS resolution on Linux (level 2: nsswitch.conf)
Perhaps you’ve come across
.local
names. For instance, on my LAN at home, I can ping the machine named
zagreb
with
ping zagreb.local
:
$ ping -4 zagreb.local
PING zagreb.local (10.0.0.30) 56(84) bytes of data.
64 bytes from 10.0.0.30: icmp_seq=1 ttl=64 time=2.16 ms
...

http
,
ftp
,

to port numbers and vice versa)

files
, which means
/etc/hosts
(that’s why we can hard-code some name and IP addresses in that file!);
mymachines
, which is something used for
systemd-machined
containers;
myhostname
, whi
43451861.article_summary:
本文探讨了Linux和Kubernetes上的DNS解析机制，特别是针对Kubernetes中出现的警告信息："DNSConfigForming ... Nameserver limits were exceeded, some nameservers have been omitted"。Kubernetes通过DNS进行服务发现，当创建服务如"foo"时，Kubernetes自动生成DNS记录（如foo.bar.svc.cluster.local），使得Pod可以通过该名称访问服务。

在Linux中，DNS配置主要通过`/etc/resolv.conf`文件进行，其中定义了 nameserver 和搜索域。系统默认只使用第一个nameserver，超时后才会尝试下一个。搜索域用于自动扩展不完全限定域名（如"hello"会依次尝试hello.example.com、hello.example.net等）。该文件有以下限制：最多3个nameserver、6个搜索域，以及可通过`ndots`选项调整查询行为。

此外，`/etc/nsswitch.conf`文件定义了系统解析主机名的顺序，包括本地文件（如`/etc/hosts`）、mDNS（如`.local`域名）和DNS。Kubernetes环境中的DNS问题通常涉及这些配置的交互和限制。
43451861.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Unix系统中的DNS解析机制及相关配置的合理性，Kubernetes中的DNS使用，以及私有域名使用的规范性。

不同观点：
• [zokier] 认为传统的UNIX系统没有运行本地的DNS resolver守护进程，而是通过`resolv.conf`和`nsswitch.conf`文件进行配置，这种方式有些奇怪。他指出，使用守护进程不仅可以简化配置，还可以实现系统范围内的DNS缓存，这在过去网络速度较慢的时代应该更有价值。同时，他觉得名称解析被嵌入到libc中显得不太寻常，因为Unix系统通常为各种功能都提供了守护进程。

• [szszrk] 讨论了Kubernetes中DNS解析的一个具体现象，即它会将A-B-C-D.N.pod.cluster.local解析为A.B.C.D，只要A.B.C.D是一个有效的IP地址且N是一个存在的命名空间。他对这种设计的实际用途表示困惑，并提出几个可能的用途，包括测试奇怪的DNS配置、为TLS证书颁发提供支持（尽管某些服务如Let's Encrypt禁止这种做法），以及在反向代理配置中使用单一IP和端口为多个服务提供支持。

• [AndyMcConachie] 则关注私有域名的使用，指出人们不应使用`.local`或`.dev`作为私有域名。他解释说，`.dev`是一个实际的顶级域名（TLD），而`.local`是用于多播DNS的。他提到ICANN已经声明永远不会将`.internal`委派出去，并建议使用`.internal`作为私有用途。他还表明自己是一份关于此问题的Internet草案的合著者，因此存在一定偏见。

补充讨论：
- Kubernetes的DNS解析机制引发的实际用途讨论，尤其是对复杂DNS配置和TLS证书颁发的支持。
- 关于私有域名使用的规范性问题，尤其是`.local`、`.dev`和`.internal`的选择与ICANN的政策。
- 对UNIX系统中DNS解析设计的历史背景和替代方案的思考，特别是为何名称解析被嵌入到libc而不是通过守护进程实现。

data.title: Jeffrey Goldberg on the Group Chat That Broke the Internet
data.author: marban
data.article_summary: 《大西洋月刊》主编杰弗里·戈德堡意外通过Signal应用收到来自一位自称“迈克尔·沃尔兹”的消息，后者与特朗普总统的国家安全顾问同名。随后，他被加入一个涉及高级政府官员的群聊，讨论对也门胡塞武装的军事行动。尽管起初怀疑是恶作剧，但随着多名内阁官员加入讨论，并准备进行实际军事打击，戈德堡意识到这可能是真实的。国家安全委员会发言人事后证实了该聊天组的真实性。这一事件引发对国防官员通过非正式渠道讨论重要军事决策的关注。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对“broke the internet”这一表达的看法以及是否应由政府机构开发专用的安全通信平台

不同观点：
• [对“broke the internet”这一表达的反感]：chilmers 表示不喜欢“broke the internet”这个短语，暗示这个表达被过度使用或令人厌烦。虽然没有详细解释原因，但可以推测这种表达可能被认为夸大其实或过于流行化。

• [对政府使用DARPA或NSA开发通信平台的质疑]：hnpolicestate 提出一个问题，询问为什么美国不使用DARPA或NSA开发一个专为政府高官使用的非商业移动通信平台。他暗示对Signal这类现有平台的信任度存在怀疑，特别是怀疑它们是否与政府有不当联系。这反映出对现有加密通信工具的不信任，和对政府开发自有平台的支持。

补充讨论：
• [对Signal的怀疑]：hnpolicestate 提到Signal是否与政府有勾结，表明一些用户对商业通信平台的安全性和独立性存在疑虑，尤其是在涉及政府通信时。

• [技术理解的局限]：hnpolicestate 也提到自己可能不够技术性，无法理解为何不开发自有平台。这显示出讨论者对技术实现和政府决策过程缺乏了解，反映出公众对复杂技术问题与政府决策之间关系的困惑。

争议焦点：
• 争议的焦点在于是否应由政府机构开发专用的安全通信平台，以及对现有平台如Signal的不信任。部分人可能认为政府有能力开发更安全的平台，而另一些人可能对政府参与技术开发持怀疑态度，或者认为现有平台已经足够安全和独立。

总结：讨论中出现了对流行表达的个人反感，以及对政府开发通信平台的呼吁与质疑，特别是对现有通信工具的不信任构成了争议的核心。

It’s happened to the best of us. We mistakenly send a text about a colleague we are mad at to that very colleague. We accidentally include our mom on the sibling text chain about our mom. Today on
Radio Atlantic
, a much higher-stakes texting error:
The
Atlantic
’s editor in chief,
Jeffrey Goldberg,
received a connection request on Signal from a “Michael Waltz,” which is the name of President Donald Trump’s national security adviser. Two days later, he was added to a group text with top administration officials created for the purpose of coordinating high-level national-security conversations about the Houthis in Yemen. On March 15, Goldberg sat in his car in a grocery-store parking lot waiting to see if the strike would actually happen. The bombs fell. The text thread had to be real.
We talk with Goldberg about this absurd chain of events, and with Shane Harris, who covers national security for
The
Atlantic
, about what it means that defense officials were discussing detailed war plans on a text chain.
The following is a transcript of the episode:
Hanna Rosin:
On March 15, the U.S. began a bombing campaign against Houthi groups in Yemen. A couple of hours before that, our editor in chief, Jeffrey Goldberg, sat in his car in a supermarket parking lot, waiting to see if and when the attack would start. How he knew about this military campaign is a very weird story. Not long ago, Jeff was added to a text chain of very important people in the administration. Presumably, he was added to it by accident.
I know, it happens to the best of us—but there was the editor of
The Atlantic
monitoring the back-and-forth between Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, Vice President J. D. Vance, and others, wondering:
Could this possibly be real?
In fact, Brian Hughes, the spokesman for the National Security Council, later confirmed that it was indeed all real. I’m Hanna Rosin. This is
Radio Atlantic
, and today, we have on the show editor in chief Jeffrey Goldberg and staff writer Shane Harris, who covers national security, to explain what happened and what it might mean.
Jeff, welcome to the show.
Jeffrey Goldberg:
Hey, Hanna.
Rosin:
Hi, Shane.
Shane Harris:
Hi.
Rosin:
Jeff, on Tuesday, March 11, you get a Signal message from a user identified as Michael Waltz, which is also the name of President Trump’s national security adviser. Where are you when you get this message, and what are you thinking?
Goldberg:
Weirdly and randomly, I was in Salzburg, Austria, and what I’m thinking is not much, because in my line of work, that wouldn’t be the craziest thing to happen.
Rosin:
Like, it could be him; it could be someone pretending to be him. You’re not that fussed.
Goldberg:
Well, I am always cautious about people reaching out across social media or messaging apps.
I don’t assume that they’re the person that the name suggests, but I would have to say that I was glad, also, and I was hoping that it was the actual Michael Waltz, because I’d like to be in regular contact with Michael Waltz for all the obvious journalistic reasons.
Rosin:
Right. So you’re like,
Oh, maybe he has a scoop for me.
Goldberg:
Yeah.
Rosin:
Okay, so then what happens next? You’re going about your life, going about your business, and …
Goldberg:
And then I get added to a group, a Signal group—you know, a text-messaging chat group—called “Houthi PC small group.”
PC
I know from covering White House issues, you know: “Principals Committee,” basically the top leaders of Cabinet departments generally associated with national-security issues, and then a message from Mike Waltz talking about how he’s putting together this PC small group to talk about the Houthis, because something’s gonna be happening over the next 72 hours. That’s when I sort of think—I mean, honestly, the first thing I thought was:
I’m really being spoofed.
Like, somebody is—this is a hoax. This is a state or nonstate actor, probably nonstate actor, looking to entrap, embarrass, whatever word you wanna use, a journalist.
Rosin:
Right. So you’re on alert. Like, it’s a little bit interesting, but also …
Goldberg:
Hanna, as you know, I’m always on alert.
Rosin:
Yeah, okay, okay, okay.
Goldberg:
Hanna, what am I gonna tell you?
Rosin:
All right, so then, so maybe it’s a spoof, maybe it’s not. How does it start to get more real?
Goldberg:
Well, it gets real in the sense that if somebody’s doing a spoof, it’s a very, very accurate spoof. What happens is, a number of Cabinet-level officials start reporting into this chain, giving the names of their deputies or contact people over the weekend, when, clearly, something’s gonna happen in Yemen. Uh, in retrospect, clearly something’s gonna happen in Yemen. And that was that for that day; it was the next day that they start engaging in a policy discussion really in earnest. And it’s, you know, explicated in the story that I wrote. But, um, that’s when I’m sort of

不同观点：
• [jcalx] 认为该评论让他想起了一个名为 "Late Night Commits" 的网站，暗示该网站可能包含一些幽默或有趣的编程提交内容。

data.title: Linux 6.15 Goes Heavy on Intel and AMD x86_64 CPU Changes
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: Linux 6.15引入了大量针对Intel和AMD x86/x86_64处理器的更新。主要变化包括对AMD Zen 3及更新处理器的INVLPGB功能支持，提升了TLB失效性能。同时，AMD SMN和Node驱动得到改进。Intel方面，重构了CPU家族处理以适应即将推出的非"Family 6"处理器，并更新了线性地址掩码（LAM）和FineIBT-BHI防御机制。此外，改进了对P和E核的安全缓解处理，并新增了"setcpuid="和"clearcpuid="启动参数以强制CPU功能或缓解措施。还改进了KASLR以支持PCI BAR空间，并提高了GCC和Clang的最低版本要求。对32位x86内核的支持也进行了调整，移除了对超过4GB内存的支持。整体上，这些变化旨在提升性能和安全性。
